## English Translation:

(Large ornamental initial at left)

**WILLIAM, BY THE GRACE OF GOD,** Prince of Orange, etc., Stadholder, together with the Councillors, in the name of the Noble Lords the States of the Principality of Guelders and the County of Zutphen, make known by virtue of these presents: Whereas it has pleased the said Noble Lords the States to resolve, at the Diet (Landdag) held at the town of Zutphen in April 1644, by the advice and pronouncement of His Highness, also the most Illustrious and High-born Prince and Lord **FREDERICK HENRY,** Prince of Orange, etc., of laudable memory, in life likewise Stadholder, the Lord Father of our Stadholder — [that pronouncement being] dated the 13/25 of the aforesaid month of April — that, for the greatest welfare and relief of the said Principality and County, in the present circumstances, certain sums of money shall be raised and negotiated at interest, to be applied and employed for the payment of the necessary debts and burdens of the Province, as more fully set forth in the aforesaid pronouncement, and in the said Resolution thereupon following, of the said Noble Lords the States:

So do we acknowledge, by virtue of these presents, that {Evert[?] van Beckhoven[?], of [Cletelborst?]} has, on the day this is subscribed below, in good current money, for the benefit of the said Noble Lords the States, counted out and delivered the sum of {six hundred and fifty guilders}, at twenty stivers the [guilder]. And accordingly, wishing to properly safeguard the said {Evert van Beckhoven[?]}, his heirs, or holders of his claim, we have, in the name of the said Noble Lords the States, by virtue of the aforesaid resolution of their Noble Mightinesses, and adhering to the aforementioned pronouncement, promised and do promise by these presents to pay interest on the said sum of {six hundred and fifty guilders} at six and a quarter per hundred, making yearly {forty guilders[?] ...}, to be paid from year to year, whereof the first year shall fall due on the {[16th?] of [month — illegible]} of the next following year {[illegible date]}, and so forth from year to year, until redemption.

Whereupon we assure the said {Evert van Beckhoven[?]}, as to both the capital and the interest, together with the costs which, in default of prompt payment on the said terms, or within fourteen days thereafter (undefined, subject to assessment by the Court), after due summons, might arise. Binding thereto all the common means, imposts, land-taxes (Verpondingen), and the revenue-offices of the said Principality and County, none excepted, and each and all, for the security and indemnification of the said {Evert van Beckhoven[?]}, his heirs or holders of his claim, so as to prosecute the same before the Court of the said Principality and County, in case of non-payment, by real execution, up to effective payment, without anything being done, or suffered to be done in any way, to the contrary. To which end all exceptions and benefits of law are hereby renounced. Provided that it shall be free to either side, the one as well as the other, both to make redemption and to demand the capital back again; on the understanding, however, that the request and notice of redemption be given respectively half a year beforehand. And that in such case, as also of the rent, the payment shall be made in good current and lawful money.

Willing that this our letter, an authentic vidimus or copy, together with an assignation upon any revenue-office of the said Principality and County by us, for the first time with a receipt (quittance), and thereafter with a receipt only, as often as need be, being delivered over, the payment shall be made to the said {Evert van Beckhoven[?]}; which payment the Land-Receiver-General of the said Principality and County, or whoever else shall be charged therewith, shall have allowed in his account (uytgave) without difficulty. All without fraud or guile. In witness whereof we have caused the great Seal of the said Principality and County to be appended to the present instrument, and the same to be signed by the Court's Clerk (Griffier). **Given at Arnhem, the** {[16th?] [month — illegible], 16{48}}.

(signature of the Court's clerk, illegible)

(archival docket: 1648)

title: Kingdom of Sweden Royal Loan Bond (Amsterdam)
description: A printed sovereign loan bond of King Gustavus III of Sweden, granted under the king's hand at Gripsholm Castle on 20 October 1784 and countersigned by J. Liljencrants. The Crown raises two million guilders, equal to 800,000 Rijksdaalders Holland current money, bearing interest at four and a half percent a year, payable every six months, redeemable after the first year on six months' notice, the whole capital to be reimbursed within fifteen years reckoned from the first of December. The loan is secured on the effects and revenues of the Crown, backed further by four Swedish State Treasury obligations of 200,000 Rijksdaalders each deposited as special mortgage by Hope en Compagnie and Fizeaux, Grand en Compagnie, and ranks after an earlier loan of 800,000 Rijksdaalders; it may itself be divided into obligations of smaller amounts. It was contracted at Amsterdam through those two houses. This Dutch sheet is a sworn translation of a French original, made at Amsterdam on 9 February 1785 by the sworn translator Johannes Vergeel.
creator: King Gustav III of Sweden
notes: Swedish royal loan bond, King Gustav III. 400,000 Rijksdaalders Hollandsch Courant. Amsterdam, February 9, 1782. Issued through Amsterdam money market. Johannes Verge, agent/translator. Gustav III borrowed extensively in Amsterdam to finance Swedish policy.
transcription:
# Royal Loan Bond of King Gustavus III of Sweden, Contracted at Amsterdam (Gripsholm, 20 October 1784; sworn Dutch translation, Amsterdam, 9 February 1785) — Transcription

## Original:

**Wy GUSTAVUS, door Gods Genade Koning van Zweeden, der Gothen en Wenden &c. &c. &c., Erf Heer van Noorwegen, Hertog van Schleeswyk, Holstein, Stormarn en Ditmarsen, Grave van Oldenburg, Delmenhorst &c. &c.**

Doen te weeten: Dat wy, goedgevonden hebbende ten welzyn van onze Staaten een Leening te doen van Twee Millioenen Guldens, of acht maal honderd Duizend Ryxdaalders Hollandsch Courant Geld, geevende tot zeekerheid alle de Effecten en Revenuen van de Kroon, welke niet reeds zyn verhypotheequeerd en Speciaal de Inkomsten van onze Douanen en Tollen, aan de Heeren *Hope* en *Compagnie* en *Fizeaux*, *Grand* en *Compagnie*, te Amsterdam, last gegeeven hebben en dezelve uit krachte van deeze tegenwoordige, Volmacht geeven om voor ons en ons Koningryk dezelve Leening te negotieeren.

En vermits wy van bovengemelde Heeren tot ons volkomen genoegen en ten behoeve van ons Koningryk, ontvangen hebben eene Somma van Acht maal Honderd Duizend Ryxdaalders Hollandsch Courant geld, om aan ons te worden geleend, tegens Een Interest van vier en een half ten Honderd Jaarlyks, en voor den tyd gestipuleerd in de Vier Obligatien van ons Staats Comptoir, ieder groot Tweemaal Honderd Duizend Ryxdaalders Hollandsch Courant geld, gedeposeerd by de voorzeide Heeren als Speciaale Hypotheecq van deeze Leening, welke Somma van Achtmaal Honderd Duizend Ryxdaalders Hollandsch Courant geld, aan ons en ons Koningryk deugdlyk is gefourneerd geworden.

Zo verbinden wy ons, voor ons, onze Erfgenaamen en Opvolgers in het Koningryk Zweeden, om niet alleen aan opgemelde Heeren te Amsterdam, alle zes Maanden te doen betaalen de Interessen van bovengemelde Somma van Achtmaal Honderd Duizend Ryxdaalders Hollandsch Courant geld, tegens vier en een half ten Honderd Jaarlyks, maar ook het geheele Capitaal op de vervaltyd dewelke binnen Vyftien Jaaren zyn zal, te rekenen van den Eersten December aanstaande, te doen rembourseeren, ten zy met gezaamentlyke overeenstemming mogte worden goedgevonden, den Termyn van het zelve Remboursement te prolongeeren, in welk laatst geval zulks zes Maanden te vooren zal worden gedeclareerd; ons echter de Faculteit voorbehoudende om deze Leening naa verloop van de Eerste Elf Jaaren geheel of gedeeltelyk te doen rembourseeren.

Teffens permitteren wy mits dezen aan opgemelde Heeren, om de voorgemelde Hoofdsomma in Obligatien van mindere Sommen te verdeelen, en dezelve onder hunne Handtekening aan wien zy zullen goedvinden te vernegotieren, mits dezelve Obligatien door een beëedigd Openbaar Notaris werden gecontrasigneerd, zullende dezelve in zodanig geval van dezelfde kracht en waarde zyn als deeze tegenwoordige Hoofd Obligatie, zodanig, dat aan de Eigenaars of Houders van dezelve Obligatien van zes tot zes Maanden ten Comptoire van bovengemelde Heeren zal worden betaald de Interest tegens vier en een half ten Honderd Jaarlyks, en by expiratie van de vervaltyd der Leening, het Capitaal zelve, ten waare dat men wegens een Ulterieure Prolongatie mogte zyn overeengekomen, alles zonder eenige korting.

Tot zekerheid van het Remboursement dezer Geldleening, zo wel ten opzichte van het Capitaal als de Interessen, verbinden en verhypothequeeren wy alle de Effecten en Revenuen van ons Koningryk, welke niet reeds zyn verhypothequeerd, van wat naam en Hoedanigheid dezelve ook mogen zyn en Speciaal de Inkomsten van onze Douanen en Tollen, en daar en boven de voorschreven vier Obligatien van ons Staats Comptoir, ieder groot Tweemaal Honderd Duizend Ryxdaaldaars, Hollandsch Courant geld, Authoriseerende de meergedachte Heeren, hunne Erfgenaamen en Opvolgers, ingeval van non betaaling van het Capitaal of de Interessen op Plaats en Termyn voorschreeven, als dan direct de gemelde Obligatien van ons Staats Comptoir te verkoopen en vernegotieeren tot de Concurrentie van het gunt hen verschuldigd zyn zal.

Na dat het Capitaal en de Interessen dezer Leening, van Achtmaal Honderd Duizend Ryxdaalders Hollandsch Courant geld, volgens den Inhoud van deeze tegenwoordige Hoofd-Obligatie door ons geheel zullen zyn Gerembourseerd, zo zal deeze zelve Obligatie mitsgaders de Obligatien van ons Staats Comptoir voor deze Leening Special verhypothequeerd, aan ons en onze Kroon, vry en ontslagen van alle verbintenis hoe genaamd, moeten worden te rug gegeeven en overgeleverd.

Approberende wy voor het overige al het geene meergedachte Heeren zullen nodig vinden by deze Leenings Negotiatie, ten beste en voordeele van ons Koningryk, overeenkomstig onze hier voren uitgedrukte Intentien, te reguleeren.

Ten Oirkonde waarvan, wy deeze tegenwoordige Authorisatie en Obligatie eigenhandig hebben geteekend, en ons Koninglyk Zegel daar by doen Apposeeren.

Gedaan op het Kasteel Gripsholm, deezen Twintigsten October des Jaars Een Duizend Zeven Honderd Vier en Tachtig.

(Was getekend)
GUSTAF. (L. S.)

(Lager was getekend)
J. LILJENCRANTS.

Accordeerd met het Fransch Origineel getekend N°. 4155. ne varietur.

Amsterdam den 9 February 1785.

JOHANNES VERGEEL Luc. Zn.
*Beëedigd Translateur.*

---

## English Translation:

**We GUSTAVUS, by the Grace of God King of Sweden, of the Goths and Wends &c. &c. &c., Hereditary Lord of Norway, Duke of Schleswig, Holstein, Stormarn and Dithmarschen, Count of Oldenburg, Delmenhorst &c. &c.**

Be it known: That we, having deemed it good for the welfare of our States to contract a Loan of Two Million Guilders, or eight times one hundred thousand Rijksdaalders in Dutch Current Money, giving as security all the Effects and Revenues of the Crown, which are not already mortgaged, and especially the Incomes of our Customs and Tolls, have given full charge and power to the Messrs. Hope and Company and Fizeaux, Grand and Company, at Amsterdam, and by virtue of these presents do grant them full authority to negotiate the said Loan for us and our Kingdom.

And whereas we have received from the aforesaid Messrs., to our full satisfaction and for the benefit of our Kingdom, a Sum of Eight times One Hundred Thousand Rijksdaalders Dutch Current Money, to be lent to us, at an Interest of four and one half per Hundred yearly, and for the term stipulated in the Four Obligations of our State Treasury (Staats Comptoir), each amounting to Twice One Hundred Thousand Rijksdaalders Dutch Current Money, deposited with the aforesaid Messrs. as Special Security (Hypothec) of this Loan — which Sum of Eight times One Hundred Thousand Rijksdaalders Dutch Current Money has been duly furnished to us and our Kingdom.

Thus we bind ourselves, for ourselves, our Heirs and Successors in the Kingdom of Sweden, not only to cause to be paid to the aforesaid Messrs. at Amsterdam, every six Months, the Interest on the abovementioned Sum of Eight times One Hundred Thousand Rijksdaalders Dutch Current Money, at four and one half per Hundred yearly, but also the whole Capital at the maturity which shall fall within Fifteen Years, reckoned from the coming First of December, to be reimbursed — unless by mutual agreement it should be found good to prolong the term of the said Reimbursement, in which latter case such shall be declared six Months beforehand; reserving to ourselves, however, the Faculty to reimburse this Loan wholly or in part after the lapse of the first Eleven Years.

At the same time we hereby permit the aforesaid Messrs. to divide the abovementioned Principal Sum into Obligations of smaller amounts, and to negotiate the same, under their Signature, to whomsoever they shall think fit, provided that the said Obligations be countersigned by a sworn Public Notary; in which case the same shall be of the same force and value as this present Principal Obligation, so that to the Owners or Holders of the said Obligations there shall be paid, from six to six Months at the Office of the abovementioned Messrs., the Interest at four and one half per Hundred yearly, and at the expiration of the maturity of the Loan, the Capital itself — unless an Ulterior Prolongation should have been agreed upon — all without any deduction.

For the security of the Reimbursement of this Money-loan, both as regards the Capital and the Interest, we bind and mortgage all the Effects and Revenues of our Kingdom, which are not already mortgaged, of whatever name and quality they may be, and especially the Incomes of our Customs and Tolls, and furthermore the aforesaid four Obligations of our State Treasury, each amounting to Twice One Hundred Thousand Rijksdaalders Dutch Current Money, authorizing the aforesaid Messrs., their Heirs and Successors, in case of non-payment of the Capital or the Interest at the place and term aforesaid, then directly to sell and negotiate the said Obligations of our State Treasury up to the amount of what shall be owed to them.

After the Capital and the Interest of this Loan, of Eight times One Hundred Thousand Rijksdaalders Dutch Current Money, according to the tenor of this present Principal Obligation, shall have been wholly Reimbursed by us, then this same Obligation, together with the Obligations of our State Treasury specially mortgaged for this Loan, shall have to be returned and delivered up to us and our Crown, free and discharged of every obligation whatsoever.

Approving for the rest all that the aforesaid Messrs. shall find necessary to arrange in this Loan Negotiation, for the best advantage of our Kingdom, in conformity with our intention expressed above.

In witness whereof, we have signed this present Authorization and Obligation with our own hand, and caused our Royal Seal to be affixed thereto.

Done at Gripsholm Castle, this Twentieth of October in the Year One Thousand Seven Hundred Eighty-four.

(Was signed)
GUSTAF. (L. S.)

(Below was signed)
J. LILJENCRANTS.

Agreeing with the French Original signed No. 4155, ne varietur.

Amsterdam, the 9th of February 1785.

JOHANNES VERGEEL, son of Lucas.
*Sworn Translator.*

title: Bourbon Princes in Exile Loan Certificate, Amsterdam
description: A bond certificate raising a loan in the name of the exiled French Bourbon princes, drawn at Amsterdam on 28 September 1793. Its authorization, given at Hamm in Westphalia on 25 September 1793 and dated to the first year of the King's reign, bears the names of Louis Stanislas Xavier, the future Louis XVIII, and Charles Philippe, Comte d'Artois, countersigned by the Maréchal Duc de Broglie as Minister of State, with a separate signature at the foot, "Par ordre de leurs Altesses Royales," by the Garde du Trésor Royal. The Amsterdam house of J. Bourcourd and the widow E. Croese & Comp. acknowledges, on behalf of the Princes of France, receipt of one thousand guilders Dutch current for a share in the obligation, with coupons attached. Louis XVI had been executed in January of that year.

title: Conditions of the Daniel Changuion Plantation Loan, Essequibo and Demerara
description: Printed conditions of a loan fund raised under the direction of Daniel Changuion for planters in the Rio Essequebo and Rio Demmerary, dated 1816. The heading sets the terms: a total sum of 400,000 Dutch guilders, advanced for ten years at 6 percent interest yearly, to continue and improve their plantations. The articles that follow establish the security. Borrowers must have their estates valued by sworn appraisers, covering the grounds, buildings, works and the enslaved people but excluding furniture and movables, and the resulting inventory and mortgage deed registered with the colony's secretary. Against this, a planter is advanced at most five-eighths of the appraised value.
creator: Daniel Changuion

title: Gemeente Warnsveld Municipal Loan Certificate
description: A certificate of share representing a 250-guilder participation in a 12,000-guilder loan charged to the municipality of Warnsveld in the Dutch province of Gelderland, given at Warnsveld on 30 April 1883 over the signatures of the mayor and aldermen. It bears interest of four and a half percent yearly, payable against surrender of attached coupons. The loan rested on resolutions of the municipal council of 16 September and 21 October 1882, approved by the Provincial States of Gelderland on 25 October 1882 for a maximum of 14,000 guilders. Redemption proceeds by annual lottery: one share drawn each of the first twelve years, two in the following ten, three thereafter, paid the next 30 April at the municipal receiver's office, after which interest ceases. A BETAALD cancellation marks its eventual redemption.
creator: Gemeente Warnsveld
notes: Municipal loan; f.12,000 total; f.250 denomination; 4.5% interest; lottery redemption; Warnsveld, Gelderland

BEWIJS van AANDEEL

IN DE

GELDLEENING

groot f 12,000,

ten laste der Gemeente WARNSVELD,

vastgesteld bij besluiten van den Gemeenteraad van den 16 September 1882 en van den 21 October d.a.a., goedgekeurd door Heeren Afgeputeerde Staten van Gelderland bij besluit van den 25 October 1882, nr. 29 [or 39] voor het bedrag van hoogstens f 14,000.

BURGEMEESTER en WETHOUDERS der gemeente WARNSVELD verklaren hierbij aan toonder schuldig te zijn de somma van **Twee honderd vijftig Gulden, f 250,—** als aandeel in de bovengenoemde geldleening en zulks tegen eene rente van vier en een half ten honderd in het jaar, te voldoen op en tegen inlevering van bijgevoegde coupons.

De eerste twaalf jaren zal telken jare een aandeel worden uitgoloot, de daarop volgende tien jaren twee aandeelen en de overige jaren drie aandeelen, bij loting te voren aan te wijzen.

De uitgelote aandeelen zullen op den dertigsten April na de uitloting ten kantore van den gemeente-ontvanger worden uitbetaald, tegen intrekking van dit bewijs en de onverschenen interest-coupons.

Zullende de rente der uitgelote aandeelen niet langer loopen dan tot den Dertigsten April van het jaar waarin de uitloting heeft plaats gehad.

Gegeven te WARNSVELD den 30 April 1883.

Burgemeester en Wethouders voornoemd,

[Signatures]

Burgemeester.
Wethouder.

CERTIFICATE OF SHARE

IN THE

MUNICIPAL LOAN

amounting to f 12,000,

charged to the Municipality of WARNSVELD,

established by resolutions of the Municipal Council of September 16, 1882 and October 21 of the same year, approved by the Appointed Representatives of the States of Gelderland by resolution of October 25, 1882, no. 29 [or 39] for the amount of at most f 14,000.

BURGEMEESTER [Mayor] and WETHOUDERS [Aldermen] of the municipality of WARNSVELD hereby declare themselves indebted to the bearer in the amount of **Two hundred fifty Guilders, f 250,—** as a share in the aforementioned municipal loan and at an interest rate of four and one half percent per year, payable upon and against submission of the attached coupons.

During the first twelve years, one share shall be drawn by lot each year; during the following ten years, two shares; and during the remaining years, three shares, to be determined beforehand by lottery.

The drawn shares shall be paid at the office of the municipal receiver on the 30th of April following the drawing, against surrender of this certificate and the unsubmitted interest coupons.

The interest on the drawn shares shall cease to accrue as of the 30th of April of the year in which the drawing takes place.

Given at WARNSVELD on April 30, 1883.

Burgemeester and Wethouders aforementioned,

title: Stolkert Surinam Plantation Mortgage to Du Plessis & Taunay, Amsterdam
description: A notarial copy opening a deed of mortgage passed before Cornelis van Homrigh, public notary at Amsterdam, on 29 December 1777. It records a transaction first executed on 22 July 1777 before the council of civil justice of the colony of Surinam: Fredrik Cornelis Stolkert, owner of one-third of the named plantations, acting also for the owners of the remaining two-thirds, Isaac Stolkert, Hendrik Boudewyn Stolkert and Dorothea Elizabeth Werner, acknowledges a debt of 320,000 guilders Holland current money to the Amsterdam merchants Reynier Isaac du Plessis and Jan Fredrik Taunay. Of this, 108,000 guilders was newly advanced and 212,000 guilders redeemed an earlier mortgage. The principal is repayable over fifteen years from 10 April 1777 at five per hundred yearly interest, the creditors to serve as sole correspondents and consignees for the plantations' produce sold at Amsterdam. The deed binds the estates as security and obliges the debtor to maintain a sufficient number of enslaved labourers, replacing the dead, maimed, aged and runaways. The page breaks off before the plantations are named.

HARTSINCK, S. DU PLESSIS, J. W. PICHOT en A. WALLYEN gepasseerd, (zo als ook de zelve Somma van Twee honderd en twaalf duizend Guldens, door hen Heeren Comparanten uitgeschoten, en dienvolgende ook het evengezegde Hypotheecq geroyeerd is,) Hebbende dezelve Heer FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT privé en qualitatequa derhalven afstand gedaan van de exceptie van onaangetelden Gelde of niet genoegzame waarde genoten te hebben, En wyders beloofd de in voegen voorschreven opgenomen en verschuldigde Capitale Somma van Driemaal honderd en twintig duizend Guldens Hollands Courant Geld, aan hen Heeren Comparanten of derzelver regt verkrygende kost- en schadeloos binnen deze Stad te zullen restitueren en voldoen over vyftien Jaren, gerekend zederd den 10den April 1777. en inmiddels ook binnen deze Stad de Interessen te betalen op het verschynen van ieder Jaar, ook gerekend zederd den zelven 10den April 1777. tegens vyf ten honderd in het Jaar, vrygeld, zonder eenige korting hoe genaamd, en zulks tot de volle en effectueele voldoening van het Capitaal toe, Des dat aan hem Heer FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT, privé en qq., zal vrystaan, om de voorschreven Capitale Somma eerder, dan de gezegde vyftien Jaren af te leggen in termynen, het zy met het eindigen van het zesde Jaar, en zo vervolgens Jaarlyks met tien Percent, ofte met het eindigen van het elfde Jaar, en zo vervolgens ook Jaarlyks met twintig Percent, en dat in beiden gevallen wel meerder, maar niet minder, en mits van zodanige vroegere aflossing zes Maanden te voren te waarschouwen; Met verdere beloften, dat zy Heeren Comparanten of derzelver Opvolgers in hun Comptoir van Negotie, geduurende de voormelde tyd en tot de dadelyke aflossing van het voorschrevene geheele Capitaal toe, zullen zyn de eenige Correspondenten van de na te meldene Plantagien, en dat mitsdien aan hen of derzelver gedagte Opvolgers van tyd tot tyd alle de Producten en Gewasschen van dezelve Plantagien zullen werden verzonden en geconsigneerd, ten einde alhier te Amsteldam door de Heeren Comparanten of derzelver Opvolgers in hun Comptoir van Negotie te werden verkogt, zonder iets het allerminste aldaar in de Colonie te mogen verkopen of aan iemand anders, of na eenige andere plaatzen te mogen afzenden of verdebiteren, direct nog indirect; Dat ook van het afzenden der gemelde Producten en Gewasschen van tyd tot tyd behoorlyke en tydige advisen aan hen Heeren Comparanten of derzelver gedagte Opvolgers zullen werden gegeven, tot het doen der Assurantien waar toe zy Heeren Comparanten by dezelve Acte van Hypotheecq speciaal zyn gequalificeerd, en des noods op Schip of Schepen, gelyk mede alle Provisien en noodwendigheden van tyd tot tyd ten behoeven van de na te meldene Plantagien, en het onderhoud der zelven vereischt werdende, van hen Heeren Comparanten of derzelver gedagte Opvolgers, en van niemand anders zullen werden ontboden, en dat alles op den voet der gewone Provisien volgens Costume, na aftrek van welke Provisien uit het zuivere overschietende Saldo, voor zo verre het zelve zal kunnen toereiken, door de Heeren Comparanten of derzelver Opvolgers zullen werden voldaan de voorschreven Jaarlyksche Interessen, zo mede in cas van aflossing by Termynen als voren, dezelve Termynen, zullende over het meerdere beloop van het zelve Saldo door hem Heer FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT privé en qualitatequa mogen werden gedisponeerd, dog in cas van te kort komende, het zelve door hem privé en qq. aanstonds in geld moeten worden gesuppleerd. Dat hy Heer FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT privé en qq. zal gehouden zyn, de rekening, welke Jaarlyks aan hem door de Heeren Comparanten of derzelver Opvolgers zal moeten werden overgezonden of ter hand gesteld binnen twee of uitterlyk drie Maanden na den ontfangst of overgifte van dezelve schriftelyk te approberen, of de erreuren daar in aan te wyzen, en die tyd verstreken zynde zonder dat dezelve rekening zal zyn gecontradiceerd, hy Heer FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT privé en qq. heeft verklaard, die alsdan te houden voor accoord, en door hem geapprobeerd, Hebbende voorts hy Heer FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT privé en qq. zig verpligt, om de na te meldene Plantagien geduurende de voorschreven tyd behoorlyk te administreeren of doen administreeren, mitsgaders altoos een toereikend getal Slaven op de zelve te houden, en voor de Stervende, verminkte of door Ouderdom of anderzints tot den dienst onbekwaam gewordene, als mede voor de weglopers van tyd tot tyd wederom nieuwe aan te koopen, en voorts in alles dezelve Plantagien in goeden staat te onderhouden, en ook van dezelve administratie en zulks van den staat der gedagte Plantagien, en al het geen daar omtrent komt voor te vallen, van tyd tot tyd een behoorlyk blyk over te zenden aan hen Heeren Comparanten of derzelver Opvolgers, die ook ten einde hun Edelens zullen kunnen verzekerd zyn, dat alles ter goeder trouwe geschied, dezelve Plantagien, des noods op nieuw zullen mogen doen Inventariseren en tauxeren, en zulks alles ten kosten van hem Heer FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT privé en qq.

Ter voldoeninge en naarkoming van al het welke hy Heer FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT privé en qq. heeft verbonden, niet alleen in het generaal de Personen en Goederen van die genen zoo hy repræsenteerde, en dat ieder in solidum en voor het geheel, ten bedwang van alle Regten ende Regteren, maar ook als een Legaal en Speciaal Hypotheecq derzelver, in gemelde Colonie gelegene Plantagien, te weten:

On the twenty-ninth of December in the year seventeen hundred seventy-seven, there appeared before me, CORNELIS VAN HOMRIGH, public Notary at Amsterdam, admitted by the Court of Holland, the Gentlemen REYNIER ISAAC DU PLESSIS and JAN FREDRIK TAUNAY, Merchants residing within this City.

Making known: That by Deed of Mortgage on the 22nd of July of this Year 1777, in the presence of the Honourable Worshipful Gentlemen CHRISTOFFEL NAGEL and HENDRIK ROTARIUS, Councillors in the Court of Civil Justice of the Colony of Surinam, &c. &c., by the Gentleman FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT, both for himself, as owner of a one-third part of the plantations hereinafter to be named, and also, pursuant to two separate Powers of Attorney mentioned in the said Deed of Mortgage, as authorized agent both of the Gentleman ISAAC STOLKERT, as well as of the Gentleman HENDRIK BOUDEWYN STOLKERT, and Madam DOROTHEA ELIZABETH WERNER, married couple, as owners of the remaining two-third parts of the same plantations, passed and on the same day confirmed by decree (condemnation) of the aforesaid Court, the said Gentleman FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT, thus in his private capacity and further in his aforesaid capacity, and therefore also in the names of the aforementioned Principals, has acknowledged, respectively together and each severally and for the whole, without any division, under proper renunciation, to be well and truly indebted to and for the benefit of the Gentlemen Appearers, in a Sum of Three times one hundred and twenty thousand Guilders Holland Current Money [320,000], arising, firstly, out of and by reason of a Sum of One hundred and eight thousand Guilders [108,000], Holland Current Money, advanced and furnished by the Gentlemen Appearers for the benefit of the Gentleman FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT in his private and representative capacity; and further of a Sum of Two hundred and twelve thousand Guilders [212,000], Holland Current Money, likewise to be advanced by the Gentlemen Appearers for the benefit of the Gentleman FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT in his private and representative capacity, in satisfaction of the Mortgage passed for the benefit of the Gentlemen P. HARTSINCK, S. DU PLESSIS, J. W. PICHOT and A. WALLYEN, (as also the same Sum of Two hundred and twelve thousand Guilders, advanced by the Gentlemen Appearers, and consequently the aforesaid Mortgage having also been cancelled,) the said Gentleman FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT in his private and representative capacity has therefore renounced the exception of money not counted out or of not having received sufficient value; And further has promised to restore and satisfy the Capital Sum thus taken up and owed as aforesaid, of Three times one hundred and twenty thousand Guilders Holland Current Money, to the Gentlemen Appearers or their assigns, without cost or loss, within this City, over fifteen Years, reckoned from the 10th of April 1777; and in the meantime also to pay the Interest within this City at the falling due of each Year, likewise reckoned from the same 10th of April 1777, at five per hundred per Year, free of charge, without any deduction of whatever kind, and this until the full and effective satisfaction of the Capital. So that the Gentleman FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT, in his private and representative capacity, shall be at liberty to pay off the aforesaid Capital Sum sooner than the said fifteen Years, in instalments, whether at the ending of the sixth Year, and so on thereafter yearly at ten per cent, or at the ending of the eleventh Year, and so on thereafter yearly at twenty per cent, and this in both cases indeed more, but not less, and provided that six Months' notice of such earlier repayment be given beforehand; With further promises, that the Gentlemen Appearers or their successors in their Counting-house of Trade, during the aforesaid term and until the actual repayment of the whole aforesaid Capital, shall be the sole Correspondents of the plantations hereinafter to be named, and that accordingly to them or their said successors from time to time all the Produce and Crops of the same plantations shall be sent and consigned, in order to be sold here at Amsterdam by the Gentlemen Appearers or their successors in their Counting-house of Trade, without selling the very least of it there in the Colony or to anyone else, or sending or vending it to any other places, directly nor indirectly; That also of the sending of the said Produce and Crops proper and timely advices shall from time to time be given to the Gentlemen Appearers or their said successors, for the effecting of the Insurances for which the Gentlemen Appearers are specially qualified by the same Deed of Mortgage, and if need be upon Ship or Ships; likewise that all Supplies and necessaries required from time to time for the benefit of the plantations hereinafter to be named, and for the maintenance thereof, shall be ordered from the Gentlemen Appearers or their said successors, and from no one else, and all this upon the footing of the usual Commission according to Custom; after deduction of which Commissions, from the net remaining Balance, so far as the same may suffice, the Gentlemen Appearers or their successors shall pay the aforesaid Yearly Interest, as also in case of repayment by Instalments as above, the said Instalments; and the surplus of the said Balance may be disposed of by the Gentleman FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT in his private and representative capacity, but in case of a shortfall, the same must at once be supplemented by him in cash, privately and in his representative capacity. That the Gentleman FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT, privately and in his representative capacity, shall be bound to approve in writing the account which must yearly be sent or handed to him by the Gentlemen Appearers or their successors, within two or at most three Months after its receipt or delivery, or to point out the errors therein; and that time having elapsed without the said account being contradicted, the Gentleman FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT, privately and in his representative capacity, has declared then to hold it as agreed and approved by him. Furthermore the Gentleman FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT, privately and in his representative capacity, has bound himself properly to administer or cause to be administered the plantations hereinafter to be named during the aforesaid term, and always to keep a sufficient number of Slaves upon them, and for the Dying, the maimed, or those become unfit for service through Old age or otherwise, as well as for the runaways, from time to time to purchase new ones again, and further in every respect to maintain the same plantations in good condition; and also, of the said administration and thus of the state of the said plantations, and of everything that comes to pass concerning them, from time to time to send a proper account to the Gentlemen Appearers or their successors, who, in order that their Honours may also be assured that everything is done in good faith, may, if need be, have the same plantations newly Inventoried and appraised, and all this at the cost of the Gentleman FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT, privately and in his representative capacity.

For the satisfaction and fulfilment of all which the Gentleman FREDRIK CORNELIS STOLKERT, privately and in his representative capacity, has bound, not only in general the Persons and Goods of those whom he represented, and that each in solidum and for the whole, subject to the constraint of all Laws and Judges, but also as a Legal and Special Mortgage thereof, the plantations situated in the said Colony, namely:

title: Heshuysen & Compagnie / James Balmer Mortgage on Plantation Vauxhall, Dominica (Notarial Copy, Amsterdam)
description: A notarial copy executed before Hermanus de Wolff Junior, notary public admitted by the Hof van Holland and resident at Amsterdam, recording a mortgage transaction on the twenty-first of March 1777. Frans Jacob Heshuysen, acting for the Haarlem merchant house Adolf Jan Heshuysen en Compagnie, exhibits a mortgage granted on 13 August 1776 by James Balmer, merchant in London, in favour of Adolf Jan, Floris Visscher and Frans Jacob Heshuysen for 7,100 pounds sterling, secured on Plantation Vauxhall in Dominica. The same plantation already carried, under that mortgage, a life annuity on diverse lives in Great Britain of 1,269 pounds 10 shillings sterling yearly. Balmer had purchased the estate for 9,000 pounds above that annuity charge, then granted a fresh special mortgage of 7,100 pounds.

title: Austrian Construction Lottery Loan (Bau-Los), Vienna
description: A premium debenture of the Austrian Construction Lottery Loan, the Österreichisches Bau-Los Em. 1921, issued at Vienna on 1 September 1921 by the Bundes-Wohn- und Siedlungsfonds under the law of 15 July 1921. Federally guaranteed and mortgage-secured, payable to bearer, it carries a face value of one thousand two hundred kronen. The loan totalled 600,000,000 kronen, split into 450,000 whole tickets of 1,200 kronen and 200,000 quarter-tickets of 300 kronen. It carries no fixed coupon; capital is returned over forty years through periodic draws, winning tickets taking prize premiums free of tax. The loan funded dwelling construction. pages.description: This is a bearer bond (Облигация / Bond / Obligation) of the 5% Loan of the City of Baku of 1910, its text set in parallel Russian, English, and French. The note carries a face value of 189 roubles, fixed against 20 pounds sterling and 504 French francs, and bears interest at 5 percent per annum, payable semi-annually. It forms one share of a municipal loan of 26,999,973 roubles (£2,867,340; 71,999,928 francs), authorised by imperial sanction of 8/15 October 1909 and signed by the city's mayor (Городской Голова) and members of the municipal council. Issued at Baku, then the oil-rich capital of the Baku Governorate in the Russian Empire and now Azerbaijan, the bond shows a booming Caspian port reaching past its own borders to London and Paris money markets to fund municipal works. The trilingual frame and the prominent sterling and franc equivalences make the instrument's purpose plain: to court Western European capital. The municipal arms and restrained typographic ornament keep the design sober and administrative rather than allegorical.

This is the back of a bearer bond from the 5% Loan of the City of Baku, 1910 — issued by the Baku Municipal Duma and printed in Russian, English and French (Emprunt 5% de la Ville de Bakou). Each bond is denominated as Roubles 189 = Pounds sterling 20 = Francs 504, the triple reckoning that let the issue circulate on the London and Paris markets through Lloyds Bank and the London & South-Western Bank. The conditions, approved by the Assistant Minister of Finance on 7 May 1910, set the total nominal capital at 26,999,973 roubles (2,857,140 pounds; 71,999,928 francs), to fund a waterworks, the buyout of the horse-tramway company, electric street lighting, schools and market rows, and the discharge of municipal debts. The amortization table schedules redemption from 1911 to 1959, while the engraved coupon talons at right reflect the sober, ledger-like aesthetic of state-printer securities.

title: Bolivian Interior Loan Bond
description: A vale, or interest-bearing debt certificate, for one hundred pesos, issued by the República Boliviana under its Empréstito Interior of one million pesos, authorized by the Constituent Congress law of 16 November 1826 and drawn at Chuquisaca on 24 July 1827. It promises an annual rent of six pesos, six percent, payable in thirds each January, May and September. The certificate is declared negotiable and receivable at the Republic's treasuries at face value toward the purchase of public properties and the redemption of censos, perpetual rent-charges on land, per the decrees of 12 June 1827. A line reading "Pena de muerte al falsificador y cómplices" threatens death for forgers. A departmental endorsement of 7 February 1828, the seventeenth year of Independence, assigns it to the order of Colonel Ramón Molina, recorded at folio 22.

title: Bosnia-Herzegovina Railway Land Loan Bond, Sarajevo and Vienna
description: A bearer obligation for 1,000 kronen from the 4.5 percent Bosnia-Herzegovina railway land loan of 1902, Series C, dated Sarajevo and Vienna, 1 July 1902. Its heading and denomination are set in five languages: Croatian, Serbian in Cyrillic, German, Hungarian and French. The text grounds the issue in the law of 8 June 1902 and Hungarian Law Article XIII of 1902. It was issued for the common Imperial and Royal Ministry charged with the affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina and signed by the common Minister of Finance, the territory then administered jointly by Austria and Hungary after its occupation in 1878. Proceeds, capped at 75 million kronen, funded the provincial railways.
creator: Austro-Hungarian Government or Crown Land Authority

title: Imperial Brazil Loan Conversion Circular
description: A printed circular, a subscription prospectus for a sovereign debt conversion: the offer of £20,000,000 in new Imperial Brazilian 4 percent bonds, the proceeds to be applied exclusively to converting and redeeming the Empire's outstanding 5 percent loans of 1865, 1871, 1875 and 1886. It issues under the authority of the Emperor of Brazil, sanctioned by Laws No. 3,329 of 3 September 1884 and Nos. 3,396 and 3,397 of 24 November 1888, with N.M. Rothschild & Sons of London receiving subscriptions. The new 4 percent stock is offered at 90, holders of every £100 of old 5 percent stock receiving £100 nominal of new bonds plus a small cash difference, with interest running from the first half-yearly coupon due 1 April 1890.
creator: N.M. Rothschild & Sons (agents for Imperial Brazil)
notes: Imperial Brazil debt conversion circular; £20,000,000 new 4% bonds; converts 5% loans of 1865, 1871, 1875, 1886; N.M. Rothschild & Sons; Laws 3,329, 3,396 and 3,397 (1884/1888)
transcription:
# CONVERSION AND REDEMPTION
## OF THE

# IMPERIAL BRAZILIAN FIVE PER CENT. LOANS OF 1865, 1871, 1875 AND 1886.

Issue of £20,000,000 4 per. cent. Brazilian Bonds, the proceeds to be applied exclusively to the conversion and redemption of the above Loans.

His Majesty the Emperor of Brazil having in conformity with the Laws No. 3,329 of the 3rd September, 1884, and Nos. 3,396 and 3,397 of the 24th November, 1888, authorized the negotiation of the above Loan, Messrs. N. M. ROTHSCHILD & SONS, have to announce that they are ready to receive subscriptions at their office.

Subscriptions may be made either in Cash, or in Bonds of the above-mentioned Loans.

Applications for the new Bonds, *in exchange for Bonds of the above-mentioned Loans*, will be received on Wednesday, the 2nd inst., and on the five following days, viz., until Wednesday, the 9th October, at 4 p.m., when the List will be finally closed. No subscriptions will be received on Saturday.

The conversion will be effected as follows:—

Subscribers in Bonds will receive allotment in full.

The 4 per cent. Bonds are issued at the price of 90. In the conversion, every £100 5 per cent. Stock will be reckoned at par, exclusive of accrued interest, and in addition to this, a bonus of £1. 10s. will be given on every £100 converted. Thus every holder of £100 5 per cent. Stock will on converting, receive in exchange a £100 4 per cent. Bond and £11. 10s. in cash, but for cash differences on large amounts of Bonds, subscribers may elect to have new Bonds, the fractional surplus only being regulated by a cash payment; this option must be exercised when subscribing. Interest at 5 per cent. will be paid on the old Bonds from the date of the last dividend to the 1st October, 1889, from which date the 4 per cent. Bonds will bear interest, the first half-yearly Coupon being due the 1st April, 1890.

The repayment at par, but without the Bonus of £1. 10s. per cent., of all the Bonds of the above Loans not presented for conversion will be officially notified at the earliest possible date.

The 5 per cent. Bonds to be converted must be listed on forms which can be obtained on application, and must be furnished with the Coupons not yet due.

Application must be made on the form provided herewith, and accompanied by a deposit of £5 per cent. in money, or an approximate amount in convertible Bonds, *unless subscribers prefer to deposit the whole of their Bonds when making application*. The failure to deliver the Bonds converted when the Scrip is ready to be given in exchange, will render the deposit on application liable to forfeiture.

# Principality of Bulgaria — 6% State Mortgage Loan of 1892, Bond for Two Obligations (500 leva / 500 francs) — Transcription

## Original:

*(Bilingual bond, printed in green. Bulgarian text in the left column, French text in the right column. Corner counters read "2" at upper left and upper right; the crowned Bulgarian lion arms appear at lower left. Serial appears in the top centre.)*

**Nummer 073,741 – 073,742**

**Княжество България** — **Principauté de Bulgarie**

**6% Дьржавенъ ипотекаренъ заемъ отъ 1892 година,**
издаденъ съгласно закона, утвърденъ съ Княжески указъ № 204 отъ 27 Октоврий/8 Ноемврий 1892 год., обнародванъ въ Държавенъ Вѣстникъ брой 247 отъ 10/22 Ноемврий 1892 год.,

**ПРЕДСТАВЕНЪ ОТЪ 285.560 ОБЛИГАЦИИ**
за единъ имененъ капиталъ отъ
142,780.000 Лева = 5,711.200 Лири Стерлинги = 115,651.800 Марки = 57,112.000 Австрийски Флорини Златни
изплатими по именната имъ стойность въ 33 години. Заема е обезпеченъ съ първа ипотека:
а) на Държавнитѣ желѣзници Каспичанъ—София—Кюстендилъ и Русе—Варна,
б) на пристанищата въ Варна и Бургазъ.

*(Right column, same content in French:)*

**Emprunt hypothécaire d'État 6% de l'année 1892,**
[émi]s en vertu de la loi sanctionnée par Ukase en date du 27 Octobre (8 Novembre) 1892, No. 204, et publiée dans le Journal officiel No. 247 du 10/22 Novembre 1892,
**représenté par 285.560 Obligations**
portant sur un capital nominal total de
142,780.000 Francs = 5,711.200 Livres Sterl. = 115,651.800 R.-Mark = 57,112.000 Florins d'Autriche or
remboursables au pair en 33 ans. L'emprunt est garanti par inscription en première hypothèque:
sur les chemins de fer de l'État Kaspitchan—Sophia—Kustendil et Roustchouk—Varna,
sur les ports de Varna et Bourgas.

---

**ДВѢ ОБЛИГАЦИИ** — **DEUX OBLIGATIONS**

*(central denomination band)*

на носителя отъ по
**ПЕТЬ СТОТИНЪ ЛЕВА**
= Лири Стерлинги 20 = Марки 405 = Австрийски Флорини 200 Златни. Всѣка една.

au porteur de
**CINQ CENTS FRANCS**
= Livres Sterling 20 = Reichsmark 405 = Florins d'Autriche or 200, chacune.

---

**Body text — Bulgarian (left column):**

Настоящий заемъ е издаденъ въ 61,550 отрѣзка, А№ 000.001—061.550 по 1 облигация,
„ 30,005 „ 061.551—121.560 „ 2 облигации,
„ 24,000 „ 121.561—241.560 „ 5 „
„ 1,760 „ 241.561—285.560 „ 25 „

Облигациитѣ на този заемъ носятъ годишна лихва 6% на именния капиталъ, платима шестмесечно на 2/14 Януарий и на 1/13 Юлий всѣка година срѣщу предаването на купонитѣ.

Тоя заемъ ще се изплати въ 33 години, споредъ поместената въ облигацията таблица за погашение, чрѣзъ шестмесечни тѣгления, които ще стават въ София два мѣсеца прѣди падежа на купонитѣ — първа пѫть на 1/13 Май 1893 година, но при това Правителството си запази правото да изплати по [именната] имъ стойность въ всѣко врѣме, но не прѣди 2/14 Януарий 1898 год., всичкитѣ облигации останали въ обращение.

Изтеглените облигации ще бѫдатъ изплатени по именната имъ стойность на шестмесечния лихвенъ падежъ, при който ще стане тѣглението, срѣщу предаването имъ, придружени съ всичкитѣ неизтечени купони [...].

Изплащането на изтеглените купони и на изтеглените облигации ще става съ злато и по изборъ на носителя:
въ София у касата на съкровището,
въ Виена у Импер. Кралска привилегирована Банка на Австрийскитѣ земи,
въ Лондонъ, Парижъ, Берлинъ, Амстердамъ, Женева,
и други градове у учрежденията и банкеритѣ, които отпосле ще бѫдатъ показани отъ Българското Правителство.

Изплащането става въ София съ златни левове, въ Виена съ Австрийски флорини златни, въ Лондонъ съ лири стерлинги, въ Берлинъ и други Германски мѣста, гдѣто се плаща, съ марки, въ Парижъ и други градове съ златни франкове.

Купонитѣ и изтеглените облигации отъ настоящий заемъ сѫ и ще бѫдатъ свободни отъ всичкия видъ налози, такси или други данъкъ прѣдвидени или които не се прѣдвидятъ отъ Българскитѣ закони.

Изтеглените купони както и изтеглените облигации отъ настоящий заемъ ще се приематъ по именната имъ стойность въ всичкитѣ правителствени касси на Княжество България за изплащане на такси, мита, налози и други данъци, прѣдвидени или които не се прѣдвидятъ отъ бюджета на Княжеството.

Неизвадените купони губятъ стойностьта си слѣдъ петь години, а изтеглените облигации — слѣдъ тридесеть години отъ падежа имъ.

Плащането на купонитѣ и на изтеглените облигации е обезпечено съ първа ипотека:
а) на желѣзно-пѫтнитѣ линии Каспичанъ—София—Кюстендилъ и Русе—Варна,
б) на пристанищата въ Варна и Бургазъ и на всичкитѣ приходи на такси, които се събиратъ или ще се събиратъ въ тия пристанища.

За тая цѣль Българското правителство е установило на 18/30 Ноемврий 1892 год. подъ № 123, съгласно гражданскитѣ Български закони, първа ипотека върху казанитѣ желѣзнопѫтни линии съ всичкитѣ имъ станции, постройки, принадлежности и подвиженъ и неподвиженъ материалъ, както и върху дветѣ гореспоменати пристанища съ всичкитѣ имъ постройки, сгради и сѫорѫжения. Ипотеката е дадена на Императорската Кралска привилегирована Банка на Австрийскитѣ земи въ нейно име притежателка на облигациитѣ.

Ако Българското правителство не плати въ разстояние на шесть мѣсеци слѣдъ падежа изтеглените купони или изтеглените облигации, притежателя на облигациитѣ ще имать властьта и правото да вземать въ своя рѫка експлоатацията на ипотекиранитѣ желѣзници и пристанища за да се изплатятъ [...].

Ако Българското правителство не изплати въ разстояние на двѣ години происходящи [...] [линиитѣ] Каспичанъ—Шуменъ—Търново—Севлиево—Ловечъ—[...] пристанищата въ Варна и Бургасъ и неможе подъ [никаква форма да отклони тѣзи приходи отъ] специалното имъ назначение [...] да служи за основа. *(fine print; several clauses [illegible])*

**Body text — French (right column):**

Le présent emprunt est émis en 61.550 coupures No. 000.001—061.550 de 1 Obligation,
„ 30.005 „ 061.551—121.560 „ 2 Obligations,
„ 24.000 „ 121.561—241.560 „ 5 „
„ 1.760 „ 241.561—285.560 „ 25 „

Les obligations de cet emprunt portent intérêts à 6% l'an du capital nominal, [pay]ables semestriellement les 2/14 Janvier et 1/13 Juillet de chaque année contre remise coupons.

L'amortissement de cet emprunt se fera au pair en 33 ans suivant le tableau d'amortissement annexé aux obligations, par voie de tirages semestriels qui auront lieu à Sophia deux mois avant chaque échéance de coupons — la première fois le 1/13 Mai 1893; toutefois le Gouvernement se réserve la faculté de rembourser au pair à toute époque, mais pas avant le 1/13 Janvier 1898, toutes les obligations restant en circulation.

Les obligations sorties au tirage seront remboursées au pair à l'échéance semestrielle d'intérêts postérieure à leur tirage, contre remise des dites, munies de tous les coupons non encore échus après le terme de remboursement et du talon y afférent.

Le paiement des coupons et des obligations arrivées à remboursement a lieu en or, [au choix] du porteur:
à Sophia: à la Caisse du Trésor,
à Vienne: à la Banque Impériale Royale Privilégiée des Pays Autrichiens,
à Londres, Paris, Berlin, Amsterdam, Genève,
[et] autres villes auprès des établissements et banquiers qui seront ultérieurement désignés par le Gouvernement Bulgare.

Le paiement a lieu à Sophia en Levs or, à Vienne en Florins d'Autriche or, [à Londres en Livres Sterling, à Berlin et autres places d'Allemagne en Marks, à Paris et autres villes en Francs or]. *(remaining French clauses mirror the Bulgarian text; portions [illegible])*

[...] Varna et ne pourra sous aucun prétexte [être détourné de sa destination spéciale] (Art. II de la loi d'Emprunt.)

---

**Signatures / date (foot):**

София, 3/15 Декемврий 1892 година. — SOFIA, le 3/15 Décembre 1892.

Министръ на финанситѣ: — Le Ministre des Finances:
*(signed)* Iwan Salabascheff

Контролирано: Ковчежникътъ. — Pour contrôle: Le trésorier.

[Делегатъ] на българското правителство. — Le délégué du Gouvernement de Bulgarie.
*(signature [illegible])*

## English Translation:

**Nummer 073,741 – 073,742**

**Principality of Bulgaria**

**6% State Mortgage Loan of the year 1892,** issued in conformity with the law confirmed by Princely Ukase No. 204 of 27 October / 8 November 1892, promulgated in the State Gazette No. 247 of 10/22 November 1892,

**REPRESENTED BY 285,560 OBLIGATIONS** for a total nominal capital of 142,780,000 Leva = 5,711,200 Pounds Sterling = 115,651,800 Marks = 57,112,000 Austrian Gold Florins, redeemable at their nominal value over 33 years. The loan is secured by a first mortgage:
a) on the State railways Kaspichan—Sofia—Kyustendil and Ruse—Varna,
b) on the ports of Varna and Burgas.

**TWO OBLIGATIONS** at the bearer of **FIVE HUNDRED LEVA** each = 20 Pounds Sterling = 405 Marks = 200 Austrian Gold Florins each (French: **FIVE HUNDRED FRANCS** each).

**Body:** The present loan is issued in 61,550 certificates (Nos. 000,001—061,550) of 1 obligation, 30,005 (Nos. 061,551—121,560) of 2 obligations, 24,000 (Nos. 121,561—241,560) of 5, and 1,760 (Nos. 241,561—285,560) of 25.

The obligations of this loan bear interest at 6% per annum on the nominal capital, payable half-yearly on 2/14 January and 1/13 July each year against surrender of the coupons.

This loan shall be repaid over 33 years, according to the amortization table printed on the obligation, by half-yearly drawings held at Sofia two months before the coupon due date — the first on 1/13 May 1893; however the Government reserves the right to repay at nominal value at any time, but not before 2/14 January 1898, all obligations remaining in circulation.

Obligations drawn shall be repaid at their nominal value on the half-yearly interest due date at which the drawing takes place, against their surrender, accompanied by all coupons not yet due [...].

Payment of the drawn coupons and obligations shall be made in gold, at the bearer's choice: at Sofia, at the Treasury cashier's office; at Vienna, at the Imperial Royal Privileged Bank of the Austrian Lands; at London, Paris, Berlin, Amsterdam, Geneva; and in other towns at establishments and bankers to be designated later by the Bulgarian Government. Payment is made at Sofia in gold leva, at Vienna in Austrian gold florins, at London in pounds sterling, at Berlin and other German places in marks, at Paris and other towns in gold francs.

The coupons and drawn obligations of this loan are and shall be free from every kind of tax, duty or other levy foreseen or not foreseen by the Bulgarian laws. The matured coupons and drawn obligations shall be accepted at their nominal value at all government treasuries of the Principality of Bulgaria for payment of fees, customs, taxes and other duties. Uncollected coupons lose their value after five years, and drawn obligations after thirty years from their due date.

Payment of the coupons and of the drawn obligations is secured by a first mortgage: a) on the railway lines Kaspichan—Sofia—Kyustendil and Ruse—Varna; b) on the ports of Varna and Burgas and on all the revenues and fees collected or to be collected in those ports. To this end the Bulgarian Government established, on 18/30 November 1892 under No. 123, in conformity with the Bulgarian civil laws, a first mortgage upon the said railway lines with all their stations, buildings, appurtenances and movable and immovable material, as well as upon the two aforesaid ports with all their buildings, structures and installations. The mortgage is granted to the Imperial Royal Privileged Bank of the Austrian Lands, in its name as holder of the obligations.

Should the Bulgarian Government fail to pay within six months after the due date the matured coupons or drawn obligations, the holder of the obligations shall have the power and right to take over the operation of the mortgaged railways and ports in order to obtain payment [...]. *(Further clauses concerning the lines Kaspichan—Shumen—Tirnovo—Sevlievo—Lovech—[...] and the ports of Varna and Burgas, which may under no pretext be diverted from their special purpose — Art. II of the Loan Law; portions illegible.)*

**Foot:** Sofia, 3/15 December 1892. The Minister of Finance: *(signed)* Ivan Salabashev. For control: The Treasurer *(signature illegible)*. The Delegate of the Bulgarian Government *(signature illegible)*.

title: Republic of Colombia Funding Certificate
description: A bearer scrip certificate for £2 16s. 8d., representing a holder's share in the Republic of Colombia's 4 percent Funding Certificates, 1934/46, issued in London by Lazard Brothers & Co., Ltd., of 11 Old Broad Street, and dated 1 September 1934. The issue is limited to a nominal amount not exceeding £155,892 14s. 0d., in accordance with a plan announced in The Times of 22 February 1934. description: A specimen of a 4.5 percent gold bond of the Republic of Cuba, an external loan due 1949, dated at Havana on 2 August 1909. It binds the Republic to pay the bearer on 1 August 1949, with half-yearly interest from 1 August 1909, a single principal expressed at once in four currencies: 500,000 dollars in United States gold coin, £102,880 13s. 2d. sterling, 2,100,000 German marks and 2,590,000 French francs, payable at the holder's option in New York, London, Frankfurt or Berlin, or Paris. ## Main Document Text

**REPUBLICA DE CUBA**

Bono de la Deuda Exterior Pagadero en Oro en 1949

Four and One-half Per Cent. Gold Bond, Due 1949 [External Loan]

The Republic of Cuba, for value received, promises to pay to the bearer hereof on the first day of August, 1949, in the City of New York, United States of America, Five Hundred Thousand Dollars, in gold coin of the United States of America of the present standard of weight and fineness, or, at the holder's option, in the City of London, England, £2 880 13s. 2d. Sterling, or in Frankfurt a.M. or Berlin, Germany, 2,100,000 German Marks, or in Paris, France, 2,590,000 Francs, and to pay interest on the above named sums, in any of said cities in the said respective currencies, at the rate of four and one-half per centum per annum from the first day of August, 1909, semi-annually on the first days of February and August in each year upon presentation of this bond for endorsement of statement of payment hereon.

The amount represented by this temporary bond forms a part of the loan of sixteen million, five hundred thousand dollars ($16,500,000) in gold coin of the United States of America, or its equivalent in foreign moneys as above stated, issued in pursuance of the decree dated January 25, 1909, of the Provisional Governor of Cuba and

in pursuance of the agreement between the Republic of Cuba and Speyer & Co., dated August__________, 1909, which decree together with extracts from said agreement is printed on the back hereof.

The principal, as well as the interest of this bond is forever exempt from all kinds of Cuban taxes, stamps, duties or assessments (whether of the Republic of Cuba or of any province or municipality therein) which exist or may be imposed hereafter. The Republic of Cuba will provide a sinking-fund for the retirement of said bonds as prescribed in said agreement with Speyer & Co. This bond is subject to be drawn for redemption at par and interest as stated in Article VI. of said agreement, and is also subject to redemption, at the option of the Republic of Cuba, at one hundred and five per cent. and accrued interest, as stated in Article VIII. of said agreement. At the date fixed for the redemption of this bond the interest thereon shall cease.

This bond shall not be valid or obligatory until the same shall have been duly authenticated by the execution by Speyer & Co. of the certificate endorsed hereon.

**HAVANA, CUBA, August 2, 1909.**

title: Czechoslovak State Sterling Bond, Prague
description: A bearer bond of the Czechoslovak State for £100, dated at Prague on 23 May 1924, part of an issue of £2,050,000 Eight Per Cent Sterling Bonds bearing the series name "1922." Bilingual in English and Czech, it has principal and interest payable in London through Baring Brothers & Co. and at Amsterdam through Hope & Co. title: Egyptian Credit Foncier Bearer Share

# Kingdom of Serbia — 5% Gold Loan of 1913, Bearer Obligation of 500 Francs / 500 Dinars — Transcription

## Original:

(Bilingual bond — French text in the left half, Serbian Cyrillic in the right half. The royal arms of Serbia, a crowned double-headed eagle on an ermine mantle, appear at the top centre. Elaborate interlaced Celtic-style borders frame the sheet.)

### Left half — French

**ROYAUME DE SERBIE**

**EMPRUNT 5% OR 1913**

D'UN MONTANT NOMINAL DE

**DEUX CENT CINQUANTE MILLIONS DE FRANCS**

*Créé en vertu de la loi du 18/31 Octobre 1913, dont extrait ci-contre.*

**Cet Emprunt est représenté par 500.000 Obligations de 500 Francs Or**

RAPPORTANT UN INTÉRÊT ANNUEL DE **25** FRANCS

Remboursables au pair par voie de tirages semestriels ou par achats en Bourse au-dessous du pair.

**MAXIMUM DE LA DURÉE DE L'AMORTISSEMENT : CINQUANTE ANS**

**Annuité affectée au service de l'intérêt et de l'amortissement de l'Emprunt :**
**13.550.000 FRANCS**

En dehors de l'engagement direct du Gouvernement Royal Serbe, cet Emprunt a pour gage spécial les recettes nettes de l'Administration Autonome des Monopoles, disponibles après le service des Emprunts visés par les lois des 8/20 Juillet 1895, 26 Juillet/8 Août 1902, 14/27 Décembre 1906 et 15/28 Décembre 1909, conformément à la loi du 18/31 Octobre 1913. L'Emprunt est en outre spécialement garanti, en première hypothèque, par les bénéfices nets du Monopole de l'Alcool, institué suivant la loi du 3/15 Août 1893 et géré par l'Administration Autonome des Monopoles.

**LES OBLIGATIONS ET COUPONS DU PRÉSENT EMPRUNT SONT EXEMPTS DE TOUS IMPÔTS TAXES OU RETENUES EXISTANTS OU FUTURS EN SERBIE**

**Obligation de 500 Francs 5%**
**AU PORTEUR**

**N° 467,139**

**INTÉRÊT**

Les Obligations de cet Emprunt rapportent annuellement **5 %** sur leur capital nominal. Les intérêts en sont payés semestriellement les 16 Février/1er Mars et 19 Août/1er Septembre de chaque année, contre remise des coupons correspondants.

**AMORTISSEMENT**

Dans le cas où l'amortissement ne pourrait s'opérer par achats au-dessous du pair, les tirages au sort auront lieu à Belgrade, les 19 Décembre/1er Janvier et 18 Juin/1er Juillet de chaque année, et les Obligations sorties seront remboursées au pair deux mois après, soit les 16 Février/1er Mars et 19 Août/1er Septembre respectivement.

Le paiement des coupons échus aura lieu, au choix des porteurs, chez les Établissements qui auront été désignés :

(bracketed list, left column of cities / right column of amounts:)
A **Belgrade** / A **Paris** / A **Bruxelles** / A **Genève** — à raison de — Fr. **12,50** le 16 Février/1er Mars. / Fr. **12,50** le 19 Août/1er Septembre. / Fr. **25** » par an, contre remise des coupons portant lesdites échéances,
A **Berlin** / A **Vienne** — Aux mêmes échéances, dans les monnaies de ces villes respectivement, *au cours du change à vue sur Paris.*

**Le texte français des Obligations fait foi.**

**Belgrade, le 18/31 Octobre 1913.**

ADMINISTRATION AUTONOME DES MONOPOLES
**du ROYAUME DE SERBIE :**
*POUR LE PRÉSIDENT DU CONSEIL.*
(signature: *M. T. Lecc[?]* — [illegible handwritten])

LE MINISTRE DES FINANCES
**du ROYAUME DE SERBIE,**
(signature: *[illegible] Patchou[?]* — [illegible handwritten])

POUR CONTROLE :
(signature: [illegible handwritten])

### Right half — Serbian (Cyrillic)

**КРАЉЕВИНА СРБИЈА**

**ЗАЈАМ 5% ЗЛАТО 1913**

У НОМИНАЛНОМ ИЗНОСУ ОД

**ДВЕ СТОТИНЕ ПЕДЕСЕТ МИЛИОНА ДИНАРА**

*Закључен на основу закона од 18./31. октобра 1913. г., чији се извод налази на другој страни.*

**Овај зајам представљен са 500.000 обавезница од 500 дин. у злату**

доноси годишњи интерес **25** динара

Исплатан помоћу шестомесечних вучења, кад је ал пари или, путем откупа испод номиналне вредности.

**НАЈДУЖЕ ТРАЈАЊЕ ИСПЛАТА : ПЕДЕСЕТ ГОДИНА**

**Годишњина намењена интересу и отплати овог зајма :**
**13.550.000 ДИНАРА.**

Осем нарочите обавезе Српске Краљевске Владе, овај зајам обезбеђен је вишковима чистих прихода Самосталне Монополске Управе, који остају слободни, пошто се подмире годишњине зајмове од 8./20. јула 1895. год., 26. јула/8. августа 1902. год. 14./27. децембра 1906. г. и 15./28. децембра 1909. г. према закону од 18./31. октобра 1913. год. Сем тога за обезбеду овога зајма служи још на првом месту и као нарочита залога и чиста добит Монопола на алкохол, установљеног по закону од 3./15. августа 1893. год. а којом рукује Управа Државних Монопола.

**ОБАВЕЗНИЦЕ И КУПОНИ ОВОГ ЗАЈМА ОСЛОБОЂЕНИ СУ СВИХ ПОРЕЗА И ТАКСА САДАШЊИХ И БУДУЋИХ У СРБИЈИ.**

**Обавезница од 500 динара 5%**
**на доносиоца**

**ИНТЕРЕС**

Обавезнице овога зајма доносе годишње **5 %** од свог номиналног капитала. Интерес се плаћа шестомесечно, 16. фебруара/1. марта и 19. августа/1. септембра сваке године, по предаји одговарајућих купона.

**ОТПЛАТА**

У случају да се отплата не може извршити путем откупа испод номиналне вредности, вучења ће се извршити у Београду 19. децембра/1. јануара и 18. јуна/1. јула сваке године а извучене обавезнице исплаћиваће се по номиналном износу после два месеца то јест 16. фебруара/1. марта и 19. августа/1. септембра.

Купони ће се исплаћивати по жељи доносиоца код означених Завода и то :

(bracketed list, left column of cities / right column of amounts:)
У **Београду** / У **Паризу** / У **Брислу** / У **Женеви** — по — Динара **12,50** 16. фебруара/1. марта. / Динара **12,50** 19. августа/1. септембра. / Динара **25.** » годишње уз предају купона, чији је рок за исплату.
У **Берлину** / У **Бечу** — У истим роковима за исплату у монети тих вароши односно *по берзанском курсу по виђењу на Париз.*

**Француски текст Обавезница је обавезан.**

### Lower centre band
**5% OR 1913**

### Printer's imprint (bottom)
IMPRIMERIE CHAIX, RUE BERGÈRE, 20, PARIS. — 4825-1-14 — (Encre Lorilleux).

### Tax stamp (black circular overprint, left of serial number)
FONDS D'ÉTATS ÉTRANGERS / 3% PAYÉS AVANT LE 9 AVRIL 1914 / PARIS / 30 · 12 · 1914

## English Translation:

(Bilingual bond — French on the left, Serbian on the right; both texts are identical in content. The crowned Serbian royal arms sit at the top.)

**KINGDOM OF SERBIA**

**5% GOLD LOAN 1913**

OF A NOMINAL AMOUNT OF

**TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY MILLION FRANCS**

*Created by virtue of the law of 18/31 October 1913, an extract of which appears alongside.*

**This Loan is represented by 500,000 Obligations of 500 Gold Francs**

BEARING ANNUAL INTEREST OF **25** FRANCS

Redeemable at par by means of semi-annual drawings or by purchases on the Bourse below par.

**MAXIMUM DURATION OF AMORTIZATION: FIFTY YEARS**

**Annuity assigned to the service of the interest and amortization of the Loan:**
**13,550,000 FRANCS**

Apart from the direct undertaking of the Royal Serbian Government, this Loan has as special security the net revenues of the Autonomous Administration of Monopolies, available after the service of the Loans covered by the laws of 8/20 July 1895, 26 July/8 August 1902, 14/27 December 1906 and 15/28 December 1909, in conformity with the law of 18/31 October 1913. The Loan is moreover specially guaranteed, by first mortgage, by the net profits of the Alcohol Monopoly, established under the law of 3/15 August 1893 and managed by the Autonomous Administration of Monopolies.

**TO BEARER**

**INTEREST**

The Obligations of this Loan bear interest annually at **5%** on their nominal capital. The interest is paid semi-annually on 16 February/1 March and 19 August/1 September of each year, against surrender of the corresponding coupons.

**AMORTIZATION**

In the event that amortization cannot be carried out by purchases below par, the drawings by lot will take place at Belgrade, on 19 December/1 January and 18 June/1 July of each year, and the Obligations drawn will be redeemed at par two months later, that is on 16 February/1 March and 19 August/1 September respectively.

Payment of matured coupons will take place, at the bearers' choice, at the Establishments that will have been designated:

At **Berlin** / At **Vienna** — On the same due dates, in the currencies of these cities respectively, *at the rate of exchange at sight on Paris.*

**The French text of the Obligations is authoritative.**

**Belgrade, 18/31 October 1913.**

AUTONOMOUS ADMINISTRATION OF MONOPOLIES
of the KINGDOM OF SERBIA:

THE MINISTER OF FINANCE

title: City of Berlin Municipal Loan Bond, Berlin
description: A bearer debenture of the City of Berlin for fifty thousand marks in Reich currency, part of the 8 to 18 percent Berliner Stadtanleihe of 3.75 billion marks, dated Berlin, 31 July 1923. Bilingual German and English text records that the issue rested on resolutions of the municipal authorities of 11 and 26 April 1923, authorizing a loan of up to ten billion marks against the city's assets and revenues, the bond being non-callable by its holder. The mark was in hyperinflation at the time of issue, which both the floating 8 to 18 percent coupon and the scale of the face value reflect.

# STADT BERLIN - SCHULDVERSCHREIBUNG (Municipal Bond)

## Original (German):

1923
Januar/Juli

M. 50000

**Main Document:**

STADT BERLIN

Schuldverschreibung

Buchtabe S über Nr: 15581

Fünfzigtausend Mark
deutsche Reichswährung

Ausgeüertigt mit Grund der mit Ermächtigung des preußischen Staatsministeriums erteilten Genehmigung nach Maßgabe des Beschlusses vom 30. Juni 1923 (Reichsbl. Anlage- und Veneralsamtsblatt) vom 5. Juli 1923).

Auf Grund der von dem Oberpräsidenten von Berlin genehmigten Beschlüsse der städtischen Behörden vom 11., 26. April 1923 wegen Aufnahme einer Anleihe von 10. Milliarden Mark bekundet hierdurch die Magistratur der Stadt Berlin namens der Stadt durch diese, für jeden Inhaber gültige Schuldverschreibung die Gewährung einer tiefsten des Gläubigers unhinderbar Darlehnsschuld von

50 000 Mark.

Die Bedingungen dieser Anleihe sind umfältig abgedruckt.

Zur Sicherheit der hierdurch eingegangenen Verpflichtung haftet die Stadt Berlin mit ihrem Vermögen und mit ihrer Steuerkraft.

Dafern unr Urkunde haben wir diese Aussfertigung unter unserer Unterschrift erteilt.

Berlin, den 31. Juli 1923.

Magistrat der Reichshauptstadt.

[Signatures]
Oberbürgermeister [illegible signature]
Kämmerer [illegible signature]

Aussfertigt [illegible] Seite 156

[Illegible signature]
Kämmerermeister.

1923

M. 50000

CITY OF BERLIN

Debenture (Debt Certificate)

Volume S, No: 15581

Fifty Thousand Marks
German Reich Currency

Issued on the basis of authorization from the Prussian State Ministry, issued in accordance with the resolution of 30 June 1923 (Reichsbl. Loan and General Administrative Gazette) of 5 July 1923.

On the basis of the resolutions of the municipal authorities of Berlin approved by the Superior President of Berlin from 11 and 26 April 1923 regarding the raising of a loan of 10 billion marks, the Magistracy of the City of Berlin hereby declares to every bearer of this debenture the granting of a debt obligation from the creditor of

50,000 Marks.

The conditions of this loan are printed on the reverse.

For the security of the obligations hereby incurred, the City of Berlin is liable with its assets and with its tax revenues.

We have issued this document under our signature in confirmation thereof.

Berlin, 31 July 1923.

Magistrate of the Imperial Capital.

Municipal Treasurer [illegible]

title: Kingdom of Greece Guaranteed Gold Loan Bond
description: A bearer bond of the Kingdom of Greece for the 2.5 percent Guaranteed Gold Loan of 1898, with a face value of 2,500 drachmas, equal to 2,500 francs, and a sterling equivalent of £100, the holder drawing £2 10s a year payable half-yearly on 1 April and 1 October. Printed in four languages, Greek, French, English and Russian, the text records the joint and several guarantee of France, Great Britain and Russia, settled by the International Convention of Paris of March 1898. title: Hungarian Mortgage Bank Conversion Prize Bond, Budapest
description: A trilingual conversion prize bond for 100 korona, issued in Budapest and dated 1 October 1906 by A Magyar Jelzálog-Hitelbank, styled in German as the Ungarische Hypothekenbank and in French as the Société de Crédit Foncier du Royaume de Hongrie. The heading recites its purpose: the bank's original 1894 loan of 70,000,000 korona had 68,820,000 korona still outstanding, and under the law of 1889 and royal finance-ministry decrees of 1905 and 1906 the unredeemed remainder was converted into these new lottery obligations. Upon conversion the original bonds' 3 percent interest ceased, so this conversion prize bond pays no coupon interest; it offers holders only participation in the periodic prize drawings.
creator: Magyar Jelzalog-Hitelbank (Hungarian Mortgage Credit Bank)
notes: Littera A, Serie 881, No. 77, 100 Korona. Budapest, 1894. Total issue: 60,000,000 korona. Trilingual Hungarian/French/German. Signed by Bank President and Director.

*(Center body, Hungarian)*

Jelen A. részkötvény az azonos sorozatú és számú B. részkötvénynyel együtt az ugyanilyen sorozatú és számú eredeti 200 koronás 3%-os nyereménykötvény helyébe lépvén, ezen részkötvény a B. jelűvel együtt, tehát mindegyik részkötvény fele-fele részben jogot ad az eredeti 3%-os nyereménykötvény változatlan nyereményélvezetére, a túloldali I. sorsolási terv értelmében.

A konverzió folytán az eredeti 3%-os kötvénykamatozás megszünvén, ennek helyébe a kötvénytulajdonos — mindegyik részkötvény után is osztatlanul és egészben — a II. alatti sorsolási terv szerinti nyereményhuzásokban való részvételre nyert jogosultságot.

**SOCIÉTÉ DE CRÉDIT FONCIER DU ROYAUME DE HONGRIE.**

**COUPURE A**

**DE 100 COURONNES**

**DE L'OBLIGATION À LOTS CONVERTIE**

émise en vertu de la loi IX de l'an 1889 et aux termes des modalités acceptées par les arrêtés No 98456/1905, 14193/1906 et 26351/1906 du Ministre des Finances, pour la conversion des 68.320,000 Cour. nomin. encore non amorties des Obligations 3% à primes de la Société de Crédit Foncier du Royaume de Hongrie émises en 1894 pour un montant de 70.000,000 de Cour. nomin.

Par suite, la présente Coupure A, avec l'autre Coupure B, soit chacune de ces Coupures pour la moitié, donne droit à la jouissance invariable des lots de l'Obligation originale 3% à lots, conformément au plan des tirages I imprimé au verso.

The repayment of the capital amounting to 100 Cr. for each Coupon, i.e. the 200 Cr. original for the two Coupons, takes place, in accordance with plan III printed on the reverse, within the 53 years still remaining to run of the amortization period, fixed originally at 65 years, of the converted 3% prize Obligations, and in such a way that each Coupon receives the nominal amount of 100 Cr. and at the same time a premium of 40 Cr.

These Obligations are guaranteed by the loans made by the Society under the terms of the law XXXII of the year 1897 and in accordance with its Statutes, to municipalities, towns, communes and other civil persons able to contract a loan.

The withdrawal of the Obligations drawn at the drawings and the payment of the winnings and premiums take place in accordance with the provisions printed on the reverse.

title: Principality of Bulgaria Hypothecary State Loan Bond, Sophia
description: A bearer bond of the Principality of Bulgaria for its 6 percent Hypothecary State Loan of 1892, dated at Sophia on 3/15 December 1892, with a face value of five hundred francs, equal to five hundred leva at the gold par then linking the two currencies.
