**Body text — Bulgarian column (left):**

Настоящий заемъ е издаденъ:
въ 61.550 отрѣзка № 000.001—061.550 по 1 облигация,
» 30.005 » » 061.551—121.560 » 2 облигации,
» 24.000 » » 121.561—241.560 » 5 »,
» 1.760 » » 241.561—285.560 » 25 ».

Облигациитѣ на този заемъ носятъ годишна лихва 6% на именния капиталъ, платима шестмесечно на 2/14 Януарий и на 1/13 Юлий всяка година срѣщу предаването на купонитѣ.

Тоя заемъ ще се изплати въ 33 години, споредъ помѣстената въ облигациитѣ таблица за погашение, чрѣзъ шестмесечни тѣгления, които ще станатъ въ София два мѣсеца прѣди падежа на купонитѣ — първи пѫть на 1/13 Май 1893 година; отъ гдѣто Правителството [запазва] правото да изплати по номинала стойность въ всяко врѣме, но не прѣди 2/14 Януарий 1898 год., всичкитѣ облигации останали въ обращение.

Изваденитѣ при тѣглението облигации ще бѫдатъ изплатени по именната имъ стойность на шестмесечния лихвенъ падежъ, който ще слѣдъ тѣглението, срѣщу предаването имъ, придружени съ всичкитѣ неизтекли купони слѣдъ срока за изплащането и съ съотвѣтствующий талонъ.

Изплащането на изтеченитѣ купони и на изтеглѣнитѣ облигации ще става въ злато и по избора на носителя:
въ София у касата за съкровището,
въ Виена у Импер. Кралска привилегирована Банка на Австрийскитѣ земи,
въ Лондонъ, Парижъ, Берлинъ, Амстердамъ, Женева
и други градове у учрежденията и банкеритѣ, които относно ще бѫдатъ показани отъ Българското Правителство.

Изплащането става въ София съ златни левове, въ Виена съ Австрийски флорини златни, въ Лондонъ съ лири стерлинги, въ Берлинъ и други Германски мѣста, гдѣто се случи, съ марки, въ Парижъ и други градове съ златни франкове.

Купонитѣ и изтеглѣнитѣ облигации отъ настоящий заемъ сѫ и ще бѫдатъ свободни отъ всѣкакъвъ видъ налогъ, такси или другъ данъкъ прѣдвидени или който би се прѣдвидялъ отъ българскитѣ закони.

Изтеченитѣ купони както и изтеглѣнитѣ облигации отъ настоящий заемъ ще се приематъ по именната имъ стойность въ всичкитѣ правителствени каси на Княжество България за изплащане на такси, мита, налози и други данъци, прѣдвидени или които би се прѣдвидели отъ бюджета на Княжеството.

Непрѣдставенитѣ купони губятъ стойностьта си слѣдъ петь години, а изтеглѣнитѣ облигации — слѣдъ трийсеть години отъ падежа имъ.

Плащането на купонитѣ и на изтеглѣнитѣ облигации е обезпечено съ първа ипотека:
а) на желѣзо-пѫтнитѣ линии Каспичанъ—София—Кюстендилъ и Русе—Варна,
б) на пристанищата въ Варна и Бургасъ и всичкитѣ приходи и такси, които се събиратъ или ще се събиратъ въ тѣзи пристанища.

За тая цѣль Българското правителство е установило на 18/30 Ноемврий 1892 год. подъ № 123, съгласно гражданский Български законъ, първа ипотека върху казанитѣ желѣзо-пѫтни линии съ всичкитѣ имъ станции, постройки, принадлежности и подвижни и неподвиженъ материалъ, както и върху двѣтѣ горѣозначени пристанища съ всичкитѣ имъ постройки, сгради и сѫоръжения. Ипотеката е дадена на Императорската Кралска привилегирована Банка на Австрийскитѣ земи въ името на притежателитѣ на облигациитѣ.

Ако Българското правителство не плати въ разстояние на шесть мѣсеца слѣдъ падежа изтеченитѣ купони или изтеглѣнитѣ облигации, притежателитѣ на облигациитѣ ще иматъ властьта и правото да взематъ въ свои рѫцѣ експлоатацията на ипотекиранитѣ желѣзници и пристанища за да се изплатятъ.

Ако Българското правителство не изплати въ разстояние на двѣ години произходящитѣ отъ този заемъ длъгове, притежателитѣ на облигациитѣ ще иматъ правото да пристѫпятъ къмъ продажбата на казанитѣ желѣзопѫтни линии и да употрѣбятъ произведенето отъ тая продажба за изплащане изтеченитѣ купони, изтеглѣнитѣ облигации и остатъка отъ заемътъ, който не бѫде още погашенъ, слѣдъ като се прибѣгне до правителството за неизплатеното количество.

Всичкитѣ тия права що могатъ да бѫдатъ упражнени въ името и за смѣтка на притежателитѣ на облигациитѣ отъ Императорската Кралска привилегирована Банка на Австрийскитѣ земи, безъ да бѫде тя задължена за това.

Извлечение отъ удостовѣрението за ипотечното вписване:

« Нотариата при Софийский Окр. Сѫдъ удостовѣрява чрѣзъ настоящето, че за обезпечение на Държавний заемъ отъ 1892 год. отъ 142,780.000 лева злати = 5,711.200 лири стерлинги = 115,651.800 марки = 57,112.000 австрийски флорини злати, раздѣленъ на 285.560 облигации по 500 лева = 20 лири стерлинги = 405 марки = 200 австрийски флорини злати всѣка една и издаденъ съгласно Княжески Указъ отъ 27 Октомврий/8 Ноемврий 1892 година подъ № 204, въсъ основание закона утвърденъ съ Княжески Указъ отъ 18/30 Декемврий 1888 г. подъ № 288, обнародванъ въ Държавенъ Вѣстникъ брой 8 отъ 1889 год., се вписани въ ипотечния книга подъ първа ипотека Бълг. Държавни желѣзопѫтни линии Каспичанъ—София—Кюстендилъ и Русе—Варна съ всичкитѣ имъ станции, постройки, принадлежности, подвижен и неподвиженъ материалъ и пристанищата въ Варна и Бургасъ съ всичкитѣ имъ приходи и такси, които се получаватъ или ще се получаватъ, на Императорската Кралска привилегирована Банка на Австрийскитѣ земи, като представитель на притежателитѣ на облигациитѣ. »

Добивката отъ настоящий заемъ е предназначена изключително за построенето и турянето въ експлоатация на желѣзницата Каспичанъ—Шумень—Търново—Селвиево—Ловечъ—Плѣвенъ—София—Кюстендилъ и на пристанищата въ Варна и Бургасъ и не може подъ никакъвъ предлогъ да се отклече отъ това си спеціално предназначение.

Френский текстъ на облигациитѣ служи за основа.

**СОФИЯ, 3/15 Декемврий 1892 година.**

---

**Body text — French column (right):**

Le présent emprunt est émis:
en 61.550 coupures No. 000,001—061.550 à 1 Obligation,
» 30.005 » » 061.551—121.560 à 2 Obligations,
» 24.000 » » 121.561—241.560 à 5 »,
» 1.760 » » 241.561—285.560 à 25 ».

Les obligations de cet emprunt portent intérêts à 6% l'an du capital nominal, payables semestriellement les 2/14 Janvier et 1/13 Juillet de chaque année contre remise des coupons.

L'amortissement de cet emprunt se fera au pair en 33 ans suivant le tableau d'amortissement annexé aux obligations, par voie de tirages semestriels qui auront lieu à Sophia deux mois avant chaque échéance de coupons — la première fois le 1/13 Mai 1893; toutefois le Gouvernement se réserve la faculté de rembourser au pair à toute époque, mais pas avant le 1/13 Janvier 1898, toutes les obligations restant en circulation.

Les obligations sorties au tirage seront remboursables au pair à l'échéance semestrielle d'intérêts postérieure à leur tirage, contre remise des dites, munies de tous les coupons non encore échus après le terme de remboursement et du talon y afférent.

Le paiement des coupons et des obligations arrivées à remboursement a lieu en or, au choix du porteur:
À Sophia: à la Caisse du Trésor,
À Vienne: à la Banque Impériale Royale Privilégiée des Pays Autrichiens,
À Londres, Paris, Berlin, Amsterdam, Genève et dans quelques villes auprès des établissements et banquiers qui seront ultérieurement désignés par le Gouvernement Bulgare.

Le paiement a lieu à Sophia en Leva or, à Vienne en Florins d'Autriche or, à Londres en Livres Sterling, à Berlin et autres places allemandes à désigner éventuellement, en Reichsmark, à Paris et autres villes en Francs or.

Les coupons et les obligations sorties au tirage du présent emprunt sont et seront libres de toute espèce d'impôt, taxes ou autres redevances prévues ou à prévoir par les lois bulgares.

Les coupons échus ainsi que les obligations sorties au tirage du présent emprunt seront reçus au pair par toutes les caisses gouvernementales de la Principauté de Bulgarie en paiement de droits de taxes, douane, impôts et autres redevances prévues ou à prévoir par le budget de la Principauté.

Les coupons non-présentés sont prescrits après cinq ans et les titres remboursables après trente ans de leur échéance.

Le paiement des coupons et des obligations sorties au tirage est garanti par première hypothèque:
a) sur les lignes ferrées Kaspitchan—Sophia—Kustendil et Roustchouk—Varna,
b) sur les ports de Varna et Bourgas et sur tous les revenus et taxes perçus ou à percevoir dans ces ports.

À cet effet, le Gouvernement Bulgare a constitué en date du 18/30 Novembre 1892, No. 123, conformément à la loi civile bulgare, une première hypothèque sur les dites lignes ferrées avec toutes leurs stations, construction, dépendances et matériel fixe et roulant ainsi que sur les deux ports sus nommés avec toutes leurs constructions, bâtiments et installations. L'hypothèque est donnée à la Banque Impériale Royale Privilégiée des Pays Autrichiens au nom des obligataires.

Si le Gouvernement de Bulgarie ne payait pas pendant six mois après l'échéance les coupons échus ou les obligations sorties au tirage, les obligataires auront la faculté et le droit de prendre en main l'exploitation des lignes et des ports hypothéqués pour se faire payer.

Si le Gouvernement de Bulgarie n'acquittait pas pendant deux ans les dettes provenant de cet emprunt, les obligataires auront le droit de procéder à la vente des dites lignes de chemins de fer et d'appliquer les résultats de cette vente au remboursement des coupons échus, des obligations sorties au tirage et du reste éventuel de l'emprunt qui ne serait pas encore amorti, sauf recours contre le gouvernement pour la somme restée en souffrance.

At Sophia: at the Treasury Fund,

At London, Paris, Berlin, Amsterdam, Geneva and in some cities at the establishments and bankers who will later be designated by the Bulgarian Government.

a) on the railway lines Kaspitchan—Sophia—Kustendil and Roustchouk—Varna,

Настоящий заемъ е изданъ:
въ 61.550 отрѣзъка № 000.001—061.550 по 1 облигация,
„ 30.005 „ „ 061.551—121.560 „ 2 облигации,

Облигациитѣ на тоя заемъ носятъ годишна лихва 6% на именний капиталъ, платима шестмѣсечно на 2/14 Януарий и на 1/13 Юлий всѣка година срѣщо прѣдаваннето на купонитѣ.

Тоя заемъ ще се исплати въ 33 години, споредъ помѣстената въ облигациитѣ таблица за погашение, чрѣзъ шестмѣсечни тѣгления, които ще ставатъ въ София два мѣсеца прѣди падежа на купонитѣ — първня пѫть на 1/13 Май 1893 година, нъ при това Правителството си запазя правото да исплати по именната имъ стойность въ всѣко врѣме, нъ не прѣди 2/14 Януарий 1898 год., всичкитѣ облигации останали въ обращение.

Излѣзналитѣ при тѣглението облигации ще бѫдатъ исплатени по именната имъ стойность на шестмѣсечний лихвенъ падежъ, който иде слѣдъ тѣглението, срѣщо прѣдаваннето имъ, придружени съ всичкитѣ неизсрочени купони слѣдъ срока за исплащанието и съ съотвѣтствующий талонъ.

Исплащаннето на изсроченитѣ купони и на истѣгленитѣ облигации ще става въ злато и по избора на носителя:
въ София у кассата на съкровището,
въ Виена у Импер. Кралска привилегирована Банка на Австрийскитѣ земи,
въ Лондонъ, Парижъ, Берлинъ, Амстердамъ, Женева
и други градове у учрежденията и банкеритѣ, които отпослѣ ще бѫдатъ показани отъ Българското Правителство.

Исплащанието става въ София съ златни левове, въ Виена съ Австрийски флорини златни, въ Лондонъ съ лири стерлинги, въ Берлинъ и други Германски мѣста, гдѣто се случи, съ марки, въ Парижъ и други градове съ златни франкове.

Купонитѣ и истѣгленитѣ облигации отъ настоящий заемъ сѫ и ще бѫдатъ свободни отъ всѣкакъвъ видъ налогъ, такси или другъ данъкъ прѣдвиденъ или който би се прѣдвидѣлъ отъ българскитѣ закони.

Изсроченитѣ купони както и истѣгленитѣ облигации отъ настоящий заемъ ще се приматъ по именната имъ стойность въ всичкитѣ правителственни касси на Княжество България за исплащание на такси, мита, налози и други данъци, прѣдвидени или които би се прѣдвидѣли въ бюджета на Княжеството.

Непрѣдявенитѣ купони губятъ стойностьта си слѣдъ петь години, а истѣгленитѣ облигации — слѣдъ тридесеть години отъ падежа имъ.

Плащаннето на купонитѣ и на истѣгленитѣ облигации е обезпечено съ първа ипотека:
а) на желѣзно-пѫтнитѣ линии Каспичанъ—София—Кюстендилъ и Руссе—Варна,
б) на пристанищата въ Варна и Бургазъ и на всичкитѣ приходи и такси, които се събиратъ или ще се събиратъ въ тия пристанища.

За тая цѣль Българското правителство е установило на 18/30 Ноемврий 1892 год. подъ № 123, съгласно гражданский Български законъ, първа ипотека върху казанитѣ желѣзно-пѫтни линии съ всичкитѣ имъ станции, постройки, принадлѣжности и подвиженъ и неподвиженъ материалъ, както и върху двѣтѣ горѣспомѣнати пристанища съ всичкитѣ имъ постройки, сгради и съорѫжения. Ипотеката е дадена на Императорската Кралска привилегирована Банка на Австрийскитѣ земи въ името на притѣжателитѣ на облигациитѣ.

Ако Българското правителство не плати въ растояние на шесть мѣсеци слѣдъ падежа изсроченитѣ купони или истѣгленитѣ облигации, притѣжателитѣ на облигациитѣ ще иматъ властьта и правото да взематъ въ своя рѫка експлоатацията на ипотекиранитѣ желѣзници и пристанища за да се наплатятъ.

Ако Българското правителство не исплати въ растояние на двѣ години происходящитѣ отъ тоя заемъ дългове, притѣжателитѣ на облигациитѣ ще иматъ правото да пристѫпятъ къмъ продажбата на казанитѣ желѣзно-пѫтни линии и да употрѣбятъ произвѣденнето отъ тая продажба за исплащание изсроченитѣ купони, истѣгленитѣ облигации и случайний остатъкъ отъ заема, който не бѫде още погасенъ, освѣнъ ако не се прибѣгне до правителството за неплатеното количество.

Всичкитѣ тия права ще могатъ да бѫдатъ упражнени въ името и за смѣтка на притѣжателитѣ на облигациитѣ отъ Императорската Кралска привилегирована Банка на Австрийскитѣ земи, безъ да бѫде тя задължена за това.

Извлечение отъ удостовѣреннето за ипотечното вписвание:

„Нотарната при Софийский Окр. Сѫдъ удостовѣряка чрѣзъ настоящето, че за обезпечение на Държавний заемъ отъ 1892 год. отъ 142,780.000 лева златни = 5,711.200 лири стерлинги = 115,651.800 марки = 57,112.000 австрийски флорини златни, раздѣленъ на 285.560 облигации по 500 лева златни = 20 лири стерлинги = 405 марки = 200 австрийски флорини златни всѣка една и изданъ съгласно Княжеский Указъ отъ 27 Октомврий / 8 Ноемврий 1892 година подъ № 204, възъ основание закона утвърденъ съ Княжески Указъ отъ 18/30 Декемврий 1888 г. подъ № 288, обнародванъ въ Държавенъ Вѣстникъ брой 8 отъ 1889 год., сѫ вписани въ ипотечната книга подъ първа ипотека Блъг. Държавни желѣзнопѫтни линии Каспичанъ—София—Кюстендилъ и Руссе—Варна съ всичкитѣ имъ станции, постройки, принадлѣжности, подвиженъ и неподвиженъ материалъ и пристанищата въ Варна и Бургазъ съ всичкитѣ имъ приходи и такси, които се получаватъ или ще се получаватъ, въ полза на Императорската Кралска привилегирована Банка на Австрийскитѣ земи, като прѣдставитель на притѣжателитѣ на облигациитѣ.“

Добивката отъ настоящия заемъ е назначена исключително за построението и туряннето въ експлоатация на желѣзницата Каспичанъ—Шуменъ—Търново—Севлиево—Ловечъ—Плѣвенъ—София—Кюстендилъ и на пристанищата въ Варна и Бургасъ и не може подъ никакъвъ предлогъ да се отвлече отъ това си специално назначение.

Les coupons et les obligations sorties au tirage du présent emprunt sont et seront libres de toute espèce d'impôt, taxes ou autres redevances prévues ou à prévoir par les lois bulgares.

Les coupons échus ainsi que les obligations sorties au tirage du présent emprunt seront reçus au pair par toutes les caisses gouvernementales de la Principauté de Bulgarie en paiement de droits de taxes, douane, impôts et autres redevances prévues ou à prévoir par le budget de la Principauté.

Les coupons non-présentés sont prescrits après cinq ans et les titres remboursables après trente ans de leur échéance.

Le paiement des coupons et des obligations sorties au tirage est garanti par première hypothèque:
a) sur les lignes ferrées Kaspitchan—Sophia—Kustendil et Roustchouk—Varna,
b) sur les ports de Varna et Bourgas et sur tous les revenus et taxes perçus ou à percevoir dans ces ports.

A cet effet, le Gouvernement Bulgare a constitué en date du 18/30 Novembre 1892, No. 123, conformément à la loi civile bulgare, une première hypothèque sur les dites lignes ferrées avec toutes leurs stations, constructions, dépendances et matériel fixe et roulant ainsi que sur les deux ports sus nommées avec toutes leurs constructions, bâtiments et installations. L'hypothèque est donnée à la Banque Impériale Royale Privilégiée des Pays Autrichiens au nom des obligataires.

Si le Gouvernement de Bulgarie ne payait pas pendant six mois après l'échéance les coupons échus ou les obligations sorties au tirage, les obligataires auront la faculté et le droit de prendre en main l'exploitation des lignes et des ports hypothéqués pour se faire payer.

Si le Gouvernement de Bulgarie n'acquittait pas pendant deux ans les dettes provenant de cet emprunt, les obligataires auront le droit de procéder à la vente des dites lignes de chemins de fer et d'appliquer les résultats de cette vente au remboursement des coupons échus, des obligations sorties au tirage et du reste éventuel de l'emprunt qui ne serait pas encore amorti, sauf recours contre le gouvernement pour la somme restée en souffrance.

Tous ces droits pourront être exercés au nom et pour le compte des obligataires par la Banque Impériale Royale Privilégiée des Pays Autrichiens, sans qu'elle y soit obligée.

Upon your report, examined in a Special Committee, We have deemed it useful to proceed with the redemption of the 4½% mortgage certificates not drawn by lot, issued in 1887 by the former Society of Mutual Land Credit and secured — on the basis of the opinion of the State Council confirmed by Us on 6 February 1895 — by state obligations, on a nominal capital of 78,367,300 rubles in gold, granting to holders, at their wish, the possibility of exchanging them for interest-bearing paper at a reduced rate of three and eight-tenths percent (3⁸/₁₀%); to which end We hereby command you: to grant holders the right, within the period and on the conditions established by you, to present the mortgage certificates belonging to them for exchange into three-and-eight-tenths percent (3⁸/₁₀%) paper, issued exclusively for this purpose, on the following bases, whereby in place of 100 gold rubles (1 ruble = 1/15 of an imperial) nominal in the 4½% mortgage certificates of the former Society of Mutual Land Credit, 150 rubles are given in the newly issued paper.

1. The said 3⁸/₁₀% paper is entered in the State Debt Book under the designation: "3⁸/₁₀% conversion bonds, issued by the Government in exchange for the 4½% mortgage certificates of the former Society of Mutual Land Credit."

2. These bonds are issued as registered or to bearer, in denominations of 150, 750 and 1500 rubles, reckoning each 150 rubles = 324 imperial German marks = 400 fr. = 15 pounds st. 17 sh. = 192 Dutch guilders.

3. Rules concerning registered bonds, their transfer from one person to another, and their exchange into bearer form and back are approved by you.

4. The rate of income is fixed at three and eight-tenths percent per annum; interest is paid semi-annually, on 2/14 January and 1/13 July.

5. The 3⁸/₁₀% conversion bonds are redeemed at nominal value over 81 years by means of semi-annual drawings held on 19 March and 19 September; the capital of bonds drawn is paid on the coupon-payment date following the drawing.
The sinking fund of these bonds is formed by a semi-annual allocation of 0.095% of their nominal capital, with the addition of 1.9% on the nominal capital of bonds already redeemed.
The bonds retain their payment validity for thirty years from the dates fixed for their payment, and the coupons for ten years from the onset of their payment dates.
Until 1/14 January 1906 the sinking-fund allocation will not be increased; before that same date neither redemption nor conversion of these bonds will be undertaken.

6. Payment of interest and repayment of capital is made, at the bearers' option, in St. Petersburg at the State Bank in rubles; in Berlin and Frankfurt a/M. in imperial German marks; in Paris and Brussels in francs; in London in pounds sterling; in Amsterdam in Dutch guilders — at the places designated by you for this purpose.
The capital and interest of the 3⁸/₁₀% conversion bonds are forever exempt from all Russian taxes.

pages.description: This is a bearer conversion bond (конверсіонная облигація) of the Imperial Russian Government, denominated at 150 rubles and equated on its face to 324 imperial German marks, 400 francs, 15 pounds 17 shillings sterling, and 192 Dutch guilders. It carries three and eight-tenths percent interest per annum, payable 2/14 January and 1/13 July, with capital and interest declared forever exempt from Russian taxation. Issued under the Imperial Ukase of 6 March 1898, it was offered in exchange for the 4.5% mortgage certificates of the former Society of Mutual Land Credit (Общество Взаимнаго Поземельнаго Кредита), part of a total emission of 85,412,400 rubles registered in the State Debt Book. Payable through Mendelssohn and Bleichröder in Berlin, Rothschild in Paris, and Lambert in Brussels, the instrument shows how late-imperial Russia refinanced costly mortgage debt into cheaper, tax-free state paper marketed across Western Europe. The double-headed eagle and dense engraved border assert sovereign credit, while a clause barring redemption or conversion before 1/14 January 1906 reassured holders of a fixed return.

This is a talon — the renewal stub of a coupon sheet — for a 3⁸/₁₀% Conversion Bond (конверсіонная облигація) of the Imperial Russian Government, with a face value of 150 rubles. The bilingual Russian and French sheet carries the bond's gold equivalences, fixing the 150 rubles at 324 reichsmark, 400 francs, 15 pounds 17 shillings sterling, and 192 Dutch florins, a multi-market pricing that bound the issue to the Berlin, Paris, London, and Amsterdam exchanges where Russia placed its debt. The retained coupons, numbered 38 through 48, each promise 2 rubles 85 kopecks, payable half-yearly through the offices and branches of the State Bank of Russia, with the visible coupons falling due between 1917 and January 1922. Such conversion loans let the Tsarist treasury refinance older, costlier obligations at a lower fixed rate, and the document's sober typographic frame and quadrilingual valuation speak to an empire that financed itself on the confidence of foreign rentiers.

**НА ПРЕДЪЯВИТЕЛЯ**

На основаніи ВЫСОЧАЙШАГО Указа 1 Марта 1902 года для реализаціи причитающагося Россіи вознагражденія въ возмѣщеніе убытковъ, понесенныхъ вслѣдствіе смутъ въ Китаѣ, выпускается настоящій 4% заемъ на нарицательный капиталъ въ 181.959.000 рублей, равныхъ 393.000.000 имперскимъ германскимъ маркамъ, равныхъ 231.870.000 голландскимъ гульденамъ, равныхъ 19.257.000 фунтамъ стерлинговъ, ежегодные платежи по коему находились въ точномъ соотвѣтствіи съ причитающимися отъ Китайскаго Правительства ежегодными уплатами процентовъ и погашенія по слѣдующей Россіи части вознагражденія, которое Китай обязался выплатить согласно эдикта Китайскаго Императора отъ 29 Мая новаго стиля 1901 года.

Заемъ сей внесенъ въ Государственную Долговую Книгу подъ наименованіемъ: „Россійскій 4% Государственный заемъ 1902 г.", выпущенный для реализаціи причитающагося Россіи отъ Китая вознагражденія".

Облигаціи сего займа выпускаются именныя и на предъявителя, достоинствомъ въ 500, 1000, 2000 и 5000 имп. герм. марокъ, считая каждыя 1000 имп. герм. марокъ = 463 рублямъ = 590 голл. гульд. = 49 фунт. стерл.

Владѣлецъ сей облигаціи имѣетъ право на сумму въ 1000 имп. герм. марокъ = 463 руб., приносящую ЧЕТЫРЕ процента въ годъ дохода до погашенія оной тиражемъ или выкупомъ; теченіе процентовъ начинается съ 19 Декабря 1901/1 Января 1902 г.

Облигаціи сіи освобождены навсегда отъ всякихъ русскихъ налоговъ.

Проценты уплачиваются два раза въ годъ: 18 Іюня/1 Іюля и 19 Декабря/1 Января, по предъявленіи купоновъ, по желанію владѣльца:
въ РОССІИ — въ Конторахъ и Отдѣленіяхъ Государственнаго Банка — рублями;
въ ГЕРМАНІИ — имперскими германскими марками —
   въ Берлинѣ; у гг. Мендельсонъ и Ко.;
      „     „ ; у г. С. Блейхредеръ;
      „     „ ; въ Дирекціи Учетнаго Общества;
      „     „ ; въ Берлинскомъ Торговомъ Обществѣ;
      „     „ ; у гг. Робертъ Варшауеръ и Ко.;
   въ Франкфуртѣ н/М. у гг. Дирекціи Учетн. Общества;
въ ГОЛЛАНДІИ — голландскими гульденами — у гг. Липпманъ, Розенталь и Ко. въ Амстердамѣ;
въ АНГЛІИ — фунтами стерлинговъ — въ Агентствѣ Русскаго для внѣшней торговли Банка въ Лондонѣ.

Облигаціи сего займа погашаются по нарицательной цѣнѣ въ теченіе 39 лѣтъ ежегодными тиражами по плану, на оборотѣ напечатанному. Тиражи будутъ производиться въ Сентябрѣ каждаго года, начиная съ 1902 г. Капиталъ по вышедшимъ въ тиражѣ облигаціямъ уплачивается въ слѣдующій за тиражемъ срокъ уплаты процентовъ. До 19 Декабря 1914/1 Января 1915 года отчисленіе на погашеніе займа не будетъ увеличиваемо сверхъ предусмотрѣнныхъ планомъ погашенія суммъ, а равно до того же срока не будетъ приступлено ни къ выкупу, ни къ конверсіи настоящаго займа.

Уплата капитала по облигаціямъ производится въ тѣхъ же городахъ и въ тѣхъ же валютахъ, какъ и уплата купоновъ, по предъявленіи самой облигаціи съ талономъ и всѣми купонами, срокъ коихъ является послѣ срока уплаты капитала; сумма недостающихъ купоновъ будетъ удержана при выдачѣ капитала по выкупаемымъ облигаціямъ.

Облигаціи сего займа сохраняютъ платежную силу въ теченіе 30 лѣтъ со сроковъ, назначенныхъ для ихъ оплаты, а купоны сихъ облигацій — въ теченіе 10 лѣтъ со срока ихъ оплаты.

Каждая облигація сего займа снабжена купонами и талономъ для полученія новыхъ купоновъ по истеченіи срока старыхъ. Облигаціи сего займа выпускаются именныя и на предъявителя. Правила относительно именныхъ облигацій, ихъ перехода отъ одного лица къ другому, ихъ обмѣна на предъявительскія и обратно утверждаются Министромъ Финансовъ.

Облигаціи сего займа будутъ принимаемы по цѣнамъ, установляемымъ на каждое полугодіе Министромъ Финансовъ и публикуемымъ черезъ Правительствующій Сенатъ, въ залоги: а) по казеннымъ подрядамъ и поставкамъ, б) по разсрочиваемому акцизу и в) по обезпеченію таможенныхъ пошлинъ. Указанныя цѣны будутъ не ниже 90% нарицательной цѣны облигацій.

**TO BEARER**

By virtue of the Supreme Ukase of 1 March 1902, for the realization of the indemnity due to Russia in compensation for the losses suffered in consequence of the disturbances in China, the present 4% loan is issued to a nominal capital of 181,959,000 rubles, equal to 393,000,000 imperial German marks, equal to 231,870,000 Dutch guilders, equal to 19,257,000 pounds sterling, the annual payments on which corresponded exactly to the annual payments of interest and amortization due from the Chinese Government for that portion of the indemnity due to Russia, which China undertook to pay in accordance with the edict of the Emperor of China of 29 May, new style, 1901.

This loan has been entered in the State Debt Book under the designation: "Russian 4% State Loan of 1902," issued for the realization of the indemnity due to Russia from China.

The bonds of this loan are issued both registered and to bearer, in denominations of 500, 1,000, 2,000 and 5,000 imperial German marks, reckoning each 1,000 imperial German marks = 463 rubles = 590 Dutch guilders = 49 pounds sterling.

The holder of this bond is entitled to the sum of 1,000 imperial German marks = 463 rubles, yielding FOUR per cent per annum of income until its redemption by drawing or buy-back; the running of interest begins on 19 December 1901 / 1 January 1902.

These bonds are forever exempt from all Russian taxes.

Interest is paid twice a year: 18 June / 1 July and 19 December / 1 January, upon presentation of the coupons, at the holder's option:
in RUSSIA — at the offices and branches of the State Bank — in rubles;
in GERMANY — in imperial German marks —
   in Berlin, at Messrs. Mendelssohn & Co.;
      "     "  , at Mr. S. Bleichröder;
      "     "  , at the Direction of the Disconto Company (Discount Society);
      "     "  , at the Berlin Trading Company (Handelsgesellschaft);
      "     "  , at Messrs. Robert Warschauer & Co.;
   in Frankfurt am Main, at Messrs. Direction of the Discount Company;
in HOLLAND — in Dutch guilders — at Messrs. Lippmann, Rosenthal & Co. in Amsterdam;
in ENGLAND — in pounds sterling — at the Agency of the Russian Bank for Foreign Trade in London.

The bonds of this loan are redeemed at par over the course of 39 years by annual drawings according to the plan printed on the reverse. The drawings will be held in September of each year, beginning in 1902. The capital of bonds drawn is paid on the interest-payment date following the drawing. Until 19 December 1914 / 1 January 1915 the amount allocated to amortization of the loan will not be increased beyond the sums of redemption provided by the plan, and likewise, up to the same date, neither buy-back nor conversion of the present loan will be undertaken.

Payment of capital on the bonds is made in the same cities and in the same currencies as the payment of coupons, upon presentation of the bond itself with the talon and all coupons whose due date falls after the date of capital payment; the amount of any missing coupons will be withheld upon payment of capital for bonds drawn for redemption.

The bonds of this loan retain their validity for payment for 30 years from the dates set for their payment, and the coupons of these bonds — for 10 years from their due date.

Each bond of this loan is provided with coupons and a talon for obtaining new coupons upon expiry of the old ones. The bonds of this loan are issued both registered and to bearer. The rules concerning registered bonds, their transfer from one person to another, and their exchange into bearer bonds and back are established by the Minister of Finance.

The bonds of this loan will be accepted, at prices fixed for each half-year by the Minister of Finance and published through the Governing Senate, as security: (a) for state contracts and supplies, (b) for excise paid in installments, and (c) for the guarantee of customs duties. The said prices will be not less than 90% of the nominal value of the bonds.

title: Moscow-Kiev-Voronezh Railway Bearer Bond
description: A bearer bond issued by the Society of the Moscow-Kiev-Voronezh Railway, printed at Moscow in 1914, denominated at 187 rubles 50 kopecks and rendered simultaneously as 500 francs, £19 15s 6d sterling, 404 German marks and 239 Dutch guilders. It bears 4.5 percent interest and forms part of a unified issue of 1,330,000 bonds floated in 1914 and guaranteed by the Imperial Russian Government. Its text runs in parallel Russian and French, and it carries a Ministry of Finance seal.

# Bond of the Moscow-Kiev-Voronezh Railway Company (1914, guaranteed by the Imperial Russian Government) — Transcription

## Original:

*(Upper heading, centred)*

**1914 г.**

**Россійскія 4½% желѣзнодорожныя облигаціи, гарантированныя ИМПЕРАТОРСКИМЪ Россійскимъ Правительствомъ.**

Объединенный выпускъ 1914 года, состоящій изъ 1.330.000 облигацій въ 187 руб. 50 коп. (1 р.=¹⁄₁₅ imp.)=500 франк.=19.15.6 фунт. стерл.=404 герм. имп. марк.=239 голл. гульд.

*(Serial number printed at left and right of the title:)* **№0567359** … **№0567359**

**ОБЛИГАЦІЯ**

**ОБЩЕСТВА**

**МОСКОВСКО-КІЕВО-ВОРОНЕЖСКОЙ желѣзной дороги**

въ 187 рублей 50 коп. (1 руб.=¹⁄₁₅ имп.)=500 франк.=19.15.6 фунт. стерл.=404 герм. имп. марк.=239 голл. гульд.

**НА ПРЕДЪЯВИТЕЛЯ,**

приносящая 8 рублей 43¾ коп.=22 франкамъ 50 сант.=17 шиллингамъ 9½ пенс.=18 герм. имп. маркамъ 18 пф.=10 голл. гульденамъ 75¾ цент. въ годъ и входящая въ составъ 1.330.000 облигацій настоящаго выпуска.

*(Left: oval seal bearing the imperial double-headed eagle. Right: circular Ministry of Finance seal inscribed «М.Ф.» with the numeral «1».)*

Выпускъ облигацій сего займа производится на основаніи постановленія Общаго Собранія акціонеровъ Общества 14/27 Іюня 1913 года и контракта о реализаціи займа, утвержденнаго Г. Министромъ Финансовъ 17/30 Января 1914 года. Владѣлецъ сей облигаціи участвуетъ въ 187 руб. 50 коп.=500 франк.=19.15.6 фунт. стерл.=404 герм. имп. марк.=239 голл. гульд. въ займѣ Общества Московско-Кіево-Воронежской желѣзной дороги, выпущенномъ на приводимыхъ ниже условіяхъ.

Настоящія облигаціи приносятъ ежегодный доходъ въ 4½%. Проценты эти уплачиваются предъявителямъ купоновъ ежеполугодно, 2/15 Февраля и 2/15 Августа каждаго года. Погашеніе облигацій производится по нарицательной цѣнѣ, въ теченіе 81 года, путемъ тиражей, въ Ноябрь мѣсяцъ каждаго года, начиная съ Ноября 1917 года. Вышедшія въ тиражъ облигаціи оплачиваются въ срокъ ближайшаго за тиражемъ купона. Начиная съ 1926 года, Общество имѣетъ право увеличить погашеніе или произвести полный или частичный выкупъ займа, съ предвареніемъ облигаціонеровъ за три мѣсяца до срока, назначеннаго для таковаго погашенія.

Уплата процентовъ и капитала тиражныхъ облигацій будетъ производиться по указаннымъ выше паритетамъ и по выбору держателей: въ Россіи—въ кассѣ Правленія Общества Московско-Кіево-Воронежской желѣзной дороги и въ Москвѣ и въ Азовско-Донскомъ Коммерческомъ Банкѣ, Волжско-Камскомъ Коммерческомъ Банкѣ, Петроградскомъ Учетномъ и Ссудномъ Банкѣ, Петроградскомъ Международномъ Коммерческомъ Банкѣ, Русскомъ для Внѣшней Торговли Банкѣ, Русско-Азіатскомъ Банкѣ, Сибирскомъ Торговомъ Банкѣ, Русскомъ Торгово-Промышленномъ Банкѣ, Петроградскомъ Частномъ Коммерческомъ Банкѣ и Московскомъ Купеческомъ Банкѣ; за границей: во Франціи—въ Парижѣ и въ отдѣленіяхъ и агентствахъ нижеслѣдующихъ кредитныхъ учрежденій: Парижско-Нидерландскаго Банка, Національной Учетной Конторы въ Парижѣ, Ліонскаго Кредита, Главнаго Общества для содѣйствія развитію торговли и промышленности во Франціи, Гг. Готтингеръ и К° и Главнаго Общества Промышленнаго и Торговаго Кредита.

Уплата процентовъ и погашенія по настоящей облигаціи обезпечивается доходами и всѣмъ имуществомъ Общества Московско-Кіево-Воронежской желѣзной дороги вслѣдъ за находящимися уже въ обращеніи облигаціями Общества и пользуется преимуществомъ передъ всѣми будущими займами. Независимо отъ сего, облигаціямъ настоящаго займа, со дня ихъ выпуска и въ теченіе всего срока ихъ обращенія, даруется безусловная гарантія Императорскаго Россійскаго Правительства въ уплатѣ процентовъ и погашенія.

Уплата процентовъ по купонамъ и капитала по вышедшимъ въ тиражъ облигаціямъ освобождается навсегда отъ всякихъ русскихъ налоговъ, какъ настоящихъ, такъ и будущихъ. Общество Московско-Кіево-Воронежской желѣзной дороги принимаетъ на себя уплату всѣхъ, какъ нынѣ существующихъ, такъ и могущихъ быть впредь установленными, налоговъ, подлежащихъ взиманію по его облигаціямъ за границею. Въ частности Общество обязуется вносить всѣ фискальные сборы, которые будутъ причитаться за обращеніе его облигацій во Франціи.

Москва, 1914 г.

Obligations réunies 4½% de chemins de fer russes garanties par le Gouvernement IMPÉRIAL de Russie.

**OBLIGATION**

**DE LA COMPAGNIE DU CHEMIN DE FER DE MOSCOU-KIEF-VORONÈGE**

de Rbls 187.50 (1 rbl.=¹⁄₁₅ imp.)=Frs 500=£ 19.15.6=Rmk 404=Fl. P.-B. 239

**AU PORTEUR,**

rapportant 8 roubles 43¾ cop.=22 francs 50 cent.=17 shillings 9½ p.=18 reichsmark 18 pf.=10 florins des Pays-Bas 75¾ c. par an, faisant partie des 1.330.000 obligations de la présente série.

L'émission des obligations de cet emprunt a été autorisée par décision de l'Assemblée Générale des actionnaires de la Compagnie du 14/27 Juin 1913; le contrat relatif à la réalisation de cet emprunt a été approuvé par Monsieur le Ministre des Finances du Gouvernement Impérial de Russie le 17/30 Janvier 1914. Le porteur de la présente obligation participe pour Rbls 187,50=Frs 500=£ 19.15.6=Rmk 404=Fl. P.-B. 239 dans l'emprunt de la Compagnie du chemin de fer de Moscou-Kief-Voronège, émis aux conditions énoncées ci-dessous.

Les présentes obligations sont productives d'intérêt à raison de 4½% l'an. Les intérêts sont payables contre remise des coupons respectifs, semestriellement, les 2/15 Février et 2/15 Août de chaque année. L'amortissement des obligations s'effectue au pair dans le courant de 81 années, par voie de tirages au sort, qui ont lieu en Novembre de chaque année, à partir de Novembre 1917. Les obligations sorties au tirage sont remboursées à l'échéance du premier coupon suivant le tirage respectif. A dater de 1926, la Compagnie a le droit d'augmenter l'amortissement ou même de rembourser en totalité ou en partie le présent emprunt, moyennant un préavis de trois mois.

Le service d'intérêt et d'amortissement s'effectuera suivant les parités indiquées ci-dessus et au choix des porteurs: en Russie—au guichet de la Compagnie du chemin de fer de Moscou-Kief-Voronège à Moscou et aux guichets de: la Banque de Commerce de l'Azof-Don, la Banque de Commerce à Pétrograde, la Banque Russe pour le Commerce Etranger, la Banque Russo-Asiatique, la Banque de Commerce de Volga-Kama, la Banque d'Escompte de Pétrograde, la Banque Internationale de Commerce de Sibérie, la Banque Russe du Commerce et de l'Industrie, la Banque de Commerce Privée de Pétrograde, la Banque des Marchands de Moscou (Koupetchesky); à l'étranger: en France, en Allemagne, en Angleterre, en Belgique, en Hollande et en Suisse—aux guichets des sièges, succursales, agences et filiales des établissements de crédit et maison de banque ci-après: Banque de Paris et des Pays-Bas, Comptoir National d'Escompte de Paris, Crédit Lyonnais, Société Générale pour favoriser le développement du Commerce et de l'Industrie en France, MM. Hottinguer et Cie, Société Générale de Crédit Industriel et Commercial.

Le service d'intérêt et d'amortissement des présentes obligations est garanti par les recettes et par la totalité de l'avoir de la Compagnie du chemin de fer de Moscou-Kief-Voronège à la suite des obligations déjà en circulation, et le droit de priorité sur tous les emprunts futurs. En outre, à partir du jour de leur émission et pendant toute leur durée, est accordée aux dites obligations du présent emprunt la garantie absolue du Gouvernement Impérial de Russie, pour le paiement de l'intérêt et de l'amortissement.

Le paiement des coupons échus et le remboursement des obligations sorties au tirage s'effectueront à tout jamais libres de tous impôts russes, présents ou à venir. La Compagnie du chemin de fer de Moscou-Kief-Voronège prend à sa charge les impôts et taxes présents ou futurs dont ses titres seraient passibles à l'étranger. La Compagnie s'est engagée à maintenir l'abonnement aux taxes fiscales en France pendant toute la durée des obligations.

Moscou, 1914.

The present bonds yield an annual income of 4½%. This interest is paid to the holders of coupons half-yearly, on 2/15 February and 2/15 August of each year. Redemption of the bonds is effected at par, over the course of 81 years, by drawings held in the month of November each year, beginning in November 1917. The payment of interest on coupons and of principal on drawn bonds is forever exempt from all Russian taxes, present and future. The Moscow-Kiev-Voronezh Railway Company takes upon itself the payment of all taxes, whether now existing or that may hereafter be established, chargeable on its bonds abroad. ## English Translation:

**1867**

**IMPERIAL RUSSIAN GOVERNMENT.**

**NIKOLAEVSKY RAILWAY.**

**ISSUE OF 600,000 BONDS,** each **OF ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE RUBLES**, or **FIVE HUNDRED FRANCS, or TWENTY POUNDS STERLING**, or two hundred and thirty-six Dutch guilders;

of which 400,000 bonds are one bond per sheet, Nos. 1—400,000, and 200,000 are five to a sheet, Nos. 400,001—600,000, for a nominal capital of **75,000,000 RUBLES, or 300,000,000 FRANCS, or 12,000,000 POUNDS STERLING, or 141,600,000 DUTCH GUILDERS.**

This issue was authorized by Imperial Ukase of 18 July 1867 (¹).

**FIVE BONDS**
from No. 579536 to No. 579540
**of 625 rubles — 2,500 francs — 100 pounds sterling — 1,180 Dutch guilders.**

These bonds carry the right, until such time as they fall due for redemption by drawing, to an annual income of 4%, that is, one hundred francs, or four pounds sterling, or forty-seven Dutch guilders twenty cents, free of any deduction or duty. This income is paid at the rate of fifty francs, or two pounds sterling, or twenty-three guilders sixty cents, semi-annually, on 19 April / 1 May and 20 October / 1 November of each year.

The bonds are redeemed at their nominal value over the course of 84 years, by drawing carried out annually at St. Petersburg, beginning 20 October / 1 November 1868, in accordance with the redemption table printed on the reverse.

Payment of bonds drawn for redemption, as well as of the semi-annual coupons, will be made:

In Paris: at the Discount Bank (Comptoir d'Escompte) and at Messrs. Hottinguer & Co.
In London, at Messrs. Baring Brothers & Co.
In Amsterdam, at Messrs. Hope & Co.

These bonds are furnished with forty coupons, for collecting the income during the first twenty years, and with a talon. Upon the expiry of these twenty years, if the bonds have not been drawn for redemption, a new coupon sheet shall be issued in due course, upon presentation of the talon, free of any charge, in Paris, London, or Amsterdam, by the above-named banking houses or by the Bank.

Accountant [signature — illegible]     Authorized Representative of the Government [signature — illegible]

*(¹) Bottom notice — text of the Imperial Ukase:*

**To the Minister of Finance.**

Having deemed it necessary, in accordance with your submission examined in the Committee appointed by Us, in order to establish a special monetary fund intended exclusively for the completion of Our railways, to effect a sale, for a term of approximately 85 years, of the Nikolaevsky Railway, and, with a view to facilitating such sale, to issue from the Administration of the said railway bonds, We command you to carry out the issue of these bonds on the following conditions:

1) A total of 600,000 bonds shall be issued, the price of each bond being fixed at 500 francs, 20 pounds sterling, 236 Dutch guilders, or 125 rubles.

2) These bonds shall bear, from 19 April / 1 May 1867, an annual income of 4%, paid semi-annually: on 20 October / 1 November and 19 April / 1 May.

3) The redemption of the bonds at their nominal value shall be effected, beginning 20 October / 1 November 1868, over 84 years, by means of an annual drawing at St. Petersburg, for which purpose a sinking fund shall be established.

4) The subscription for the bonds shall be opened through the banking houses of Baring Brothers & Co. in London, Hope & Co. in Amsterdam, Hottinguer & Co. and the Discount Bank in Paris.

5) The interest and the redemption of the said bonds shall be paid at a fixed rate of exchange, reckoning 500 francs, 20 pounds sterling, 236 Dutch guilders per 125 rubles, in London, Amsterdam, and Paris, at the option of the bondholders. The sums required for payments on the bonds shall be delivered in good time to London to the bankers Baring Brothers & Co., to Amsterdam to Hope & Co., and to Paris to Hottinguer & Co. and to the Discount Bank.

6) These bonds shall be forever exempt from the payment of any duty.

7) In the event of the sale of the Nikolaevsky Railway, the payment of interest and the redemption of these bonds must be imposed upon the company that acquires this line, but this must in no way diminish the obligation of Our State Treasury with respect to the payment of interest and the redemption of these bonds.

On the original, in the Own Hand of HIS IMPERIAL MAJESTY, is written: "ALEXANDER."
Tsarskoye Selo, 18 July 1867.

pages.description: This is a £100 sterling (Soles 500 Peruvian currency) bearer bond of The National Pisco to Yca Railway Company, issued in London on the first day of May 1869 under "The Guaranteed Loan" and carrying interest of 5 per cent per annum payable half-yearly on 1 January and 1 July. It forms part of a total issue of £290,000 / Soles 1,450,000, split between Series A bonds of £20 (S.100) each, numbered 1 to 3,000, and Series B bonds of £100 (S.500) each, numbered 3,001 to 5,300, with capital redeemable in cash on six months' notice or by semi-annual drawings at par. Crucially, the loan is guaranteed unconditionally by the Supreme Government of the Republic of Peru, charged on the surplus from the sales of Peruvian guano. The bond thus belongs to the guano-financed railway boom of the 1860s, when Peru pledged its fertiliser revenues to underwrite British-built lines from the coast inland. Engraved by Nissen, Parker & Arnold of London, the vignette sets the national arms—the vicuña, the cinchona tree, and a cornucopia spilling coins—upon a locomotive flanked by flags, fusing republican emblem with the promise of steam transport.

The verso of a £100 bearer bond of the Guaranteed Loan of the National Pisco to Yca Railway Company, Republic of Peru (recto at goetzmann0689). Two engraved undertakings, each dated London, the first day of May, 1869, occupy the right: the Company, signed J. A. de Lavalle as Director, charges and hypothecates its properties and assets to fulfil the loan's conditions, while the Supreme Government of Peru, through its special agent Manuel Fco. Perola, guarantees the loan unconditionally, binding the Republic to an annuity of £29,300 sterling — covering the 5 per cent interest and a sinking fund to redeem the whole within twenty-five years. At lower right the back cover repeats the issue, denomination (£100), and number 3395. The attached coupon sheet, printed in Spanish, fixes each half-yearly cédula at £2:10s (or S/12½ in Lima, payable at José Canevaro é hijos), the dated coupons running to the forty-ninth semester of 1 July 1893. The sheet documents how a young Andean republic borrowed in London to lay rails from Pisco to Ica, pledging the sovereign's guarantee where the enterprise's own credit could not yet stand alone.

pages.description: This is a bearer first mortgage gold bond (obligation de première hypothèque au porteur) of The Chilian Eastern Central Railway Company, Limited (Compagnie du Chemin de Fer de l'Est Central Chilien), one of an issue of 4,625 five per cent bonds numbered 1 to 4,625, each of $20 or Frs. 503, carrying interest at five per cent and free of British income tax. Created by resolution of the directors dated 21 March 1910 and executed under the company's common seal on the 2nd day of August 1910, the bond was issued by a London-registered company (share capital £240,000 in 240,000 shares of £1) to finance railway construction in Chile. The bilingual French and English text, the gold clause, and the franc-and-dollar denomination reveal a British promoter raising Continental capital for a South American line. The decorative steel-engraved border, with a small vignette of port works, signals security and engineering ambition to prospective bearers.

The reverse of a £20 (twenty pound) bearer bond of The Chilian Eastern Central Railway Company, Limited, a £555,000 issue of Five per Cent. First Mortgage Gold Bonds raised in London in 1910 to build a Chilean line running from Lebu to Los Sauces. The left field prints "The Conditions of Issue," opening with the recital that the bond is one of a series "created by a resolution of the Board of Directors of the Company on the 21st day of March, 1910," secured by first mortgage and resting on a Government guarantee conferred by the railway concession. A redemption schedule tabulates, year by year from 1916 onward, the number of bonds to be drawn, their sterling value, and the balance left outstanding, the mechanism of a sinking fund retiring the debt to maturity. At right, an engraved label in carmine repeats the issuer, "First Mortgage Bond for £20," and "5%," the whole cancelled by hole-punch. The document records how a small Andean railway reached London's capital market under sovereign guarantee, the security on which a remote concession was financed.

pages.description: A 4% bearer bond of 500 dinars issued by the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes "za finansijsko likvidiranje agrarnih odnosa u Bosni i Hercegovini" — for the financial liquidation of agrarian relations in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Signed for the Minister of Finance and the Director of State Debts, it bears the sheet of fifty semi-annual coupons (the talon promising a fresh sheet once the fiftieth is drawn), the last falling due 1 May 1947, which places issue around 1921–1922. The instrument is fiscal machinery for one of the new kingdom's most charged tasks: dismantling the late Ottoman kmet tenancy and indemnifying former landholders, the state borrowing against itself to settle the land. The allegory states this plainly. A diademed sovereign-figure presides over a frieze of double-headed eagles; below sit two peasants — a fez-wearing Muslim before a minaret, an Orthodox Serb before a domed monastery — the confessional halves of Bosnia reconciled in agriculture. The drawing is assured fin-de-siècle academic work; the framing draws on Byzantine-Serbian revival motifs rather than strict Art Nouveau.

The verso of a 4% bearer obligation issued by the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes "za finansisko likvidiranje agrarnih odnosa u Bosni i Hercegovini" — for the financial liquidation of agrarian relations in Bosnia and Herzegovina (recto at goetzmann0693). Printed in Serbian Cyrillic, Croatian, Slovene and French, it sets out the conditions of issue: authorized under Article 21 of the Decree on the agrarian liquidation, the loan comprised 1,300,000 obligations in 26,000 series of fifty, for a nominal 130,000,000 dinars, repayable at par over fifty years. The sheet is a block of five bearer bonds of 100 dinars (500 dinars), its TALON exchangeable for a new coupon sheet after the fiftieth half-yearly coupon. Below, a quadrilingual amortization table ("Tableau d'amortissement") schedules the annual sums drawn by lot. The document records the new South-Slav state assuming the fiscal burden of dismantling Ottoman-era feudal land tenure in its newly incorporated provinces, converting expropriated landlords' claims into long-dated public debt. Belgrade, 18 June 1921.

pages.description: A bearer amortisable bond (Obligation / Обавезница) of the Kingdom of Serbia, denominated 500 Francs = 500 Dinars in gold, equivalent to R.M. 405 and 200 Austrian gold florins, bearing 4 per cent interest payable semi-annually and redeemable at par in gold over seventy-two years. It is one of 710,584 obligations forming a nominal capital of 355,292,000 Francs, created under the law of 8/20 July 1895. The trilingual text in French, Serbian (Cyrillic) and German, with payment places at Belgrade, Paris, Berlin and Vienna, marks this as Serbia's great unification loan, consolidating earlier debts and pledging the net revenues of the state railways together with the tobacco, salt and petroleum monopolies and the customs, all administered by the Autonomous Monopolies Administration. The instrument's appeal to foreign capital rested less on its restrained engraved guilloche border and small royal crown than on this elaborate pledge of revenue, a sovereign borrower binding its fiscal apparatus to reassure the Berlin and Paris markets. Printed in Vienna.

This is the official amortization plan for the Kingdom of Serbia's 4% amortizable loan of 1895, a state bond with a nominal capital of 355,292,000 francs. Printed in three parallel languages — French (Tableau d'Amortissement), Serbian Cyrillic (Амортизациони план), and German (Tilgungs-Plan) — it sets out the schedule of half-yearly redemption payments, falling each 13 January and 13 July (new style), beginning in 1896. The conditions panels explain that service of the loan is secured on the newly reorganized Administration des Monopoles, which independently manages the state's tobacco, salt, and petroleum monopolies together with stamp, spirits, customs, and railway receipts, and which is bound to forward these revenues to designated banking houses. The instrument records Serbia's large 1895 conversion operation, by which scattered earlier obligations — including the lottery loans of 1881 and 1888 — were consolidated and refinanced under foreign-supervised monopoly security. Dated Belgrade, 1/13 August 1895, and signed by government delegates and bank representatives (among them Schröder). The austere ruled tables and unadorned typography present the bond as an exercise in fiscal discipline rather than display.

pages.description: A £100 sterling bearer bond of the Chinese Imperial Government's 4½ per cent Gold Loan of 1898, printed bilingually in English and German and styled as both a "Bond for £100 Sterling" and an "Obligation über £100 Sterling." Interest runs from 1 March 1898 at four and a half per cent, payable each 1 March and 1 September; the principal is repayable by annual drawings beginning January 1899, redeemable in sterling at the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation in London and at the Deutsch-Asiatische Bank in Berlin, which acted as agent for the emission. The bond forms part of a total nominal loan of £16,000,000 sterling, divided among denominations of £25, £50, £100, and £500. Authorised by Imperial Edict of 2 March 1898 and secured upon the revenues of the Imperial Maritime Customs of the Treaty Ports together with a first charge on the likin of certain ports and districts, the issue records how the late Qing state, pressed by indemnity and reform after the war with Japan, raised capital through Anglo-German banking houses and pledged its customs receipts to foreign creditors. The ornate engraved frame, executed at the Reichsdruckerei in Berlin, joins European scrollwork with Chinese motifs and a red seal in seal-script characters, the visual idiom of a loan negotiated between empires.

The reverse of a £100 sterling bond of the Chinese Imperial Government 4½% Gold Loan of 1898 (Littera C), a bilingual sheet whose English and German columns reproduce extracts from the loan agreement ("Extracts" / "Auszug ... aus der Obligation erwähnten Vertrage") and, at right, the Table of Drawings or Amortisations-Plan. Interest fell due half-yearly on 1 March and 1 September. The amortisation schedule begins with the drawing of 1 March 1899, when £115,225 became repayable against an outstanding balance of £15,884,775, figures that fix the total issue at £16,000,000. Floated in 1898 through the Deutsch-Asiatische Bank, the loan belongs to the wave of European-secured Chinese borrowing that followed the indemnity owed to Japan after the war of 1894–95; the gold-denominated, sterling-fixed terms and the prominent redemption table reveal creditors' demand for security and predictable amortisation in lending to a hard-pressed empire. The engraved frame is restrained, its corner ornament conventional rather than emblematic.

This is a horizontal strip of interest coupons detached from a £100 bearer bond of the Chinese Imperial Government 4½% Gold Loan of 1898. Fifteen coupons, numbered 76 through 90 and all keyed to Bond C. No. 076230, each promise £2 5s.—a half-year's interest at 4½ per cent—falling due at successive March and September dates, the printed examples running from 1 March 1936 to 1 March 1943. Each is payable in London at the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation or in Berlin at the Deutsch-Asiatische Bank. The loan, raised to fund the indemnity China owed Japan after the war of 1894–95, bound the empire's revenues to European creditors; the twin London-Berlin paying agents register the Anglo-German banking rivalry over China's finances. Printed in orange on engraved guilloche borders, the coupons are cancelled by hole-punch, marking interest already drawn.

A sheet of detachable interest coupons belonging to a bearer obligation of the Imperial Chinese Government 4½% Gold Loan of 1898 ("Kaiserlich Chinesische Staatsanleihe in Gold von 1898"), denominated in sterling and serviced through German banking channels. Each coupon promises semi-annual interest of £2.5s. — two pounds five shillings, the half-year's yield on a £100 bond at 4½% — payable on fixed dates by draft on London ("Wechsel auf London, zahlbar zum Tagescours") at the Deutsch-Asiatische Bank in Berlin and its houses in London, Hamburg, Frankfurt, Cologne and Shanghai. The surviving coupons run to maturities as late as 1936 and 1943, all cancelled by hole-punch. Issued amid the post-1895 scramble for Chinese loans, the sheet records a Qing borrowing floated on European markets and underwritten by German finance, its sober engraved guilloche borders projecting the creditworthiness such instruments needed to sell abroad.

transcription:
# Government of Honduras Loan — Bearer Obligation of the State Railways, 300 Francs, Paris 1869 — Transcription

## Original:

*(Single sheet. LEFT PANEL carries two engraved bonds — the FRENCH text in the upper half, the SPANISH text in the lower half — each with a large ornamental "300" as the central device. A block of coupons fills the RIGHT PANEL. Printed throughout in blue; the running legal text is set in very light blue and is only partly legible, the numeral/heading strokes and the bold words being the clearest.)*

---

### FRENCH BOND (upper half)

*(Vertical banner along the left edge, wrapped on a scroll:)*

**EMPRUNT DU GOUVERNEMENT DE HONDURAS · 1869**

*(Heading lines, centred to the right of the banner:)*

**OBLIGATION DES CHEMINS DE FER DE L'ÉTAT**

**ÉMISSION DE 207,509 OBLIGATIONS DE 300 FRANCS**

[…] SOIT 12 LIVRES STERLING

*(Large central numeral device, with cursive title overlaid:)*

**300** — *Obligation de 300 Francs au Porteur*

**JOUISSANCE DU 1ᵉʳ MARS 1869.**

*(Body text, in light print and partly obscured by the numerals — legible fragments only; [illegible] marks gaps:)*

[Le porteur a droit à] un intérêt annuel de **20 francs**, payable par semestre, et au remboursement en [illegible ; se termine par « -sept »] années, suivant le tableau ci-contre. [Les] paiements [se feront] en or, à Paris, sans impôt ni déduction [quelconque].

[La présente Obligation est garantie par première] hypothèque sur le chemin de fer [en voie d'exécution, bois] et forêts de l'État, hypothèque [consentie pour …] des deux emprunts de 1867 [et 1869]. [La neutralité de la voie … la France, l'Angleterre] et les États-Unis d'Amérique. Les [produits …] inter-océanique […] les titres de la même émission […] par une Action de jouissance, portant [le même numéro] et donnant [droit …] revenus nets de la ligne pendant une durée [de quinze années après le rem]boursement. […Cortez…] [illegible]

**Paris, le 28 février 1869.**

*(Attestation and signature, right side:)*

**LE MINISTRE DE HONDURAS À P[ARIS],**
Agissant en son nom et en celui de son collègue,
en vertu de leurs pleins pouvoirs.

*(large cursive signature)* — [illegible signature]

---

### SPANISH BOND (lower half)

*(National arms of Honduras at upper left — cornucopias, wreath, the legend "…REPUBLICA DE HONDURAS…" and the date "1821"; the word "…LIBRE" visible. Serial number on a scroll:)*

**Nº 7854**

*(Vertical banner along the left edge:)*

**EMPRÉSTITO DEL GOBIERNO DE HONDURAS · 1869**

*(Heading lines:)*

**OBLIGACIONES DE LOS FERRO CARRILES DEL ESTADO**

**EMISION DE 207,509 OBLIGACIONES DE 300 FRANCOS**

IGUALES Á 60 CUPONES, Ó SEA Á 12 LIBRAS ESTERLINAS

*(Large central numeral device, with cursive title overlaid:)*

**300** — *Obligacion de 300 Francos al Portador*

**GOCE DEL 1º DE MARZO DE 1869.**

*(Body text, light print, legible fragments only:)*

[El portador tiene derecho á] un interés anual de **veinte francos**, pagadero por semestre, y al reembolso [en … años], con arreglo al [cuadro] al margen. [Los] pagos [se harán] en oro, en Paris, sin impuesto ni deduccion [alguna].

[La presente Obligacion está garantida con primera hipoteca sobre] el ferro carril que va eje[cutándose, bosques y montes del Estado], hipoteca otorgada [para …] la amortizacion de los dos [empréstitos de 1867 y 1869 …] la Francia, la Inglaterra [y los Estados-Unidos de América …] especialmente [para] servir integral[mente …] quedarán reemplazados con [una Acción de goce …] en el tercio del producto [… una parte proporcional en el terce]ro [… hasta el reembolso] por completo de este empréstito.

**Paris, á 28 de febrero de 1869.**

*(Attestation and signature:)*

**EL MINISTRO DE HONDURAS,**
Obrando en su propio nombre y en [el de su colega],
en u[so de sus plenos poderes].

*(large cursive signature — same as French)* — [illegible signature]

*(Circular hand-stamp near the arms, largely [illegible]; the name "L. GUY[…]" and a place — apparently MARSEILLE — can be partly made out.)*

---

### COUPON SHEET (right panel)

*(A grid of detachable coupons, printed in blue, each of identical form. Bilingual French/English text; representative coupons read:)*

**GOUVERNEMENT DE HONDURAS**
Intérêt du 1ᵉʳ [Septembre / Mars] 18[..] — Interest due 1st [March / September] 18[..]
**8 sh.**
**EIGHT SHILLINGS**
payable in London

*(Each coupon is stamped with the bond serial, e.g. 7854. Coupons are semi-annual (1st March / 1st September) and each pays 8 shillings; dated examples visible include "1st March 1882" and "1st September 1884". Individual coupon dates otherwise [illegible] at this resolution.)*

---

## English Translation:

**GOVERNMENT OF HONDURAS LOAN, 1869**

**OBLIGATION [BOND] OF THE STATE RAILWAYS**

**ISSUE OF 207,509 OBLIGATIONS OF 300 FRANCS**

[…] equal to 12 pounds sterling

**300** — *Obligation of 300 Francs to Bearer*

**INTEREST RUNNING FROM 1 MARCH 1869.**

[The bearer is entitled to] an annual interest of **20 francs**, payable half-yearly, and to redemption over [illegible; ends in "-seven"] years, in accordance with the table opposite. [The] payments [shall be made] in gold, at Paris, free of any tax or deduction [whatsoever].

[The present Obligation is secured by a first] mortgage on the railway [under construction, the woods] and forests of the State, a mortgage [granted for …] the two loans of 1867 [and 1869]. [The neutrality of the line … France, England] and the United States of America. The [proceeds …] interoceanic […] the bonds of the same issue […] by a "jouissance" (participation) Share, bearing [the same number] and giving [the right to a share in] the net revenues of the line for a period [of fifteen years after re]demption. […Cortez (Puerto Cortés)…] [illegible]

**Paris, 28 February 1869.**

**THE MINISTER OF HONDURAS AT PARIS,**
Acting in his own name and in that of his colleague,
by virtue of their full powers.

*(signature — illegible)*

**Coupon (each):**
**GOVERNMENT OF HONDURAS** — Interest due 1st [March/September] 18[..] — **8 sh. / EIGHT SHILLINGS — payable in London.**

*(The Spanish half of the sheet repeats the same text: "Empréstito del Gobierno de Honduras 1869 — Obligations of the State Railways — Issue of 207,509 Obligations of 300 Francos, equal to 60 coupons, i.e. to 12 pounds sterling — Obligation of 300 Francos to Bearer — Interest running from 1 March 1869 — annual interest of twenty francs, payable half-yearly … in gold, at Paris, free of tax or deduction … secured by a first mortgage on the railway under construction and the forests of the State … France, England and the United States … Paris, 28 February 1869 — The Minister of Honduras." Serial No. 7854.)*

---

*Notes on conflicts with the supplied description / prior transcription:*
- *Denomination is **300 francs** (large numeral, cursive title, and both heading lines all read 300), confirming the verified fact and correcting the earlier garbled "500."*
- *Emission count reads **207,509 obligations of 300 francs** (in both the French and Spanish heading lines). 207,509 × 300 fr = 62,252,700 fr ≈ £2,490,000 at 25 fr/£ — matching the known 1869 Honduras loan — which corroborates the reading. This replaces the earlier fabricated "2,059" / "301,004."*
- *Serial number is **7854** (stamped on the Spanish bond and on the coupons), not the earlier "74444."*
- *Printed **date is 28 February 1869**; the supplied description's "1 February 1869" appears incorrect. Interest/"jouissance" runs from **1 March 1869**.*
- *The clause on guarantees names **France, England AND the United States of America** as guaranteeing the line's neutrality; the description mentions only France and England.*
- *Coupons are engraved **8 shillings** each, semi-annual, "payable in London" (bilingual French/English), consistent with 20 fr annual interest (≈16 sh/yr ⇒ the sheet's "12 livres sterling / 60 coupons" describes the full 300-fr / 30-year run).*

pages.description: This is a bearer obligation of the Government of Honduras for its 1869 State Railway loan (Emprunt du Gouvernement de Honduras 1869 / Obligation des Chemins de Fer de l'État), a 300-franc bond carrying coupons and bearing interest from 1 March 1869. The text appears twice on the sheet, in French above and Spanish below, with the great "300 Francs au Porteur" / "300 Francos al Portador" numerals dominating each half and a block of coupons attached at the right. The bond was issued at Paris and dated 1 February 1869, payable in gold francs free of tax, secured by a mortgage on the State railway, with the loan partly guaranteed by France and England. The obligation belongs to the wave of European-placed railway loans by which a small Central American state sought to finance an interoceanic line, drawing on Paris and London capital it could not raise at home. The restrained engraved frame and the national arms favour the sober probity expected of a sovereign credit instrument rather than ornament for its own sake.

The verso of a bearer bond for the Honduras Government Loan of 1869 (Emprunt du Gouvernement de Honduras / Staats-Anleihe der Regierung von Honduras), a sovereign loan floated at Paris by Victor Herran, the Republic's minister there. The upper portion sets out the loan's conditions in parallel English, French, and German, declaring an emission of 207,509 obligations of 300 francs (£12) on the bearer, dated Paris, 28 February 1869, the proceeds pledged to complete the State Railways; interest is payable 1 March and 1 September, with triennial drawings on 1 February and 1 August. A printed amortization table (Tableau d'Amortissement) schedules redemptions every March and September from 1869 to 1886, summing to the full 207,509 bonds. Backed by railway revenues and citing the neutrality of England and the United States, the issue exemplifies the speculative European lending to small Latin American states that culminated in Honduras's notorious default. Ornament is confined to engraved blue lettering and patterned borders; the cover panels reprise the denomination and terms.

The engrossed text reproduces the enabling decree: the loan was raised expressly to convert Bolivia's debased "feble" silver coinage back into moneda de buena ley, the State bearing the loss. The feble coin was that struck under Mariano Melgarejo, the peso Melgarejo, which circulated well below its face silver content. pages.description: A bearer bond (bono al portador) of the Republic of Bolivia for one thousand pesos fuertes, issued under the Empréstito de 1870 and dated at La Paz de Ayacucho on 1 January 1870, its attached coupon sheet paying eight per cent a year — principal and interest payable in Santiago de Chile, and engraved by the National Bank Note Company of New York. The central vignette is a neoclassical allegory of abundance, a seated figure amid wheat, fruit, and grapes. The engrossed text reproduces the enabling decree: the loan was raised expressly to convert Bolivia's debased ‘feble’ silver coinage back into moneda de buena ley, the State bearing the loss. That debasement was the work of the dictator Mariano Melgarejo, whose ‘pesos Melgarejo’ had discredited the country's money at home and abroad. The bond's ending is its point: when Melgarejo was overthrown and fled in January 1871, the successor government annulled the still-forming Empréstito de 1870 — leaving certificates like this one as the paper of a loan repudiated almost before it began.

This is the verso of a bearer bond of the Republic of Bolivia, issued under the Empréstito de 1870 (the loan of 1870). The left half carries a printed-and-handwritten panel of conditions, headed in cursive Spanish (Condiciones del Empréstito), within an engraved guilloche border in teal ink. The right half preserves an intact sheet of forty detachable interest coupons, arranged four across and ten down, each bearing the legend REPUBLICA DE BOLIVIA, EMPRESTITO DE 1870 and a central value of 40. Bolivia, dated to the 1870 loan. A young Andean republic chronically short of specie, Bolivia turned to the European and New York capital markets to fund its obligations, and the engraving was executed by the Compañía Nacional de Billetes de Banco of New York (the National Bank Note Company), whose dense lathe-work and intricate counters served less as decoration than as a guarantee against forgery for a security meant to circulate abroad among bondholders who would never see the issuer.

title: República Mexicana Consolidated External Debt Gold Bond
description: A bearer bond of the República Mexicana for the five percent Consolidated External Debt loan of 1899. Its face value is stated in parallel across the markets that took the loan: £200 sterling, $970 United States gold dollars, and 4,080 German reichsmark, with capital and interest expressly payable in gold. The bond forms one of 198,000 pieces, in series of £20, £100 and £200, of a total issue of about $22,700,000, raised under contracts of 2 June and 3 July 1899 and serviced in Berlin, Paris, London and Mexico. The loan consolidated and refunded Mexico's older external obligations.
creator: Republica Mexicana / Ministerio de Hacienda
notes: República Mexicana, Bono de la Deuda Consolidada Exterior Mexicana, Serie C, No. 621768. £200 / $970. 3% of 1899. Mexico City, 1899.

# United Mexican States — 5% Consolidated External Debt Gold Bond, 1899 (£200 / $970 U.S. Gold / M. 4,080) — Transcription

## Original (Spanish):

*(This bond is printed in four parallel languages. The upper vignette and headings are in Spanish; the legal body appears in four columns — Spanish (col. 1), German (col. 2), English (col. 3), French (col. 4). The Spanish and headings are given here; the German, English and French bodies follow, and the English column serves as the official translation reproduced below.)*

*(Top margin, small type:)* REPUBLICA MEXICANA

*(Central cartouche, top:)* **M. 4,080 D.R.W.**

*(Upper left and upper right corners, repeated:)* **SÉRIE C** — **Nº 024766**

*(Engraved arch over the eagle vignette:)* **REPÚBLICA MEXICANA**

*(Denomination box, left:)* **£200**  *(Denomination box, right:)* **$970 U.S. GOLD**

**Bono de la Deuda Consolidada Exterior Mexicana**

**DEL 5 P%. DEL — AÑO DE 1899.**

**CAPITAL É INTERESES PAGADEROS EN ORO**

**ESTE BONO PERTENECE Á UNA DE LAS SÉRIES DE 198,000 BONOS DE LA NUMERACIÓN Y VALORES SIGUIENTES:**

*(Series table — columns: series · numbering · pieces · £ value · Mark value (D.R.W.) · U.S. gold $ value)*

- SÉRIE A Nºˢ 000.001 Á 004.000. — 4.000 BONOS DE £ 1.000. Ó M. 20.400. D.R.W. Ó $ ORO E.U. 4.850.
- " B " 004.001 Á 016.000. — 12.000 " " £ 500. Ó M. 10.200. " " Ó $ 2.425.
- " C " 016.001 Á 041.000. — 25.000 " " £ 200. Ó M. 4.080. " " Ó $ 970.
- " D " 041.001 Á 098.000. — 57.000 " " £ 100. Ó M. 2.040. " " Ó $ 485.
- " E " 098.001 Á 198.000. — 100.000 " " £ 20. Ó M. 408. " " Ó $ 97.

**198,000 BONOS REPRESENTANDO UN VALOR TOTAL DE £ 22.700.000. Ó M. 463.080.000. D.R.W. Ó $ ORO E.U. 110.095.000.**

**[Column 1 — Spanish body:]**

Los Estados Unidos Mexicanos reconocen deber por este bono al portador la suma de Lstg 200 ó 4.080 Marcos del Imperio Alemán, al cambio fijo de 20.40 Marcos por libra esterlina, ó 970 pesos americanos oro al cambio fijo de Dollars 4.85 centavos oro E.U. por libra esterlina.

Esta suma forma parte del Empréstito de Lstg 22.700.000 ó 463.080.000 Marcos del Imperio Alemán é 110.095.000 pesos oro de los Estados Unidos del América, emitido de conformidad con la ley del 2 de Junio de 1899 y con el contrato celebrado en Berlín, París y Londres con las casas de S. Bleichroder, Deutsche Bank y Dresdner Bank de Berlín; J. S. Morgan y Cía de Londres, J. P. Morgan y Cía de Nueva York y Banco Nacional de México; contrato que en lo conducente se inserta al respaldo de este bono.

El Tesoro Federal pagará intereses sobre la expresada suma de Lstg 200 ó 4.080 Marcos del Imperio Alemán é Dollars 970 oro E.U. á razón de 5% anual, por trimestres vencidos y la redimirá por compras ó por sorteos á la par con arreglo al artículo 4º del citado contrato.

Todos los pagos tendrán lugar á elección del portador, en Berlín, Londres, Nueva York y en Francfort s/M en la moneda correspondiente y en Amsterdam á otro lugar que las casas de emisión designen, en la moneda de curso al cambio á la vista sobre Berlín.

El capital que este bono representa y los intereses que devengue, estarán siempre exentos de toda clase de contribuciones é impuestos mexicanos existentes ó futuros cualquiera que sea su naturaleza, y están garantizados con la consignación del 62% de las contribuciones sobre la importación y exportación que se recauden en la República como se fija en el artículo 5º del precitado contrato.

**[Column 2 — German body:]**

Die Vereinigten Staaten von Mexico anerkennen durch diese Obligation, dem Inhaber derselben die Summe von £ 200 oder zum festen Course von Mark 20.40 für ein Pfund Sterling 4.080 Mark D.R.W. oder zum festen Course von Doll. 4.85 für ein Pfund Sterling 970 Ver. St. Gold Dollars zu verschulden.

Diese Summe bildet einen Theil der Anleihe von £ 22.700.000 oder 463.080.000 Deutsche Reichsmark oder 110.095.000 Ver. St. Gold Dollars, welche ausgegeben ist in Ausführung des Gesetzes vom 2 Juni 1899 und des Vertrages vom 2 und 3 Juli 1899, der in Berlin, Paris [und] London mit den Bankhäusern S. Bleichröder, Deutsche Bank und Dresdner Bank zu Berlin, J. S. Morgan & Co. zu London, J. P. Morgan & Co. zu New York und der Nationalbank zu Mexico abgeschlossen und auszugsweise anstehend abgedruckt ist.

Das Bundes-Schatzamt verzinst die vorbezeichnete Summe von £ 200 oder 4.080 Deutsche Reichsmark oder 970 Ver. St. Gold Dollars mit 5% jährlich in dreimonatlichen Terminen und amortisirt die Anleihe durch Rückkauf im Markt oder Auslosung zum Nennwerthe nach Massgabe des Artikel 4 vorbezeichneten Vertrages.

Alle Zahlungen finden nach Wahl des Inhabers in Berlin, London, New York und Frankfurt a/M in entsprechender Landeswährung, in Amsterdam und anderen durch die Emissionsbanken zu bezeichnenden Plätzen ebenfalls in Landeswährung, der Betrag der Mark zum Sichtwechselcurse auf Berlin umgerechnet, statt.

Der durch diese Obligation dargestellte Capitalbetrag sowie die daraus erwachsenden Zinsen sind für immer von jeder itzt bestehenden oder zukünftiger mexicanischer Steuer oder Auflage befreit und sind sichergestellt durch die Überweisung von 62% der in der Republik erhobenen Ein- und Ausfuhrzölle, wie dies in Art. 5 des oben bezeichneten Vertrages festgestellt ist.

**[Column 3 — English body (as printed):]**

The United States of Mexico acknowledge themselves by this Bond to be indebted to the Bearer thereof in the sum of Lstg 200 or at the fixed exchange of 20 M. 40 pf per £ sterling 4.080 Marks currency of the German Empire, or at the fixed exchange of Doll. 4.85 U.S. gold Doll. 970 U.S. gold Dollars.

This sum forms part of the Loan of Lstg 22.700.000 or Marks 463.080.000 currency of the German Empire or Doll. 110.095.000 U.S. gold Dollars, issued in pursuance of the law of the 2nd June 1899 and of the Agreement dated 1st, 2nd and 3rd July entered into in Berlin, Paris and London with the Banking firms of S. Bleichroder, Deutsche Bank and Dresdner Bank of Berlin, J. S. Morgan & Co. of London, J. P. Morgan & Co. of New York and the National Bank of Mexico, extracts from which Agreement are printed at the back hereof.

The Treasury of the Federal Government will pay interest on the above named sum of £ 200 or 4.080 Marks currency of the German Empire or Doll. 970 U.S. gold Dollars at the rate of 5 per centum per annum quarterly, and will redeem the same by purchase in the market or by drawings at par, in accordance with Art. 4 of the aforesaid Agreement.

All payments will be made either in Berlin, London, New York or Frankfort on Main, at the option of the holder, in the above stated currencies, and at Amsterdam and other places appointed by the issuing Banks, in their respective currencies, the amount in Marks being calculated at the rate of exchange at sight on Berlin.

The capital represented by this Bond, as well as the interest thereon, are for ever exempt from any Mexican taxes or assessments which may at present exist or may hereafter be imposed, and are secured by the assignment of 62 per cent of the export and import dues levied by the Republic, as stated in Art. 5 of the aforesaid Agreement.

**[Column 4 — French body:]**

Les États-Unis du Mexique reconnaissent par la présente obligation devoir au porteur la somme de Lstg 200 ou au change fixe de 20 m.40 par Lstg 1, 4.080 marks monnaie courante de l'Empire Allemand, ou au change fixe de Doll. 4.85 or É.U. par Lstg 1, 970 dollars américains or.

Cette somme forme partie de l'Emprunt de Lstg 22.700.000 ou Marks 463.080.000 monnaie courante de l'Empire Allemand, Dollars or É.U. 110.095.000, émis en vertu de la loi du 2 Juin 1899 et du contrat passé le 1er et 3 juillet 1899 à Berlin, Paris et Londres avec les maisons de Banque S. Bleichröder, Deutsche Bank & Dresdner Bank de Berlin, J. S. Morgan & Co. de Londres, J. P. Morgan & Co. de New York et la Banque Nationale du Mexique, des extraits duquel se trouvent imprimés au dos de la présente.

Le Trésor du Gouvernement Fédéral paiera les intérêts sur la somme précitée de Lstg 200 ou Marks 4.080 monnaie courante de l'Empire Allemand, ou Dollars or É.U. 970 au taux de 5 pour cent par an, trimestriellement et l'amortira, soit au moyen d'achats en Bourse, soit au moyen d'achats par tirages au pair conformément à l'article 4 du contrat précité. Tous paiements auront lieu à Berlin, Londres, New York, Francfort s/M au choix du porteur et dans les monnaies courantes précitées, et à Amsterdam ou toutes places désignées par les Banques d'émission dans les monnaies courantes de l'endroit, le montant des marks calculé au cours du change à vue sur Berlin.

Le montant du capital représenté par cette obligation, aussi bien que l'intérêt en provenant, sont exempts à tout jamais de toute taxe ou impôt mexicains existants et à venir, de quelque nature qu'ils soient, et sont garantis par l'assignation de 62 pour cent des droits d'importation et exportation perçus par la République, ainsi qu'il est prévu par l'article 5 du susdit contrat.

**[Signature captions, bottom, left to right:]**

EL TESORERO GENERAL DE LA FEDERACION.  —  EL CONTADOR DE LA TESORERIA GENERAL.  —  EL DELEGADO ESPECIAL DE HACIENDA.

*(Three manuscript signatures below the captions; one legible-ish at right ends "C. R[omero?]" — otherwise [illegible].)*

*(Red diagonal overprint stamp across lower-right of the body, mostly [illegible]; fragments legible: "…main office…", "Received", "…10 … Street…", "…thereof and the rights…".)*

*(Ornate green-and-black engraved border; central vignette of the Mexican eagle on a cactus grasping a serpent.)*

**Bond of the Mexican Consolidated External Debt**

**OF 5 PER CENT — YEAR 1899.**

**CAPITAL AND INTEREST PAYABLE IN GOLD**

**THIS BOND BELONGS TO ONE OF THE SERIES OF 198,000 BONDS OF THE FOLLOWING NUMBERING AND VALUES:**
