**[Body of the obligation — the official English text printed on the bond:]**

The United States of Mexico acknowledge themselves by this Bond to be indebted to the Bearer thereof in the sum of £200 sterling, or at the fixed exchange of 20 Marks 40 pfennig per £ sterling, 4,080 Marks currency of the German Empire, or at the fixed exchange of $4.85 U.S. gold, 970 U.S. gold Dollars.

This sum forms part of the Loan of £22,700,000, or 463,080,000 Marks currency of the German Empire, or 110,095,000 U.S. gold Dollars, issued in pursuance of the law of the 2nd of June 1899 and of the Agreement dated the 1st, 2nd and 3rd of July [1899] entered into in Berlin, Paris and London with the banking firms of S. Bleichroder, Deutsche Bank and Dresdner Bank of Berlin, J. S. Morgan & Co. of London, J. P. Morgan & Co. of New York, and the National Bank of Mexico — extracts from which Agreement are printed on the back hereof.

The Treasury of the Federal Government will pay interest on the above-named sum of £200, or 4,080 Marks currency of the German Empire, or 970 U.S. gold Dollars, at the rate of 5 per centum per annum, quarterly in arrears, and will redeem the same by purchase in the market or by drawings at par, in accordance with Article 4 of the aforesaid Agreement.

All payments will be made, at the option of the holder, in Berlin, London, New York or Frankfort-on-Main in the corresponding currency, and at Amsterdam or such other place as the issuing houses shall designate, in the current currency, the amount in Marks being converted at the rate of exchange at sight on Berlin.

The capital represented by this Bond, as well as the interest it earns, shall at all times be exempt from every class of Mexican tax or impost, present or future, of whatever nature, and are secured by the assignment of 62 per cent of the import and export duties collected in the Republic, as fixed in Article 5 of the aforesaid contract.

**[Signature captions:]** The Treasurer General of the Federation. — The Comptroller of the General Treasury. — The Special Delegate of the Treasury (Hacienda).

*(Note: the German, French and Spanish columns are word-for-word equivalents of the English text above.)*

title: Mexico Gold Treasury Bond
description: A bearer treasury bond of the Federal Government of the United Mexican States, styled "6% Oro, 10 Años, de 1913" and dated México, 8 June 1913. This certificate represents the smallest tranche of the Primera Serie "A": a face value of 195 Mexican pesos, rendered in gold and quoted simultaneously as 505 francs, £20, 409 marks, 97 United States dollars and 242 Dutch guilders, paying six percent annually. The whole series comprised 222,358 bonds across three denominations, 4,050 of 1,950 pesos, 10,298 of 975 pesos and 208,010 of 195 pesos, for a total of 58,500,000 pesos.

title: Provisional Bearer Receipt for the Ottoman Unified Converted Debt, Paris
description: A provisional bearer receipt issued by the Conseil de la Dette Publique Répartie de l'Ancien Empire Ottoman, dated Paris, 1 October 1933, delivered against the surrender of one unit obligation of the 4 percent Emprunt Ottoman Dette Convertie Unifiée, nominal 500 francs, or £20, or 22 Turkish pounds. It was issued through the Hamburg branch of the Deutsche Bank und Disconto-Gesellschaft. The receipt rests on the Commission decision of 9 June 1933, taken under Article 49 of the Treaty of Lausanne, which apportioned the nominal capital of the old Ottoman public debt among the empire's successor states. A central table sets out those debtor states, Greece, Bulgaria, Yugoslavia, Albania, Transjordan, the Hejaz, Asir, Yemen and others, with each one's proportion and share of capital.
creator: Conseil de la Dette Publique Repartie de l'Ancien Empire Ottoman
notes: Conseil de la Dette Publique Répartie de l'Ancien Empire Ottoman, Reçu Provisoire au Porteur No. 0,951,240. Emprunt Ottoman Dette Convertie Unifiée 4%. German paying agent: Deutsche Bank und Disconto-Gesellschaft Filiale Hamburg. Coupon sheet attached below with orange cancellation stamps.

# Provisional Bearer Receipt for the 4% Ottoman Unified Converted Debt, Paris, 1933 — Transcription

## Original (French):

**CONSEIL DE LA DETTE PUBLIQUE RÉPARTIE DE L'ANCIEN EMPIRE OTTOMAN**

**RÉCÉPISSÉ PROVISOIRE AU PORTEUR N° 0,951,240**

Délivré contre remise d'une obligation unitaire d'un capital nominal de Frs. 500 ou £ 20 ou Ltqs. 22

**DE L'EMPRUNT OTTOMAN DETTE CONVERTIE UNIFIÉE 4°/o.**

Conformément à la décision en date du 9 Juin 1933 de la Commission pour la répartition du capital nominal de la Dette Publique de l'Ancien Empire Ottoman, créée en vertu de l'Article 49 du Traité de Lausanne, le présent récépissé a été délivré, contre retrait de l'obligation susvisée, par l'entremise de la Banque

**DEUTSCHE BANK UND DISCONTO-GESELLSCHAFT FILIALE HAMBURG**

a) que la quote-part de la Turquie a fait l'objet d'une émission spéciale ; que les quotes-parts de l'Italie (Dodécanèse), de la Palestine, de l'Irak et des États du Levant sous Mandat français n'ont été entièrement amorties ;

Le présent récépissé provisoire est exclusivement émis pour constater les droits des porteurs des titres retirés de la circulation sur les États débiteurs indiqués ci-dessus. Le Conseil de la Dette, détenteur des titres ottomans retirés de la circulation, aura seul qualité pour procéder aux paiements ou autres opérations qui pourront être effectués au moyen du présent récépissé provisoire, en vue de l'application des Accords conclus avec les États pour le règlement de leurs quotes-parts dans la Dette Ottomane. Les coupons n°s 1 à 12 attachés au présent récépissé serviront à constater les dits paiements ou opérations, dont les modalités seront portées, en temps utile, à la connaissance des porteurs, par des avis publiés par le Conseil de la Dette.

title: Société Ottomane du Chemin de Fer de Damas-Hamah Bond, Constantinople
description: A bearer bond of the Société Ottomane du Chemin de Fer de Damas-Hamah et Prolongements, issued at Constantinople and dated 1 February 1910. It carries a face value of 500 francs, or 22 Turkish pounds, and pays 4 percent annual interest, 20 francs or 88 piastres, by half-yearly coupons of 10 francs falling due on 1 March and 1 September, with redemption at par by lot beginning 1 September 1910. title: Ottoman Public Debt Bearer Receipt, Amsterdam
description: A bearer receipt issued by the Conseil de la Dette Publique Répartie de l'Ancien Empire Ottoman, issued at Amsterdam on 22 April 1930 by the Banque de Paris et des Pays-Bas, recording a nominal claim of 2.20 Turkish pounds, equivalent to £2 or 50 French francs. The document does not bear interest; it is exchangeable for a bearer title of the Bons Représentatifs des Annuités Arriérées de la Dette Publique Ottomane, Série A 1928, with holders invited to combine receipts up to 22 Turkish pounds, £20 or 500 francs to claim unitary bonds. It was created under Article IV of the contract of 13 June 1928 between the Turkish Republic and the bondholders, ratified by Turkish law of 1 December 1928. Unredeemed receipts were to lapse to the benefit of the debtor states within one year. It bears a Dutch 20-centime revenue stamp. Printed by Imprimerie Chaix.

## Original:

(Top-right corner, handwritten in blue ink): remb.ᵗ · juillet 1948 / Present

**TITULO ESPECIAL SEM JURO**
**DO**
**FUNDO EXTERNO PORTUGUEZ**
**3.ª SÉRIE**

Emissão de 477:517 obrigações, especiaes sem juro, amortizaveis ao par por sorteio, em 198 semestres conforme a tabella inscripta no verso, quando o forem as obrigações do juro de 3 por cento da 3.ª série, que tiverem os mesmos numeros d'estes titulos especiaes sendo, 387:517 titulos de 1 obrigação n.ºˢ 1 a 387:515, 477:516 e 477:517 e 18:000 titulos de 5 obrigações n.ºˢ 387:516 a 477:515 conforme a Obrigação Geral adeante transcripta e traduzida no verso.

**Titulo de 1 Obrigação**
**N.º 303:486**
**Réis 30$000 — Libras 6-12-8 — Francos 166,67 — Marcos 135,34 — Florins 79,34**

**⁕ OBRIGAÇÃO GERAL ⁕**

Tendo sido auctorizado o Governo Portuguez, pela carta de lei de 14 de maio de 1902, a converter a divida externa, consolidada e amortizavel, em 3 séries de titulos do typo unico de juro de 3 %, amortizaveis em 198 semestres, e devendo, em relação á 3.ª série de 477:517 obrigações destinadas á conversão da divida amortizavel externa de 4 ½ %, ser creadas outras tantas obrigações especiaes, sem juro, amortizaveis ao par, por sorteio, quando o forem as obrigações do juro de 3 % da referida série que tiverem os mesmos numeros d'estes titulos especiaes:

Declaro, em nome do dito Governo, eu, Fernando Mattozo Santos, Ministro e Secretario de Estado dos Negocios da Fazenda e interino dos Estrangeiros, o seguinte, com fundamento na citada lei e no decreto de 9 de agosto ultimo:

A Nação Portugueza constitue-se devedora de 477:517 obrigações, sem vencimento de juro, do capital cada uma de réis 30$000, £.ª 6-12-8, francos 166,67, marcos 135,34, e florins 79,34 amortizaveis ao par, por sorteio, quando o forem as obrigações do juro de 3 % da 3.ª série que tiverem os mesmos numeros d'estes titulos especiaes.

Estas obrigações são consideradas para todos os effeitos titulos de divida publica fundada.

A amortização por sorteio d'estes titulos far-se-ha nos termos acima, a contar do 1.º de janeiro de 1903, e conforme a tabella no verso, sendo os titulos sorteados pagos em Portugal, Amsterdam, Anvers, Berlim, Bruxellas, Francfort, Londres e Paris.

O Capital d'estes titulos especiaes é isento de qualquer imposto ou taxa, tanto no presente como no futuro.

Para occorrer ao encargo da amortização d'estes titulos especiaes, o Governo, até integral pagamento dos mesmos titulos, fará inserir no orçamento annual do Estado as sommas para isso necessarias, applicando especialmente e de preferencia a esses encargos, nos termos do disposto na base II annexa á carta de lei de 14 de maio de 1902, os rendimentos aduaneiros no continente do reino na Europa, exceptuando os dos tabacos e cereaes, conforme os termos seguintes da mesma lei:

1.º Os thesoureiros das alfandegas entregarão todos os dias á Junta do Credito Publico quantia sufficiente para perfazer a tricentesima parte, em ouro, do total necessario para os encargos annuaes (juro e amortização) da divida externa actual que for convertida, nos termos d'esta lei, e para as despesas do serviço da mesma divida;

2.º No caso em que as receitas aduaneiras de um dia sejam inferiores á quantia necessaria, o deficit será preenchido com as receitas do dia ou dias seguintes;

3.º Logo que, no decurso de um semestre, a Junta do Credito Publico tiver recebido quantia igual á metade, em ouro, da necessaria para os encargos annuaes (juro e amortização) da referida divida externa actual que for convertida, nos termos d'esta lei, e para as despesas do respectivo serviço, cessarão n'esse semestre, quaesquer entregas dos thesoureiros das alfandegas á Junta do Credito Publico, recomeçando só no semestre seguinte;

4.º Se, por qualquer circumstancia imprevista, as entregas feitas na Junta do Credito Publico, durante qualquer semestre, não tiverem preenchido a metade da quantia total, em ouro, necessaria para os encargos annuaes da divida de que trata esta lei, o Governo preencherá o deficit pelas mais receitas e rendimentos do Thesouro Portuguez;

5.º A Junta do Credito Publico deverá transferir todos os 15 dias, pelo menos, para os estabelecimentos encarregados do serviço da divida publica portugueza nos paizes estrangeiros, as quantias que tiver em cofre, a fim de que o annuncio do pagamento dos coupons se faça 15 dias antes dos seus respectivos vencimentos, e a amortização dos titulos seja effectuada pontualmente.

Fica, porém, declarado para todos os effeitos que as disposições acima contidas, e de que trata a referida base II, annexa á carta de lei de 14 de maio de 1902, de modo algum affectarão ou poderão prejudicar a autonomia financeira, economica e administrativa da Nação Portugueza.

Os numeros dos titulos que forem amortizados serão publicados pela Junta do Credito Publico na folha official portugueza e em dois jornaes de cada paiz em que os mesmos titulos sejam ou venham a ser cotados.

O presente titulo, que não tem nenhuma vantagem além do seu opportuno reembolso, por não vencer juro, não vae munido de coupons e leva as assignaturas do Ministro e Secretario de Estado dos Negocios da Fazenda, de dois membros da Junta do Credito Publico e de um funccionario superior da Direcção Geral da Contabilidade Publica ou da Direcção Geral da Thesouraria, podendo todas as assignaturas ser de chancella menos uma que será pessoal.

Declaro mais, em nome do Governo Portuguez, que, até integral pagamento dos titulos d'esta série, serão mantidas e vigorarão as disposições dos decretos de 14 de agosto de 1893 e de 8 de outubro de 1900, que regulam a constituição, funcções e attribuições da actual Junta do Credito Publico.

Em fé do que eu, Fernando Mattozo Santos, Ministro e Secretario de Estado dos Negocios da Fazenda e interino dos Estrangeiros, assignei e sellei em Lisboa, aos 27 de dezembro de 1902, a presente Obrigação Geral, que vae tambem assignada pelo Director Geral da Thesouraria. — O Ministro da Fazenda, *Fernando Mattozo Santos* — O Director Geral da Thesouraria, *Luiz Augusto Perestrello de Vasconcellos.*

Está conforme. — Pela Junta do Credito Publico, *Alberto Antonio de Moraes Carvalho.*

Visto, Tribunal de Contas, 31 de dezembro de 1902, *Gualdino Alfredo Lobo de Gouveia Valladares.*

O portador do presente titulo, que não tem nenhuma vantagem além do seu opportuno reembolso, por não vencer juro, é credor de Réis 30$000 — Libras 6-12-8 — Francos 166,67 — Marcos 135,34 — Florins 79,34 em conta da 3.ª série de obrigações de 3 %, emittidas conforme a obrigação geral acima transcripta.

Este titulo, quando amortizado, será pago em ouro nas praças estrangeiras, mencionadas na dita obrigação geral acima.

Lisboa, Junta do Credito Publico, em 31 de dezembro de 1902.

(French fiscal stamp): **FOREIGN STATES FUND · 1 % · FULL TARIFF · PARIS · 18 (11) 1903**

**SPECIAL NON-INTEREST-BEARING BOND**
**OF THE**
**PORTUGUESE EXTERNAL FUND**
**3RD SERIES**

Issue of 477,517 special non-interest-bearing bonds, redeemable at par by lottery, over 198 semesters according to the table printed on the reverse, at such time as the 3-per-cent interest bonds of the 3rd series bearing the same numbers as these special titles are themselves redeemed — comprising 387,517 titles of 1 obligation, Nos. 1 to 387,515, plus 477,516 and 477,517, and 18,000 titles of 5 obligations each, Nos. 387,516 to 477,515, in accordance with the General Obligation transcribed and translated hereafter on the reverse.

**Title of 1 Obligation**
**No. 303,486**
**Réis 30$000 — Pounds 6-12-8 — Francs 166.67 — Marks 135.34 — Florins 79.34**

**⁕ GENERAL OBLIGATION ⁕**

The Portuguese Government having been authorized, by the charter-law of 14 May 1902, to convert the external debt, consolidated and redeemable, into 3 series of titles of the single type bearing 3 % interest, redeemable over 198 semesters; and it being required, with respect to the 3rd series of 477,517 bonds destined for the conversion of the external redeemable debt at 4 ½ %, that an equal number of special bonds be created, without interest, redeemable at par by lottery, at such time as the 3 % interest bonds of the said series bearing the same numbers as these special titles are redeemed:

I declare, in the name of the said Government — I, Fernando Mattozo Santos, Minister and Secretary of State for the Affairs of the Treasury and acting Minister for Foreign Affairs — the following, on the basis of the aforesaid law and of the decree of 9 August last:

The Portuguese Nation constitutes itself debtor of 477,517 bonds, bearing no interest, each of the capital of réis 30$000, £ 6-12-8, francs 166.67, marks 135.34, and florins 79.34, redeemable at par, by lottery, when the 3 % interest bonds of the 3rd series bearing the same numbers as these special titles are redeemed.

These bonds are considered, for all purposes, as titles of the funded public debt.

The redemption of these titles by lottery shall be effected on the terms above, beginning on the 1st of January 1903, and according to the table on the reverse, the drawn titles being paid in Portugal, Amsterdam, Antwerp, Berlin, Brussels, Frankfurt, London, and Paris.

The Capital of these special titles is exempt from any tax or duty, both in the present and in the future.

To meet the charge of the redemption of these special titles, the Government, until full payment of the same titles, shall enter in the annual budget of the State the sums necessary for that purpose, allocating specially and preferentially to those charges, on the terms provided in Base II annexed to the charter-law of 14 May 1902, the customs revenues of the continental territory of the kingdom in Europe, excepting those on tobacco and cereals, according to the following terms of the same law:

1st. The treasurers of the customs-houses shall deliver each day to the Public Credit Board a sum sufficient to make up the three-hundredth part, in gold, of the total needed for the annual charges (interest and redemption) of the present external debt to be converted, on the terms of this law, and for the expenses of the service of the same debt;

2nd. In the event that the customs receipts of one day are less than the required sum, the deficit shall be made up with the receipts of the following day or days;

3rd. As soon as, in the course of a semester, the Public Credit Board has received a sum equal to one half, in gold, of that required for the annual charges (interest and redemption) of the said present external debt to be converted, on the terms of this law, and for the expenses of the respective service, all deliveries by the customs treasurers to the Public Credit Board shall cease for that semester, resuming only in the following semester;

4th. If, by any unforeseen circumstance, the deliveries made to the Public Credit Board during any semester have not made up one half of the total sum, in gold, required for the annual charges of the debt dealt with by this law, the Government shall make up the deficit from the other receipts and revenues of the Portuguese Treasury;

5th. The Public Credit Board shall transfer at least every 15 days, to the establishments charged with the service of the Portuguese public debt in foreign countries, the sums it holds in its coffers, so that the announcement of the payment of the coupons is made 15 days before their respective maturities, and the redemption of the titles is effected punctually.

It is, however, declared for all purposes that the provisions contained above, and dealt with by the said Base II annexed to the charter-law of 14 May 1902, shall in no way affect or be able to prejudice the financial, economic, and administrative autonomy of the Portuguese Nation.

The numbers of the titles that are redeemed shall be published by the Public Credit Board in the Portuguese official gazette and in two newspapers of each country in which the same titles are or come to be quoted.

The present title, which carries no advantage beyond its timely reimbursement, since it bears no interest, is not furnished with coupons and bears the signatures of the Minister and Secretary of State for the Affairs of the Treasury, of two members of the Public Credit Board, and of a senior official of the Directorate-General of Public Accounting or of the Directorate-General of the Treasury, all the signatures being permitted to be by stamp except one which shall be personal.

I declare further, in the name of the Portuguese Government, that, until full payment of the titles of this series, the provisions of the decrees of 14 August 1893 and of 8 October 1900, which govern the constitution, functions, and powers of the present Public Credit Board, shall be maintained and remain in force.

In witness whereof I, Fernando Mattozo Santos, Minister and Secretary of State for the Affairs of the Treasury and acting Minister for Foreign Affairs, have signed and sealed at Lisbon, on the 27th of December 1902, the present General Obligation, which is also signed by the Director-General of the Treasury. — The Minister of Finance, *Fernando Mattozo Santos* — The Director-General of the Treasury, *Luiz Augusto Perestrello de Vasconcellos.*

Certified correct. — For the Public Credit Board, *Alberto Antonio de Moraes Carvalho.*

Seen, Court of Auditors, 31 December 1902, *Gualdino Alfredo Lobo de Gouveia Valladares.*

This title, when redeemed, shall be paid in gold in the foreign markets mentioned in the said general obligation above.

## Original:

**ГОСУДАРСТВЕННЫЙ ВНУТРЕННІЙ 4½% ВЫИГРЫШНЫЙ ЗАЕМЪ 1917 ГОДА,**
выпущенный на основаніи постановленія Временнаго Правительства отъ 11-го Августа 1917 года.

**БИЛЕТЪ**
**ВЪ ДВѢСТИ РУБЛЕЙ НАРИЦАТЕЛЬНЫХЪ**
**НА ПРЕДЪЯВИТЕЛЯ.**

Заемъ сей внесенъ въ Государственную Долговую Книгу подъ названіемъ "Государственный внутренній четырехъ съ половиной процентный выигрышный заемъ 1917 года".

Билеты сего займа выпускаются именные и на предъявителя, достоинствомъ въ 200 рублей нарицательныхъ.

Владѣлецъ настоящаго билета участвуетъ въ займѣ суммою въ 200 рублей, приносящей четыре съ половиной процента въ годъ до полнаго погашенія билета вышедшаго въ тиражъ выигрышемъ.

Доходъ по билетамъ второго разряда уплачивается два раза въ годъ: 16 Іюля и 16 Января по предъявленіи купоновъ въ Конторахъ и Отдѣленіяхъ Государственнаго Банка, Казначействахъ, а равно и въ Государственныхъ Сберегательныхъ Кассахъ.

Теченіе процентовъ по билетамъ настоящаго разряда начинается 16 Января 1918 года.

Тиражи выигрышей, происходящіе публично въ мѣстахъ, назначаемыхъ Министромъ Финансовъ, производятся для настоящаго разряда 16 Іюля и 16 Января каждаго года.

Первый тиражъ выигрышей для второго разряда займа назначается на 16 Іюля 1918 года.

Выплата выигрышей производится въ Конторахъ и Отдѣленіяхъ Государственнаго Банка спустя три мѣсяца послѣ тиража выигрышей, по предъявленіи билетовъ со всѣми купонами, срокъ оплаты коихъ наступаетъ послѣ срока тиража, на которые палъ выигрышъ на предъявляемый билетъ; стоимость недостающихъ купоновъ будетъ удержана изъ суммы выигрыша.

Приносящій означенный заемъ доходъ въ размѣрѣ 4½% въ годъ, а равно уплачиваемые по займу выигрыши, освобождаются навсегда отъ сбора съ доходовъ отъ денежныхъ капиталовъ.

Оплата выигрышей производится въ теченіе 30 лѣтъ со дня, назначеннаго для начала таковой уплаты, а купоновъ — въ теченіе 10 лѣтъ по наступленіи по нимъ сроковъ.

Билеты сего займа принимаются по цѣнамъ, устанавливаемымъ на каждое полугодіе Министромъ Финансовъ и публикуемымъ черезъ Правительствующій Сенатъ, въ залоги: а) по казеннымъ подрядамъ и поставкамъ, б) по обезпеченію таможенныхъ пошлинъ.

## English Translation:

**Second Series.**

*(left)* Series number **15800**
*(right)* Ticket number **32**

**RUSSIAN STATE INTERNAL 4½% LOTTERY LOAN OF THE YEAR 1917,** issued on the authority of the resolution of the Provisional Government of 11 August 1917.

**BOND**
**FOR TWO HUNDRED RUBLES NOMINAL**
**TO BEARER.**

This loan has been entered in the State Debt Register under the name "State Internal four-and-one-half per cent Lottery Loan of the year 1917."

The bonds of this loan are issued both registered and to bearer, in the denomination of 200 nominal rubles.

The holder of the present bond participates in the loan in the sum of 200 rubles, yielding four and one-half per cent per year until the full redemption of the bond drawn for prize.

Income on second-series bonds is paid twice a year: on 16 July and 16 January, upon presentation of the coupons at the Offices and Branches of the State Bank, at the Treasuries, and likewise at the State Savings Banks.

The running of interest on the bonds of the present series begins on 16 January 1918.

The prize drawings, held publicly in places designated by the Minister of Finance, are conducted for the present series on 16 July and 16 January of each year.

The first prize drawing for the second series of the loan is set for 16 July 1918.

Payment of prizes is made at the Offices and Branches of the State Bank three months after the prize drawing, upon presentation of the bonds together with all coupons whose payment date falls after the date of the drawing, on which bond the prize was drawn; the value of any missing coupons will be deducted from the prize sum.

The said loan income at the rate of 4½% per year, as well as the prizes paid on the loan, are forever exempt from the tax on income from monetary capital.

Payment of prizes is made within 30 years from the day appointed for the commencement of such payment, and of coupons — within 10 years from the falling due of their terms.

The bonds of this loan are accepted, at prices established for each half-year by the Minister of Finance and published through the Governing Senate, as security: (a) for state contracts and supplies, and (b) for the guaranteeing of customs duties.

# Transcription of Imperial Russian Three Per Cent Loan 1859 Bond

**IMPERIAL RUSSIAN THREE PER CENT LOAN 1859.**
**ONE HUNDRED POUNDS STERLING**

Inscription in the Great Book of the Public Debt of Russia representing a Capital of **ONE HUNDRED Pounds Sterling**.

Entered the _______ Book _______ folio 1546

The bearer of this Inscription is entitled to an annual Interest of **THREE per CENT**, to be paid half-yearly in London, One Pound ten shillings on the **1st OCTOBER** and **1st NOVEMBER** and One Pound ten shillings on the **1st MAY** and **1st JUNE** by Messrs **J. Thomson, T. Bonar & Co.**, or at the option of the holder in Berlin by **Mr. F. Mart, Magnus in Thalers** at the rate of six and three quarter Thalers per Pound Sterling on the said dates.

Attached to this Inscription are half-yearly dividend warrants up to **18 APRIL 1869**, with a talon. After the expiration of that date new dividend warrants will be delivered in exchange for the talon.

Extract from the Regulations of the **IMPERIAL COMMISSION OF THE SINKING FUND** (Code of Russian laws Tom. XI edit. 1857.)

§. 89. The payment of interminable annuities by the State, as well as in times of war as of peace, without any distinction whatsoever, whether the creditor be of a friendly or of a hostile nation.

§. 90. If a foreigner, proprietor of an Inscription, shall die, the Inscriptions shall pass to his heirs, in the order of succession established by the laws of the country, of which he was a subject.

§. 91. Investments in the irredeemable funded debt, constituting the inviolable property of the depositor are exempt from all imposts whatsoever.

Extract of the **IMPERIAL UKASE** of the **20 March 1859**, addressed to the Minister of Finance.

For the amortization of this Loan a special sinking fund, to be kept separate from the other Loans, will be assigned to begin from the year 1859, which fund will form annually 1½ % of the capital of the Loan. On the closure of this fund, for the purpose of buying in the inscriptions at the exchange of the day. If the holder of an inscription of this Loan should wish to have the same repurchased at any time at such price as he may require, the inscription to the bearer will be then changed into an inscription in the name of the holder, without dividend warrants, and the interest due on such inscriptions will be paid at the **IMPERIAL COMMISSION OF THE SINKING FUND** at **St. Petersburg** every half year, at the period fixed here above.

Countersigned: **THOMSON, BONAR & CO.**
per pro. **F. MART MAGNUS,**
Contractors.

pages.description: This is a bearer bond of one hundred pesos moneda nacional, part of the consolidated internal debt (Deuda Interna Consolidada) of the Province of Buenos Aires, Argentina, issued under provincial Law Nº 4293 of 27 June 1935 and dated at La Plata, 1 July 1935. The title earns 5% annual interest with an additional 1% of cumulative annual amortisation, interest payable quarterly in February, May, August and November against the attached coupons, a near-complete sheet of which survives. Issued amid the fiscal strains of the early 1930s, the bond reflects a province consolidating earlier obligations into a single internal loan placed with domestic holders in national currency rather than borrowing abroad. The engraved frame is conventionally academic: classical allegorical figures flank the provincial arms above the denomination, the restrained ornament projecting the sober creditworthiness such an instrument was meant to convey.

This is a sheet of detachable interest coupons belonging to a registered bond of the Consolidated Internal Debt (Deuda Interna Consolidada, Serie A) of the Province of Buenos Aires, issued in pesos moneda nacional under Article 9 of provincial Law No. 4393, with the public-debt provisions of Articles 50, 59 and 80 of Law No. 4225, and put into circulation by executive emission decrees dated 11 September 1925, 20 November 1926 and 16 December 1926. The reproduced decree texts authorise consolidation issues reaching into the hundreds of millions of pesos. More than a hundred small pink coupons, each bearing an engraved number from 19 onward, fill the sheet; the opening run of lower numbers has already been clipped away, marking interest periods drawn down against the principal. The dense guilloché lathe-work and medallioned frames are the standard anti-forgery engraving of the era's securities, asserting the document's negotiability and the province's pledge of payment. The sheet documents a Buenos Aires province leaning on long-term funded debt to consolidate and refinance its obligations through the central provincial loan office.

# Kingdom of Serbia 4% Amortizable Loan of 1895 — Reverse (Amortization Plan, Security Clause and Coupon Talons) — Transcription

## Original:

*(Layout note: The reverse carries three zones. TOP — a large trilingual redemption/amortization table, printed **inverted (rotated 180°)** relative to the coupons, so that it reads right-way-up when the sheet is turned. CENTRE — a trilingual explanatory/security note (German | Serbian Cyrillic | French, in three parallel columns) with signatures, also printed inverted relative to the coupons. BOTTOM — a grid of detachable coupon "talons," printed right-way-up. Languages present: **German, Serbian (Cyrillic) and French**, matching the trilingual layout throughout. The dual dates such as "1/13" and "8/20" give the Julian [Old Style, "a. St." / "ст. кал."] and Gregorian dates.)*

---

### 1. Amortization table (top of sheet)

Three parallel headings, one per language:

**TILGUNGS-PLAN**
für das Königlich Serbische 4 %ige Anlehen vom Jahre 1895 im Nominalbetrage von 355,292,000 Francs.

**АМОРТИЗАЦИОНИ ПЛАН**
за краљ. Српски 4 %, Зајам од 1895. године у номиналној вредности од 355.292.000 динара.

**TABLEAU D'AMORTISSEMENT**
du Royaume de Serbie de l'emprunt amortissable 4 % de l'année 1895, de Francs 355,292,000 capital nominal.

**Column headers** (repeated across each of the six side-by-side panels, in all three languages):
- German: *Datum (a. St.) der Zahlungen* | *Tilgung*
- Serbian: *Рок наплата* | *Отплата*
- French: *Dates (a. St.) des Payements* | *AMORTISSEMENT*

**Table structure and content:** Each row gives a year, the semi-annual payment dates (trilingual: e.g. *13 Janvier · 1. Јануар · 13. Jänner* and *13 Juillet · 1. Јули · 13. Juli*), and the amount amortized ("Tilgung / Отплата / Amortissement") in francs. The schedule runs year by year from **1896 to 1967**, with the sums drawn rising steadily to extinction. This is a very dense numeric grid; individual cell values are printed small and are **not exhaustively transcribed here** — representative, clearly legible figures follow (numbers not confidently read are marked):

- 1896: 432,000 · 440,000
- 1897: 460,000 · 460,000 [approx.]
- 1898: 480,000 · 480,000 [approx.]
- … *(intervening years — dense numeric grid, [not individually transcribed])* …
- 1958: 5,080,000 · 5,170,000
- 1959: 5,280,000 · [illegible]
- 1963–1965: 6,310,000 · 6,440,000 · 6,560,000 · 6,700,000 · 6,830,000 [approx.]
- 1966: 6,970,000 · 7,100,000
- 1967: 7,250,000 · 7,400,000

Carry-forward subtotal line (each panel foot): **À reporter — За пренос — Fürtrag** Frcs. 13,242,000 [example value; other panels differ, values [not all legible]].

Final totals row: (left column subtotal) 212,652,000 · **Total — Укупно — Summe** Frcs. **355,292,000**.

---

### 2. Trilingual security & redemption note (centre)

**German column:**

Mit der Verwaltung der Sicherheiten, welche für dieses Anlehen bestellt sind, ist eine autonome Monopolverwaltung betraut, welche auf Grund des Gesetzes vom 8./20. Juli 1895 eingesetzt worden ist. Dieselbe verwaltet selbstständig die Monopole und die Einnahmen, welche für dieses Anlehen als Pfand gegeben sind, nämlich: das Tabakmonopol, das Salzmonopol, das Petroleummonopol, sowie auch die übrigen bestehenden Staatsmonopole und die Einnahmen aus dem Stempel- und Getränkegebühren. Ferner sind die Reineinnahmen der Eisenbahnen, die Zolleinnahmen und die Erträgnisse der Obrtsteuer ebenfalls an die Casse der Monopolverwaltung abzuliefern. Zu dem Behufe sind die Direction der Serbischen Staatseisenbahnen, sowie sämmtliche Zollämter Serbiens unwiderruflich angewiesen, ihre ganzen Reineinnahmen jeden Monat, respective jede zehn Tage, unmittelbar an die Monopolverwaltung abzuliefern.

Der Verwaltungsrath der Monopolverwaltung ist gesetzlich verpflichtet, die Reineinnahmen aus dem Tabak- und Petroleummonopolen, eventuell nach Einlösung der Salzbons aus dem Salzmonopol, dann aus dem Stempel- und Getränkegebühren, endlich alle Eingänge aus den Eisenbahnen, dann aus den Zoll- und Obrtgebühren, in erster Reihe und ausschliesslich zur Bezahlung der fälligen Coupons und der verlosten Obligationen dieses Anlehens, wie auch der Coupons der Losenlehen v. J. 1881 und der Treffer dieser Losenlehen v. J. 1881 [und 1888] zu verwenden und an die für den Dienst dieser Anlehen bestimmten Zahlstellen in der Weise abzuliefern, dass letztere spätestens 14 Tage vor jedem Termine in den Besitz des vollen, jeweilig zur Auszahlung der fälligen Coupons und der verlosten Obligationen erforderlichen Betrages gesetzt sein sollen. Demnach dürfen diese Einnahmen und Erträgnisse zu gar keinem anderen Zwecke als für den vorstehenden verwendet werden.

Falls die Einnahmen der Monopolverwaltung für den jährlichen Dienst dieses Anlehens nicht ausreichen sollten, ist die Königlich Serbische Regierung verpflichtet, den eventuellen halbjährigen Fehlbetrag aus anderen Einkünften zu ergänzen.

Der französische Text der Obligation ist massgebend.

Die nicht zur Einlösung gelangten Coupons verjähren 5 Jahre, und die verlosten Obligationen 30 Jahre nach ihrer Fälligkeit.

Belgrad, am 1./13. August 1895.

**Serbian column (Cyrillic):**

Гарантијама датим за овај зајам управља Самостална Монополска Управа, установљена на основу закона од 8/20. Јула 1895. Она управља самостално Монополима и приходима заложеним за овај зајам, т. ј. Монополом Дувана, Соли, Петролеума, као и осталим државним Монополима који постоје и приходима од таксених и крчмарских марака. Даље се имају предавати благајници Монополске управе чист Железнички и Царински приход, као и приход од Обртне [пореза]. Тога ради упућене су неопозиво Дирекције српских државних Железница, као и све српске царинарнице, да све своје чисте приходе сваког месеца, односно сваки десети дан, предају непосредно Монополској Управи.

Управни одбор Монополске управе законом је обавезан, да све чисте приходе Дуванског и Петролеумског Монопола, и по исплати Соних Обвезница, [приходе] Соленог Монопола, даље од таксених и крчмарских Марака и напослетку све Железничке и Царинске приходе, као и приход од Обртне [пореза], употребљава [првенствено] и искључиво на исплату купона и извучених Обвезница од овог зајма, као и на исплату купона лутријског зајма од 1881 године и згодитака из истог зајма и Дуванских лозова од 1888 године, и да их за службу овог зајма одређеним исплатним местима предаје тако, да ови буду 14 дана пре сваког одређеног рока потпуно поседовали целокупну потребну своту за исплату купона и извучених Обвезница потребиту.

Ако приходи Монополске Управе не би били довољни за годишњу службу овога зајма, обавезна је краљевска српска влада, да [могући] полугодишњи недостатак другим приходима попуни.

Француски текст на Обвезницама меродаван је.

На исплату неподнесени купони застаревају после пет, а извучене Обвезнице после тридесет година, од дана њихова рока плаћања.

Београд, 1/13. Августа 1895.

**French column:**

*(The visible French text begins mid-sentence at the words below; the opening clause — supplied in the German and Serbian columns, "an autonomous Monopoly Administration set up under the law of…" — is not legibly printed above this first line.)*

… [du] 8/20 Juillet 1895. Elle administre en toute indépendance les monopoles et les recettes qui ont été données en gage à cet emprunt, savoir: le monopole des tabacs, le monopole du sel, le monopole du pétrole, de même que les autres monopoles d'État existants et les recettes du timbre et des taxes sur les boissons. De plus, les recettes nettes des chemins de fer, les recettes des douanes et le produit de l'Octroi devront être également versés à la caisse de l'Administration des monopoles. A cet effet, la Direction de chemin de fer de l'État et celles des douanes ont reçu l'ordre irrévocable de verser, la première chaque mois, les autres tous les dix jours leurs recettes nettes directement à l'Administration des Monopoles.

Le Conseil de l'Administration des monopoles est obligé par la loi à employer les recettes nettes des monopoles du tabac et du pétrole, du monopole du sel après le remboursement des bons de sel, le produit du timbre et des taxes sur les boissons, enfin les recettes nettes des chemins de fer, des douanes et de l'Octroi, en premier lieu et exclusivement au paiement des coupons échus et des obligations sorties de cet emprunt, ainsi qu'au paiement des coupons de l'emprunt à lots de 1881 et des titres sortis au tirage des emprunts à lots de 1881 et de 1888. Il est également obligé par la loi à faire parvenir les recettes précitées aux établissements ou maisons de banque désignés pour le service de ces emprunts de telle façon que les dits établissements ou maisons de banque soient en possession 15 jours au plus tard avant chaque échéance de la somme entière nécessaire au paiement des coupons et des obligations sorties. En conséquence, les recettes et revenus précités ne peuvent recevoir aucune affectation autre que celles ci-dessus mentionnées.

Dans le cas où les recettes de l'Administration des monopoles ne seraient pas suffisantes pour assurer le service annuel de cet emprunt, le Gouvernement Royal Serbe est tenu de parfaire, au moyen d'autres ressources, la somme qui pourrait éventuellement manquer pour un semestre.

The securities pledged for this loan are administered by an autonomous Monopoly Administration, established under the law of 8/20 July 1895. It independently manages the monopolies and revenues given as security for this loan, namely: the tobacco monopoly, the salt monopoly, the petroleum monopoly, and the other existing State monopolies, together with the revenues from stamp duties and beverage (excise) duties. To that end the Directorate of the Serbian State Railways and all Serbian customs offices are irrevocably instructed to deliver their entire net receipts — the railways each month, the others every ten days — directly to the Monopoly Administration.

The Administrative Council of the Monopoly Administration is legally bound to apply the net receipts of the tobacco and petroleum monopolies, then (after redemption of the salt bonds) those of the salt monopoly, then the stamp and beverage duties, and finally all receipts of the railways, customs and trades tax, first and exclusively to the payment of the matured coupons and drawn bonds of this loan, as well as to the payment of the coupons of the 1881 lottery loan and the prizes drawn on the lottery loans of 1881 and 1888. It must forward those receipts to the paying agents (banks) appointed for the service of these loans in such a way that the agents hold, at the latest 15 days before each due date, the full sum required to pay the coupons and drawn bonds. Consequently these receipts and revenues may not be applied to any purpose other than those stated above.

Should the receipts of the Monopoly Administration not suffice for the annual service of this loan, the Royal Serbian Government is bound to make up any half-yearly shortfall from other resources.

pages.description: This is a 500-franc bearer obligation of the Bulgarian 5% State Gold Loan of 1902 (Български 5% държавенъ заемъ въ злато отъ 1902 година / Emprunt de l'État Bulgare 5% Or 1902), one of 212,000 bonds in a loan of 106,000,000 gold levs—stated at par against francs, roubles, German marks, sterling, Austrian crowns and Dutch florins, the principality's metallic lev being pegged to the franc. The bond declares itself a direct obligation of the State, secured on the tobacco duty. It rests on a law sanctioned by decree of 3/16 June 1902 and a contract of 7/20 June 1902 with the Banque d'État de Russie in Paris and the Banque de Paris et des Pays-Bas. Issued at Sofia and printed in French, Bulgarian, German and English, the bond shows young Bulgaria, barely a generation from Ottoman suzerainty, borrowing on the Paris market through Franco-Russian houses, its credit anchored to the predictable revenue of a state tobacco monopoly. The crowned lion arms and disciplined neoclassical guilloche frame project the sober solvency such a placement required.

This interior leaf sets out the conditions and amortization schedule of the Principality of Bulgaria's five-per-cent loan, printed across parallel columns in Bulgarian (Условия на Заема), French, Russian, German and English. Each obligation bears interest at 5% on its nominal value, the half-yearly coupon payable as 12.50 gold leva, the equivalent of 12.50 gold francs, and quoted also in roubles, reichsmark, sterling, Austrian crowns and florins—a gold-standard instrument floated simultaneously on the Paris, St Petersburg, Berlin, London, Vienna, Amsterdam and Brussels markets through the Banque de Paris et des Pays-Bas. Redemption proceeds at par over fifty years by semi-annual drawings held at Sofia, the printed table opening in 1903. Issued as Bulgaria, newly autonomous, borrowed abroad to fund its young state, the document's sober, rule-bound typography—dense conditions framed by a restrained engraved border—mirrors the contractual sobriety expected by Western European creditors.

This is the talon — the coupon-renewal stub — of a bond of the Bulgarian 5% State Gold Loan of 1902, obligation No. 008,761. Printed in Bulgarian and French within a chain-link border of pale red guilloche, the cartouche names the issuer, "ЦАРСТВО БЪЛГАРИЯ / ROYAUME DE BULGARIE," and states that the loan bears five per cent in gold and is secured by a pledge on the tobacco duties ("gagé sur les droits des tabacs"). Surrendering the talon to the Ministry of Finance entitled the bearer to a fresh sheet of coupons — the device by which a long-dated bond kept paying interest once its original coupons were spent. The text sets redemption over fifty years by semi-annual drawings, the first on 1/14 August 1903. Earmarking a particular consumption tax to service a foreign-placed gold loan reflects how a small Balkan state borrowed on Western European markets, where pledged revenues reassured creditors. The sober frame, free of allegory, presents the bond as a plain undertaking.

This is the talon, or coupon-renewal slip, belonging to a bond of the Bulgarian Kingdom's 5% Gold Loan of 1902, secured on the revenues of the tobacco duties. Printed in parallel columns of Russian, German, and English (Болгарское Царство / Königreich Bulgarien / Bulgarian Kingdom), the talon promises that upon its surrender the Ministry of Finance shall in due time deliver to the bondholder a fresh sheet of interest coupons. The device speaks to the long maturity of such gold loans: once the original coupon sheet was exhausted, the talon entitled the holder to its successor. The trilingual setting marks the issue as one floated abroad for international subscription, the young principality pledging a state monopoly's income to reassure foreign creditors. The frame is a restrained typographic border, free of allegory, the sober dress of public credit rather than ornament.

pages.description: A bearer lottery bond (bon à lot au porteur) of sixty francs, issued for the Exposition Coloniale Internationale held at Paris in 1931 and placed through the Crédit Foncier de France under authority of the law of 22 July 1927. The emission ran to 2,300,000 bonds, divided into 100 series of 23,000 numbers each. Tax-free to its holder, the bond entitled the bearer to twenty entry tickets to the Exposition worth three francs apiece, to assorted travel privileges, and to participation in twelve drawings of 2,136 prizes totalling 24,264,000 francs. The bond reveals the French state's habit of financing prestige ventures by harnessing the public appetite for a flutter rather than by direct taxation: the colonial fair is sold to small savers as both spectacle and speculation. The design speaks to this purpose, framing the figures in palms, a distant minaret, and railway, maritime, and aviation coupons that promise passage to the empire on display.

The reverse of a French lottery bond (bon à lots) issued to finance the Exposition Coloniale Internationale held in Paris, authorised under the law of 22 July 1927 and managed by the Crédit Foncier de France, denominated in francs. A ruled Tableau des Tirages et des Lots sets out the redemption lottery: twelve drawings spread across 1929, 1930 and 1931, each distributing 178 prizes worth 2,022,000 francs, for an aggregate of 2,136 lots totalling 24,264,000 francs, with a single top prize of 1,000,000 francs per draw descending to lots of 250 francs. A subjoined extract of the convention enumerates the bond's non-monetary privileges: twenty admission tickets to the exposition and graduated reductions on railway, maritime and aviation fares, followed by a list of the shipping companies honouring them. The structure shows how a state-sponsored colonial showcase was capitalised through the public's appetite for chance, the prospect of a fortune underwriting an imperial spectacle. The plain ruled tabular layout is utilitarian rather than ornamental, prizing legibility of terms over decoration.

pages.description: This is a 3% bearer obligation of 125 silver-metallic rubles issued by the Grand Russian Railway Company (Главное Общество Россійскихъ Желѣзныхъ Дорогъ), the joint-stock concern chartered under an imperially confirmed statute of 3 November 1861 to build the empire's first trunk lines. The bond belongs to the Third Emission (Третій выпускъ облигацій) of 105,176 obligations, together amounting to 13,147,000 silver rubles, and offers convertible equivalents of 500 francs, 20 pounds sterling, 402 German marks, or 236 Dutch guilders — a denominational fan that announces the issue's purpose: to draw western European capital into Russian railway finance. Signed at St. Petersburg and dated 4 January 1881, it reflects the still-unfinished work of integrating the empire by rail two decades after emancipation. The teal frame crowds an imperial double-headed eagle among allegorical figures and a viaduct, binding sovereign authority to the promise of industry and transit.

The conditions side of a bond of the Grand Russian Railway Company (Grande Société des Chemins de fer Russes / Grosse Russische Eisenbahn-Gesellschaft), one obligation of its Third Emission with a face value of 125 silver rubles in metal, rendered equivalent to 500 francs, 20 pounds sterling, 402 Reichsmark and 236 Dutch guilders. It carries annual interest of 3 rubles 75 kopecks, a 3 percent coupon payable half-yearly, and is to be amortised at par over seventy years by annual drawings from 1881. Dated St. Petersburg, 23 December 1880 / 4 January 1881, the issue rests on statutes confirmed in 1861 and a sovereign decree of 19 December 1880 authorising 13,147,000 rubles in 105,176 obligations. Printed in French, German and English with a paired conversion table, the document shows how the imperial railway financed track-doubling and rolling stock by courting bourses in Paris, Berlin, London, Amsterdam and Brussels at once.

This is the coupon sheet attached to a 3% bond of the Grand Russian Railway Company (Главное Общество Российскихъ Желѣзныхъ Дорогъ), third emission of 1893. The heading and the terminal talon fix the bond's face value at 187 roubles 50 kopecks, expressed in parallel as 500 francs, £20 sterling, 236 Dutch guilders and 402 German marks (1 rouble = ¼ imperial). The page is a printed grid of numbered semi-annual interest coupons, one of which announces the "100th coupon," indicating a long redemption horizon. The multilingual valuation is the telling detail: a Russian railway financed through the Paris, London, Amsterdam and Berlin markets, its debt deliberately denominated so foreign rentiers could clip coupons in their own money. The restrained green lithography, ruled into a ledger-like matrix, subordinates ornament to fiduciary clarity, the document presenting itself as an instrument of account rather than display.

This is the coupon sheet, with attached renewal talon, for a 3% bond of the Grande Société des Chemins de Fer Russes (Grand Russian Railway Company), Third Issue of 1881. Printed in green in parallel French and English columns, it carries the bond's value across the era's principal financial centres: 187 roubles 50 copecks (one rouble reckoned at one-fifteenth of an imperial), equal to 500 francs, 20 pounds sterling, 236 Dutch florins, and 402 reichsmark. The grid holds semi-annual interest coupons, here running into the late 1920s, while the talon entitles the holder to a fresh sheet from the Imperial Commission of the Sinking-Fund. The multi-currency face reflects how Russia financed its railways through the bourses of Paris, London, Amsterdam, and Berlin, the long-dated coupons binding foreign capital to the empire's rail expansion. The sheet is utilitarian, its only ornament the ruled coupon table.

pages.description: A government redeemable stock certificate for £1,000 sterling bearing interest at 3½ per cent per annum, issued by the Province of Nova Scotia within the Dominion of Canada and dated 19 October 1904. The stock is transferable and payable through the National Provincial Bank of England, Limited, at 112 Bishopsgate Street in the City of London, and is redeemable at par there on 1 July 1954, the government reserving the option to redeem at par at any time on twelve months' notice advertised in the London Gazette and The Times. A clause invoking 40 and 41 Vict., Ch. 59, Sec. 19 confines liability to the province and its consolidated fund, expressly excluding His Majesty's Treasury. Raised in London rather than at home, the issue shows a colonial government tapping the deep imperial capital market on sterling terms. The engraved frame, provincial arms, and emphatic blackletter heading project metropolitan creditworthiness for a distant borrower.

A sheet of detachable interest coupons for the Province of Nova Scotia Government 3½% Redeemable Stock, part of the Dominion of Canada's sterling-denominated borrowing on the London market. Each coupon represents one half-year's dividend of seventeen pounds ten shillings (£17.10.0), less income tax, on a £1,000 certificate — the semi-annual half of the 3½% rate — payable at the National Provincial Bank of England, 112 Bishopsgate Street, London. The coupons fall due successively on 1 January and 1 July; those surviving on this sheet (the second of four) run through the early-to-mid 1920s. Signed by the Provincial Secretary, G. H. Murray, the coupons bear a small heraldic device and a statutory caveat that the revenues of the Province alone are liable for the stock (40 & 41 Vict., ch. 59, sec. 19). The restrained engraved borders and sober typography befit a colonial government raising long-term capital in the imperial money market.

This sheet forms the conditions-and-coupon portion of a Province of Nova Scotia Government Redeemable Stock certificate, a sterling loan of one thousand pounds bearing interest at three and one-half per cent per annum. The detachable coupons each promise a half-yearly dividend of seventeen pounds ten shillings, less income tax, due 1 January and 1 July, payable in London at the Bank of England, Limited, and countersigned for the National Provincial Bank as registrar. The reverse conditions state pointedly that the revenues of the Province of Nova Scotia alone answer for the stock and its dividends, the Consolidated Fund of the United Kingdom and His Majesty's Treasury being expressly not liable, citing the statute 40 & 41 Vict. Floated on the London market, it shows a colonial government borrowing in imperial sterling on its own credit. The dense engine-turned border in red ochre, framing a thistle vignette, signals security against forgery rather than any artistic programme.

These are the binding-spine stubs (counterfoils) of registered certificates for the Province of Nova Scotia Government Redeemable Stock, an inscribed colonial loan bearing interest at 3½ per cent per annum on a principal of £1,000 sterling. The two engraved stub labels are headed "Dominion of Canada — Province of Nova Scotia — Government Redeemable Stock," with principal repayable and coupons payable half-yearly, the first instalment falling due 1st January. Issued in London around 1910 under Imperial colonial-stock arrangements, the loan let a Canadian province borrow on the sterling market at rates far below colonial terms. The recurring legend on the lower coupon panels disclaims any Imperial guarantee: the revenues of Nova Scotia alone answer for the stock, while the Consolidated Fund of the United Kingdom and the Lords Commissioners of His Majesty's Treasury are "not directly or indirectly liable." The restrained foliate engraving in terracotta ink serves trust rather than display.

pages.description: An ordinary bearer share (action ordinaire au porteur), fully paid, for a face value of 500 French francs, issued by the Banque Industrielle de Chine (中法實業銀行, the Sino-French Industrial Bank), a société anonyme with a capital of 150,000,000 francs and its registered office in Paris. The text records statutes deposited before notaries Lavoignat and Moyne on 15 March 1913 and amended by shareholders' general assemblies of 19 May 1919, 28 November 1919, and 7 May 1920; the share therefore dates from about 1920, in the bank's last and most strained phase before its suspension of payments in 1921. The certificate speaks to the ambitions of Franco-Chinese finance on the eve of collapse: founded to channel European capital into Chinese railways, ports, and industry, the bank had over-extended, and shares such as this funded a venture soon ruined. The engraved frame turns that ambition into ornament — a Chinese gateway, paired guardian lions, and a pagoda-studded skyline in ochre and grey present China as a picturesque field for investment, a decorative orientalism characteristic of European concession finance.

The reverse of an ordinary share in the Banque Industrielle de Chine (中法實業銀行), a Paris-domiciled joint-stock bank denominated in francs. The upper panel reproduces the "Extraits des Statuts": Article 3 defines the object as all banking and finance operations "en tous pays," and especially the carrying-out of agreements concluded with the Government of the Chinese Republic; Article 4 fixes the head office at Paris; Article 5 sets a duration of ninety years; Article 6 places the share capital at 150 million francs. Below, a sheet of detachable dividend-coupon stubs is printed only with the bank's name and the words 息票 ("dividend coupon"). Established in 1913, the bank was a vehicle of Franco-Chinese financial diplomacy, channelling French capital toward concessions and public works in republican China; the bilingual statutes and Chinese coupons register that hybrid ambition before the bank's collapse in 1921.

pages.description: This is a 3½ % bearer bond (obligation au porteur) for £20 sterling, equal to 504 French francs, issued by the Compagnie des Chemins de Fer Économiques de l'Est Égyptien, Société Anonyme, with its registered office in Cairo. Interest of £0.14.0 (17.64 francs) is payable yearly in gold, half on 1 January and half on 1 July, redeemable by annual drawings within a maximum of seventy years, with coupons honoured in gold at Cairo, Alexandria, Paris, London, Amsterdam, Brussels and Geneva. Dated Cairo, 1 July 1897, and signed by two directors. The bilingual French and English text, gold-clause interest and seven European and Egyptian paying centres locate the issue within the foreign-financed railway building that knit Khedival Egypt into the capital markets of London and Paris. The dense blue guilloche border and ornate engraved lettering follow the protective convention of the period's securities, intended as much to deter forgery as to dignify the obligation.

The reverse of a 3½% bond issued in pounds sterling by the Compagnie des Chemins de Fer Économiques de l'Est Égyptien, presenting under twin headings "Garantie" and "Guarantees," in French and English, the security underpinning the loan. The conditions describe the concession: the construction and working of narrow-gauge agricultural railways, electric or steam, in the Egyptian provinces of Charkieh, Dakahlieh, and Kalioubieh, some 350 kilometres in extent. Under article 5 of the concession act of 21 May 1896, the Egyptian Government guarantees a net annual receipt of £36 sterling per kilometre, making good any shortfall. Below, a sinking-fund table ("Tableau d'Amortissement") schedules redemption from 1 January 1900 through 1960. The text speaks to the financing of light railways serving the Delta's cotton lands, where a sovereign guarantee was the instrument that drew European capital into Egyptian infrastructure.

This is a sheet of attached interest coupons from a bond (obligation no. 10592) of the Compagnie des Chemins de Fer Économiques de l'Est Égyptien, the company chartered to build and work light railway lines in the eastern Egyptian delta. The eleven coupons here, numbered 110 to 120, each entitle the bearer to eight francs and eighty-two centimes (8.82 fr.), payable on the first of January and the first of July in successive half-years; the dates run from 1 January 1953 (no. 111) through 1 July 1957 (no. 120). Each coupon may be presented at Cairo, Alexandria, Paris, London, Amsterdam, Brussels, or Geneva, the breadth of paying agents marking the international syndicate that financed Egyptian railway construction in francs. The printed terms beside the coupons set out the concession's working by sections of twenty-five kilometres. The plain guilloche frames and engraved lettering announce a fiduciary instrument whose value lay in its promise, not its ornament.

This is the final sheet of interest coupons detached from a bond of the Compagnie des Chemins de Fer Économiques de l'Est Égyptien (Company of Economic Railways of Eastern Egypt). Printed in French and English, the sheet ranges twelve identical coupons in a grid, each redeemable for £0.7.0 — seven shillings sterling — and each "Payable" on the first of January or the first of July across the years 1952 to 1958, the company's semi-annual dividend cycle. Payment is offered at a cosmopolitan roster of agencies — Cairo, Alexandria, Paris, London, Amsterdam, Brussels, and Geneva — mapping the European capital that financed Egyptian railway building and the international market in which the loan circulated. The remnant of the parent certificate, visible at the right edge with its company seal, anchors these coupons to the underlying obligation. As the last of several sheets, the document records the long tail of a fixed-income security maturing in the mid-twentieth century.

title: Esterhazy Central Casse Partial Bond
description: A partial bond of 1847 for twenty gulden in Conventions-Münze on the 20-florin standard, issued by the central treasury of Count Casimir Esterházy von Galántha, an imperial chamberlain and proprietor of lordships in Hungary and Carinthia. The certificate represents one of 50,000 equal partial obligations into which a one-million-gulden loan was divided, bearing five percent interest and redeemed by lottery drawings over forty years beginning in 1848. The underlying principal deed is dated Vienna, 6 November 1847, and a treasury stamp records 15 December 1847. The loan was placed through the Vienna wholesale house Hammer & Karis and secured on the count's Carinthian estates, among them the lordship of Tarvis with its forest districts.

The loan was placed through the Vienna wholesale house Hammer & Karis and secured on the count's Carinthian estates, among them the lordship of Tarvis with its forest districts. A magnate borrowing against landed property here taps the public credit market through a banking house rather than private lenders, the engraved comital arms with griffin supporters and coronet lending aristocratic assurance to a paper obligation.

The reverse of a partial debenture (Partial-Schuldverschreibung) issued by the Gräflich Casimir Esterházy'sche Central-Casse, the central treasury of the comital estate of Count Casimir Esterházy, for a sum of 20 Gulden Conventionsmünze. It belongs to a loan of 1,000,000 florins C.M. raised in 50,000 such 20-florin debentures, secured on the count's domains. The page sets out the Rückzahlungs-Plan, a table of dated drawings by which the bonds were progressively redeemed, followed by the printed conditions, which enumerate the pledged estates and forests and bind the central treasury to repay. Dated Vienna, 15 December 1847, it bears the engraved Esterházy arms, the manuscript signature of Count Casimir Esterházy, and a countersignature. Such estate-backed amortizing loans let a great landed house tap public credit on the security of its lands rather than through a bank, on the eve of the 1848 upheavals.

pages.description: A state loan bond with a face value of one hundred rubles (Облигация на сумму Сто Рублей), issued under the Third State Loan for the Reconstruction and Development of the National Economy of the USSR (Третий Государственный Заём Восстановления и Развития Народного Хозяйства СССР) and dated 1948. The bond belongs to the cycle of mass subscription loans by which the Soviet state, in the wake of wartime devastation, drew savings from the population to finance the recovery of industry and agriculture under the Fourth Five-Year Plan; such loans were promoted as patriotic duty and largely deducted from wages. The engraved frame is unambiguously didactic: the state emblem with hammer, sickle, and wheat crowns a panorama of a factory, a hydroelectric dam, and combine harvesters working a grain field, fusing heavy industry and mechanized agriculture into a single image of planned reconstruction.

This sheet sets out the conditions (Условия) of the Third State Loan for the Restoration and Development of the National Economy of the USSR (Третий Государственный Заём Восстановления и Развития Народного Хозяйства СССР), a lottery bond issued by the Soviet state and dated 1 October 1948 with a twenty-year term to 1 October 1968. The dense Russian text fixes the loan's terms: bonds of 100 and 200 rubles, each made up of two coupons; servicing not by fixed interest but by periodic lotteries, whose payout schedule fills the tabulated grid of prize amounts and winning-bond counts. Closing clauses pledge that the bonds, prizes, and interest are exempt from state and local taxes and levies. Issued in the third postwar year amid reconstruction, the loan channelled household savings to the Soviet treasury, the lottery substituting the chance of a windfall for the certainty of a coupon. Austere and wholly typographic, the layout treats the financial instrument as a public notice rather than an ornamented security; the imprint reads Госзнак. 1948.

pages.description: This is a fifty-ruble bond of the State Internal Lottery Loan of 1982 (Государственный внутренний выигрышный заём 1982 года), issued by the government of the USSR. The face bears the denomination spelled in full — «Облигация на сумму пятьдесят рублей» — beside a large numeral 50 and the Soviet state emblem, with «СССР» on the shield below. As a выигрышный (lottery) loan, it carried no fixed coupon; holders were rewarded instead through periodic prize draws, the printed terms extending the loan's drawings across 1982–1990. Issued in the late Brezhnev years, the bond illustrates how the Soviet state mobilised household savings domestically, dressing public borrowing as a chance at winnings rather than guaranteed interest. The restrained green guilloche printing and heraldic crest project official solidity and discourage forgery.

The reverse of a fifty-ruble (ПЯТЬДЕСЯТ РУБЛЕЙ) bond of the State Internal Lottery Loan of 1982 (Государственный внутренний выигрышный заём 1982 года), issued by the government of the USSR and printed entirely in Russian. The face value of fifty rubles recurs in the corner medallions, while the body sets out the loan's conditions: a twenty-year term, with drawings held annually beginning in 1982, repayment and purchase at nominal value through the state savings banks, and exemption of both bonds and winnings from state taxation. Its substance is the prize schedule, listing per drawing one award of 10,000 rubles, five of 5,000, twenty of 2,500, fifty-five of 1,000, two hundred fifty of 500, twenty-five hundred of 250, and 17,169 of 100, totaling 20,000 winnings. Such lottery loans let the Soviet state borrow from household savings by substituting the chance of a prize for ordinary interest, channeling personal funds into the planned economy. The restrained guilloche borders and plain typography reflect a utilitarian official aesthetic rather than any decorative program.

**Summary of Regulations**

1. In order to open up the Whampoa (Huángpǔ) Commercial Harbour and carry out the construction plan of the late Premier [Sun Yat-sen], the Nationalist Government hereby, through the Ministry of Finance, issues this second series of Lottery Public Bond, totalling ten million yuan.

2. For this lottery bond, the Ministry of Finance assigns national revenue to the Central Bank as security for redemption of principal and payment of prizes, and the Central Bank bears full responsibility therefor.

3. This lottery bond is redeemed in three stages, each stage being ten months. In the first stage 2% of principal is repaid each month; in the second stage 3% each month; in the third stage 5% each month, so that the whole is fully repaid by the thirtieth month. Each redemption is determined by lot drawn by the Ministry of Finance; after the drawing, a further prize drawing is held among the bonds due for redemption. Redemption and prize matters are entrusted by the Ministry of Finance to the Central Bank and to reputable commercial firms.

4. Bonds drawn for redemption and prize-winning bonds shall become void if the money is not collected within three months.

5. The interest on this lottery bond is applied in full to prize money, as follows: First prize, 1 ticket, prize of 50,000 yuan; Second prize, 2 tickets, 2,000 yuan each; Third prize, 4 tickets, 500 yuan each; Fourth prize, 10 tickets, 100 yuan each; Fifth prize, 20 tickets, 50 yuan each; Sixth prize, 50 tickets, 30 yuan each; Seventh prize, 100 tickets, 15 yuan each; Eighth prize, 300 tickets, 10 yuan each; Ninth prize, 600 tickets, 5 yuan each; Tenth prize — apart from the nine prize classes listed above, every other bond drawn shall each receive prize money of five mao (0.5 yuan).

6. From the date of issue, a subscription period of two months is fixed for this lottery bond, after which the drawing for redemption is immediately conducted. While the bonds are not yet fully sold, in order to reward the fleetest subscribers, additional special drawings may be held, the method to be separately determined by the Ministry of Finance.

7. This lottery bond is in bearer form; it may be freely bought and sold, and may serve as an official-service guarantee deposit, as a bank reserve deposit, and as collateral for Central Bank advances.

8. Any official or merchant managing this bond who commits an act damaging the credit of this bond shall be punished according to the criminal law.

pages.description: This is a five-yuan (伍圓) lottery public bond (有奬公債), the Second Issue (第貳次) floated by the Ministry of Finance of the Nationalist Government (國民政府財政部) of China, dated the first day of the eighth month of Year 15 of the Republic (中華民國十五年八月一日發行 = 1 August 1926). The summary of regulations (條例摘要) states that the government issued this second series, totalling ten million yuan, expressly to develop the commercial harbour at Whampoa (黃埔商港) in fulfilment of the late Premier Sun Yat-sen's construction plan, with the debt secured on national revenue assigned to the Central Bank. Rather than paying fixed coupons, principal is retired in three stages through bi-monthly drawings that also distribute cash prizes to lucky holders—a lottery-redemption structure meant to attract subscribers. Signed by Finance Minister T. V. Soong (宋子文) and Council Chairman Wang Jingwei (汪兆銘), the note dates the Canton government to its revolutionary year on the eve of the Northern Expedition; its dense purple guilloche borders and large central denomination project the fiscal credibility a fledgling regime needed to borrow.

A lottery bond of five dollars in Canton currency, issued under the Second Nationalist Government Lottery Loan in the fifteenth year of the Republic of China, namely 1926. The loan, totalling $10,000,000 and sanctioned by Nationalist Government Mandate of 25 June 1926, was raised to finance construction of the Port of Whampoa near Canton, and was secured on the revenues of the Nationalist Government with the Central Bank of China as Government Depositary. Repayment ran over thirty monthly instalments, with public drawings held on the fifth of each month at the General Chamber of Commerce, Canton; the winning numbers then entered a second drawing for prizes ranging from a single first prize of $50,000 down to six hundred ninth prizes of $5, undrawn-but-blanked bonds earning a uniform fifty cents' interest. The instrument fuses public borrowing with the lottery's allure, mobilising small subscribers for the Kuomintang's revolutionary regime in Canton on the eve of the Northern Expedition. The English text and restrained green guilloché border address foreign and treaty-port investors. Dated 1 August 1926 and signed by Wang Ching Wai (Wang Jingwei), Chairman of the Nationalist Government, and the Minister of Finance.

pages.description: A four-percent consolidated railway bond of the Imperial Russian Government (Консолидированныя Российскія Четырёхпроцентныя Желѣзнодорожныя Облигаціи, 1st Series), with a face value of 125 gold rubles bearing interest at four percent. The instrument forms part of a vast consolidated loan of 175 million gold rubles, issued on the authority of the Imperial Ukase of 20 February 1889 to refund and unify the Treasury's scattered railway debts. The denomination is restated for every market in which the paper was placed: 500 francs, 404 German marks, 19 pounds 15 shillings 6 pence sterling, 239 Dutch guilders, and 96.25 gold dollars — a ledger of the foreign capitals on which Russian railway expansion depended. Printed in dark brown, crowned by the imperial double-headed eagle, the bond's sober engraving and multilingual valuation announce a borrower courting the savers of Paris, Berlin, London and Amsterdam at once.

This sheet sets out the conditions and the bearer certificate of an Imperial Government of Russia Consolidated 4 per cent Railroad Bond, Series 1, in the denomination of 125 gold roubles (rendered as 500 Francs, 404 German Marks, 19 Pounds Sterling 15 shillings 6 pence, 239 Dutch Florins, and 96.25 United States gold dollars). Printed in parallel French, German, and English, it was issued under the Imperial Ukase of 20 February / 4 March 1889 as part of a vast loan of 175 million gold roubles (700 million Francs), divided into 505,390 titles. Interest, paid quarterly and free of every Russian tax, runs at four per cent until redemption by drawing. The loan consolidated the 5 per cent obligations of numerous state-backed railways, payable across St. Petersburg, Paris, London, Berlin, Frankfurt, Amsterdam, and New York. The plain typographic frame and multilingual columns reveal an instrument conceived less as ornament than as a passport into the great money markets of Europe, by which a fiscally pressed empire refinanced costly railway debt on cheaper foreign terms.

Issued at Shanghai and dated the twelfth of February 1992 (一九九二年二月十二日), it bears the approval of the People's Bank of China, Shanghai Branch, together with the signed seal of the company's legal representative. The certificate belongs to the earliest wave of joint-stock conversions among Shanghai service enterprises following the resumption of share trading, when the city's taxi firms were among the first to raise public capital. The reverse of a share certificate of the Shanghai Pu Dong Qiang Sheng Taxi Co., Ltd. (上海浦東強生出租汽車股份有限公司), each full certificate representing ten shares of ten yuan, or one hundred yuan renminbi in all, issued at Shanghai and dated to 1992 on the obverse. The face carries no financial terms but two administrative apparatus essential to a registered equity. A printed notice (說明) in three clauses declares the stock an ordinary share offered by the company to work units and individuals, valid only when bearing the company seal, and forbidden as a circulating instrument: it may not be transferred, bought, sold, gifted, inherited, or mortgaged except through the designated registrar and the securities authorities. Below, a ruled 股份轉讓記錄 (transfer-of-shares record) awaits entries of date, transferor, transferee, and transfer agent. A red company chop and a guilloche security ground confirm authenticity. The document records an early, tightly controlled experiment in joint-stock ownership during China's market reforms, when equity was permitted yet hedged against free trading.
