Die Anleihe ist in Serien zu 5,000.000 Kronen eingeteilt und in Abschnitte zu 100, 200, 500, 1000 und 50.000 Kronen ausgeführt; jede Staatsanleihesverschreibung ist mit 22 Coupons und mit einem Talon versehen, gegen welchen die weiteren Coupons ohne Unterschrift zu 100 Kronen oder Coupons von 50 Kronen bei Einlösung an den k. k. Staatscentralkasse in Wien zeitgerecht ausgehändigt werden. Die Anleihe ist zum Kurse von par 100 begeben mit 5½°/₀ jährlich, und zwar die Abschnitte zu 50 Kronen zu ganzjährigen Raten vom 1. Juni und zum Kurse von 50 Kronen zu halbjährigen Raten vom 1. Juni und 1. Dezember eines jeden halbjährlich verschwindenden Termin. Die Zinsen vom 1. Juni 1918 bis 31. August 1918 werden in Obligationscoupons verrechnet. Die Anleihe wird zum Nennwerte rückzahlbar und unter Beibehaltung der Couponrechte mit 1914 als amortisierbar erklärt. Im Falle einer etwaigen Rückzahlung vor dem Fälligkeitstage wird die Ausstattung auf auflösendst in den Jahren 1921 bis 1958 auf Grund von Auslosungen getätigt. Die Auslosung wird nach [illegible] Worten entschieden und findet im September jeden Jahres statt; die Rückzahlung erfolgt am dem Auslosung folgenden 1. März. Die aufgelösten Serien werden nach Ziehung gestat nach Ziehung gehört eine Liste der Serie. Verfahren wird publiziert. Kontrolle gegen Verlust.

Der k. k. Staatsverwaltung hat das Recht vorbehalten, vom 1. Januar 1927 angefangen die Aus- lösung unabhängig von Ziehungslosung oder noch ungelisten Anleihesfläches einer dringenden Rückgabefirst zum Nennwerte zurückzuschreiben. Die Kündigung wird in der amtlichen "Wiener Zeitung" verlautbart werden. Die Auswahrung der Zinsen sowie die Rückzahlung der Anleihe erfolgt bei der k. k. Staatscentralkasse in Wien oder sonstigen Abzug gegen Hinterlegung der fälligen Zinsencoupons, beziehungsweise Staatsanleihe-verschreibung. Die Rückzahlung erfolgt am Fälligkeitstage des Kapitalbetrages; es sind demzufolge alle bei dahem Neben Fällig gewordene Coupons nebst Talon zurückzustellen. Der Betrag der Staatsanleihesverschreibung erleichted durch Verjährung in Anschung der Kapitalbeträges; es sind demzufolge alle bei dahem noch Fällig gewordene Coupons plus Talon zurückzusetzen. Die Staatsanleihesverschreibung erleichted durch Verjährung in Anschung des Kapitals binnen dreißig Jahren. Im Anschlung der Zinsen sechs Jahre vom Fälligkeitstermine an.

Wien, am 1. Juni 1918.

description: An engraved scrip certificate of The Common Fund Company Limited, dated at London, 20 December 1869 and issued under the Companies' Acts of 1862 to 1867. It entitles the holder to call for one hundred shares of £20 each in the company's capital stock, to be exchanged for certificates of full stock upon payment of the £20 par cost per share in one sum. title: Tontine Royale Subscription Contract
description: A printed subscription contract for the French royal tontine created by the King's Edict of August 1734, executed before the notaries at the Châtelet de Paris. The Crown sold 1,463,000 livres of life annuities styled a tontine subject to accrual, divided into fifteen classes of subdivisions, each share carrying three hundred livres of capital. The annuities were secured, by a privilege ranking ahead of the Trésor Royal, on the duties on aides and gabelles and on the cinq grosses fermes. On a subscriber's death one quarter of the arrears reverted to the King and three quarters accrued to the survivors of the subdivision, so that its last survivor alone gathered three-quarters of the revenue, paid in two installments yearly from 1 October 1734.
creator: Notaires du Châtelet de Paris
notes: French royal tontine, August 1734. Second Class, First Subdivision. 14,063,000 livres of life annuities. Drawn up before Notaires du Châtelet de Paris including Michel Etienne Turgot. Annuities charged on Aides et Gabelles revenues.

# Transcription

**Original (French):**

TONTINE ROYALE Aoüst 1734. 2.e Classe.

M. De Raphanneuf
Subdivision

PARDEVANT les Contrôllers du Roy, Notaires au Chastelet de Paris, souffignez, furent presens Messire MICHEL ESTIENNE TURGOT, Chevalier, Seigneur de Souffons, Bons, Uffy, Potigny, Perciers, Brucourt, & autres lieux, Conseiller du Roy en ses Conseils, President au Parlement & en la seconde Chambre des Requestes du Palais, Prevost des Marchands; Claude-François Petit, Ecuyer, Conseiller du Roy, Quartiniers; Jean-Baptiste de Santeul, Ecuyer; Jean-Baptiste Tripart, Ecuyer, Conseiller du Roy & de la Ville; & François Touvenot, Ecuyer, Conseiller du Roy, Notaire au Chastelet, tous Eichevins de cette Ville.

Lesquels ont dit, que le Roy par son Edit du mois d'Aoüst 1734. registré où besoin a esté, auroit, pour les causes y contenués, ordonne qu'il seroit par les Commissaires de Sa Majesté nommeroît, vendu & alienné quatorze cens soixante-trois mille livres actuelles & effectives de rente viagere, sous le titre de Tontine, fusette à accroissement, distribuée en quinze classes, composées de differentes divisions, dont chaque action feroit de trois cens livres de capital; lesdigtes rentes à prendre sur le produit des droits d'Aydes & Gabelles, & des cinq grosses fermes, que Sa Majesté à [speciellement] & par privilege, affectez, obligez & hypothequez au payement & continuation des arrerages desdites rentes, même par préference à la partie du trésor Royal, dont les constitutions seroient faites à ceux qui defereroient les acquerois sous leurs noms, où autres qu'ils nommerioent, avec faculté à chaque personne de prendre tel nombre de parties de rente qu'il lui plairoit dans chaque subdivision de la classe, pour lesquelles il lui seroit expedié des contrats: Que de la rente de chaque rentier qui viendroit à deceder, un quart des arrearges de fadite rente seroit estenu à la defcharge des revenus de Sa Majesté, & les trois autres quarts appartiendieroît par accroissement aux survivans de la subdivision de la classe, entre lesquels ils seroient distribuée d'année en année jusqu'au dernier mourant; en forte que le dernier vivant de chaque subdivision de chacune desdites classes, recueilleeroit feul les trois quarts du revenu des capitaux qui composeroient ladite subdivision, & que lesdites rentes pourroient auffi estre acquises par les estrangers non naturalizez, même ceux demeùrans hors du Royaume; à l'efect de quoy Sa Majesté auroit renoncé à tous droits d'aubaine, confiscations, & autres qui pourroient lui appartenir: pour, des arrearges desdites rentes, seûoit par les acquéreurs leur vie durant, comme de leur propre chose, vray & loyal acquelt, en vertu des contracts qui seroient faits par lesdits Sieurs Brevolt des Marchands & Eichevins, & estre payé des arrearges desdites rentes à bureau ouvert par chacune année, en deux paiemens, sur lesquittances en parchemin, paffez devant Notaires en la forme portée audit Edit, à commencer du premier Octobre 1734. pour ceux qui auroient fourni leurs fonds avant le premier Janvier 1735. fans que lesdites rentes puiffent estre fujettes à aucunes faites pour quelque caufe que ce soit, même pour les dettes & affaires de Sa Majesté, ni estre reduites ni retranchées fous quelque pretexte que ce puiffe estre: en outre, que les rentes qui seroient acquises par les estrangers, seroient exemptes de toutes lettres de marque & de represaille, ainfi qu'il eft plus au long porté audit Edit; en execution duquel a esté faite vente & alienation par Messieurs les Commiffaires du Conseil, Procureurs speciaux de Sa Majesté auxdits Sieurs Brevolt des Marchands & Eichevins, desdites quatorze cens foixante-trois mille livres de rente, par contract paffé en vertu des Lettres patentes y enoncées, pardevant Bourron & ion conferere

ROYAL TONTINE August 1734. Second Class.

M. De Raphanneuf
Subdivision

BEFORE the Controllers of the King, Notaries of the Châtelet of Paris, undersigned, were present Messire MICHEL ESTIENNE TURGOT, Knight, Lord of Souffons, Bons, Uffy, Potigny, Perciers, Brucourt, and other places, Counselor of the King in his Councils, President of Parliament and in the Second Chamber of Petitions of the Palace, Provost of the Merchants; Claude-François Petit, Esquire, Counselor of the King, Quarternier; Jean-Baptiste de Santeul, Esquire; Jean-Baptiste Tripart, Esquire, Counselor of the King and of the City; and François Touvenot, Esquire, Counselor of the King, Notary of the Châtelet, all Aldermen of this City.

Who declared that the King, by his Edict of the month of August 1734, registered where necessary, would have, for the reasons contained therein, ordered that by the Commissioners of His Majesty appointed, fourteen thousand sixty-three thousand livres of actual and effective life annuities would be sold and alienated, under the title of Tontine, subject to increase, distributed into fifteen classes, composed of different divisions, each share consisting of three hundred livres of capital; said annuities to be charged on the proceeds of the rights of Aides and Gabelles, and the five major farms, which His Majesty had specially and by privilege, affected, obliged, and mortgaged to the payment and continuation of the arrears of said annuities, even in preference to the portion of the Royal Treasury, the constitutions of which would be made to those who would purchase the shares under their names or others whom they would name, with the faculty for each person to take such number of annuity shares as they pleased in each subdivision of the class, for which they would be issued contracts: That from the annuity of each annuitant who should come to die, one quarter of the arrears of said annuity would be retained for the discharge of the revenues of His Majesty, and the three other quarters would belong by accretion to the survivors of the subdivision of the class, among whom they would be distributed year by year until the last survivor; so that the last living member of each subdivision of each of said classes would collect alone the three quarters of the revenue of the capital which would compose said subdivision, and that said annuities could also be acquired by foreigners not naturalized, even those residing outside the Kingdom; for which purpose His Majesty would have renounced all rights of escheat, confiscations, and others which might belong to him: for, from the arrears of said annuities, would be paid by the acquirers for their lifetime, as of their own property, true and loyal ownership, by virtue of the contracts which would be made by said Messieurs Brevolt of the Merchants and Aldermen, and be paid of the arrears of said annuities at open bureau by each year, in two payments, upon receipts on parchment, passed before Notaries in the form contained in said Edict, commencing from the first October 1734 for those who would have provided their funds before the first January 1735, provided that said annuities cannot be subject to any proceedings for any cause whatsoever, even for the debts and affairs of His Majesty, nor be reduced or diminished under any pretext whatsoever: furthermore, that the annuities which would be acquired by foreigners would be exempt from all letters of marque and reprisal, as it is more fully contained in said

# Transcription

**Original (French):**

NUMÉRO DE SÉRIE: 58
NUMÉRO D'ORDRE: 111

TRAVAUX D'IRRIGATION DU GOUVERNEMENT ÉGYPTIEN

ASSOUAN ET ASSIOUT 1898

MANDAT DE PAIEMENT

£500 STERLING | £500 STERLING

Le Gouvernement Égyptien déclare par les présentes, qu'en retour de travaux effectués et de matériaux fournis pour les travaux d'irrigation susmentsionnés, il reconnaît devoir, absolument, et sans condition aucune, à MM. JOHN AIRD et CIE. la somme de Cinq cents livres sterling (£500).

Le Gouvernement s'engage par les présentes à payer à MM. JOHN AIRD et CIE., ou au PORTEUR DE CE MANDAT, le 1er Janvier 1932 la dite somme de Cinq cents livres sterling.

Ce paiement s'effectuera à LONDRES, par l'intermédiaire de la Banque d'Angleterre, contre la remise de ce mandat.

Ce paiement sera effectué à tout événement AU PORTEUR des présentes, en totalité et sans déduction quelconque et indépendamment de toute contestation qui peut être actuellement ou qui pourrait s'élever dans la suite quelconque. [Underlined text in box: "Gouvernement"]

MM. John Aird et Cie., ou de toute autre contestation quelle qu'elle soit, la dette reconnue par les présentes étant pour une somme certaine et déterminée et constituant une créance liquide et reconnue par le Gouvernement Égyptien.

Le présent mandat confère au porteur, jusqu'à son entier désintéressement, une affectation sur les travaux pour assurer le paiement de la somme indiquée dans ce mandat, le dit porteur pourra, d'accord avec les porteurs de tous mandats sans par rapport aux mêmes travaux (dont le maximum ne devra pas toutefois excéder les limites mentionnées dans la table au dos des présentes) ou d'accord avec la majorité de ces porteurs, nommer ou faire nommer par l'autorité compétente un représentant chargé de mettre à exécution de la manière qu'il appartiendra le dit droit d'affectation, au cas où ce mandat n'aura pas été payé à l'échéance.

Aucune prise de possession par le Gouvernement des travaux ni aucun autre acte quelconque ne seront susceptibles de porter atteinte à la dite affectation.

Le présent mandat et tous autres mandats émis ou à émettre dans les limites susmensionnées auront rang égal et jouiront sans aucun droit de préférence ni de priorité à raison de leur numéro, série, date d'émission ou autre circonstance quelconque.

En date du 30 Juillet 1901 | Pour le Gouvernement,
[Signatures and handwriting] | Le Ministre des Travaux Publics.

Contresigné
[Signature]
Ingénieur du Gouvernement Égyptien.

SERIES NUMBER: 58
ORDER NUMBER: 111

IRRIGATION WORKS OF THE EGYPTIAN GOVERNMENT

ASWAN AND ASSIUT 1898

PAYMENT WARRANT

£500 STERLING | £500 STERLING

The Egyptian Government declares by these presents, that in return for work executed and materials supplied for the above-mentioned irrigation works, it acknowledges owing, absolutely and unconditionally, to MM. JOHN AIRD and CO. the sum of Five Hundred Pounds Sterling (£500).

The Government undertakes by these presents to pay to MM. JOHN AIRD and CO., or to the BEARER OF THIS WARRANT, on 1st January 1932 the said sum of Five Hundred Pounds Sterling.

This payment shall be made in LONDON, through the intermediary of the Bank of England, against the surrender of this warrant.

This payment shall be made in any event TO THE BEARER of these presents, in full and without any deduction whatsoever and independently of any contestation which may currently exist or which may subsequently arise in any manner. [Underlined in box: "Government"]

No taking into possession by the Government of the works nor any other whatsoever act shall be capable of affecting the said charge.

The present warrant and all other warrants issued or to be issued within the limits aforesaid shall rank equally and shall enjoy without any right of preference or priority by reason of their number, series, date of issue or other circumstance whatsoever.

title: Unilever N.V. Option Certificate, Rotterdam, July
description: An option certificate issued by Unilever N.V. of Rotterdam in July 1937, void after 30 June 1942. Eight such certificates, surrendered together, entitle the holder to acquire one certificate for a single ordinary Unilever share of 1,000 guilders nominal, at 1,950 guilders, or 195 percent, through 31 December 1938, and 2,150 guilders, or 215 percent, from 1 January 1939. The option springs from Van den Bergh's Fabrieken N.V.'s 3.5 percent loan of 1937, capped at 30,000,000 guilders, granting bondholders an equity sweetener. A later overprint notes the renaming of the company to Lever Brothers & Unilever N.V. Printed by Joh. Enschedé en Zonen, Haarlem.
creator: Unilever N.V.
notes: Optiebewijs No. 97790. Unilever N.V., Rotterdam, July 1937; of no value after 30 June 1942. Eight certificates, surrendered together, entitle the holder to one certificate for an ordinary Unilever share of f.1000 nominal, at f.1950 (195%) through 31 December 1938 and f.2150 (215%) from 1 January 1939 to 30 June 1942. Tied to the Van den Bergh's Fabrieken N.V. 3.5% obligatielening of 1937 (max f.30,000,000), whose bonds are accepted in payment at full nominal value plus accrued interest. Printed by Joh. Enschede en Zonen, Haarlem; orange 50c Dutch revenue seal. A printed note records the renaming of Unilever N.V. to 'Lever Brothers & Unilever N.V.' by notarial act of 23 November 1937. DUPLICATE NOT DISPLAYED: the collection also holds a second example of the same option certificate - No. 86786 (formerly goetzmann0503) - removed from the website 2026-07-24 but retained in the collection.
transcription:
# Unilever N.V. Option Certificate No. 97790

**Original (Dutch):**

UNILEVER N.V.
GEVESTIGD TE ROTTERDAM.

OPTIEBEWIJS No. 97790

VAN ONWAARDE NA 30 JUNI 1942.

Bij notariële acte dd° 23 November 1937 is de naam der Unilever N.V. veranderd in: „Lever Brothers & Unilever N.V.". De naam der Van den Bergh's Fabrieken N.V. werd bij notariële acte dd° 2 September 1938 gewijzigd in: „Van den Bergh's en Jurgens' Fabrieken N.V.".

De houder van acht dezer optiebewrijzen heeft het recht, tegen inlevering dezer bewijzen van Unilever N.V. een certificaat van een gewoon aandeel in Unilever N.V., groot ƒ 1000.— nominaal, te verwerven tot de prijs van ƒ 1950.— (195%) tot en met 31 December 1938 en van ƒ 2150.— (215%) tot en met 1 Januari 1939 tot en met 30 Juni 1942, op de voorwaarden vervat in de aan de keerzijde van dit bewijs vermelde bepalingen. Overeenkomstig art. 5 dieser bepalingen worden bij de storting 3½%-obligatien, behorende tot de in 1937 ten laste van Van den Bergh's Fabrieken N.V. uitgegeven 3½%-obligatielening, ten hoogste groot ƒ 30.000.000.—, in betaling aangenomen tot haar volle nominale bedrag, vermeererd met opgelopen rente.

ROTTERDAM, Juli 1937.

[Secretary signature]
SECRETARIS.

[Chairman signature]
LID VAN DE RAAD VAN BESTUUR.

JOH. ENSCHEDÉ EN ZONEN - HAARLEM

---

**English Translation:**

UNILEVER N.V.
ESTABLISHED IN ROTTERDAM.

OPTION CERTIFICATE No. 97790

OF NO VALUE AFTER 30 JUNE 1942.

By notarial deed of 23 November 1937, the name of Unilever N.V. was changed to: "Lever Brothers & Unilever N.V.". The name of Van den Bergh's Fabrieken N.V. was changed by notarial deed of 2 September 1938 to: "Van den Bergh's and Jurgens' Fabrieken N.V.".

The holder of eight of these option certificates has the right, upon return of these certificates to Unilever N.V., to acquire a certificate of an ordinary share in Unilever N.V. with a nominal value of ƒ 1,000.— at the price of ƒ 1,950.— (195%) until and including 31 December 1938 and ƒ 2,150.— (215%) until and including 1 January 1939 and until 30 June 1942, under the conditions set forth in the provisions stated on the reverse of this certificate. In accordance with article 5 of these provisions, upon deposit of the 3½%-bonds belonging to the 3½%-bond loan issued in 1937 by Van den Bergh's Fabrieken N.V., up to a maximum amount of ƒ 30,000,000.—, shall be accepted in payment at their full nominal value, plus accrued interest.

ROTTERDAM, July 1937.

---

- Serial number: **No. 97790**
- Ornate blue decorative border frame throughout
- Printer mark at bottom: "JOH. ENSCHEDÉ EN ZONEN - HAARLEM" (Johannes Enschedé and Sons, Haarlem - a prominent Dutch security printer)
- Date: Rotterdam, Juli 1937 (July 1937)

title: United States of Brazil Funding Bond
description: A $100 bearer bond of the United States of Brazil, styled the "5 Per Cent 20-Year Funding Bond of 1931," dated October 1, 1931 and due October 1, 1951. It promises to pay the bearer one hundred dollars in gold coin of the United States, with half-yearly coupons at five percent a year, through the fiscal agency of the City Bank Farmers Trust Company in New York, successor to Dillon, Read & Co., and at the holder's option in London. The bond belongs to Brazil's 1931 funding loan, which consolidated short-term external obligations and capitalized unpaid interest into long-dated paper.
creator: United States of Brazil
notes: Brazil 5% 20-Year Funding Bond of 1931, $100. No. S2940. Due October 1, 1951. Decree No. 20,251, August 1931. Semi-annual coupons. Payable at City Bank Farmers Trust Company, New York.

title: Westchester & Philadelphia Rail Road Co. Scrip, Philadelphia
description: An interest-bearing scrip certificate of the Westchester & Philadelphia Rail Road Co., issued at Philadelphia on the first day of October, 1860, and authorized by resolution of the board on September 29th, 1860. The company acknowledges itself indebted to Washington Pastorius in the sum of fifty-eight dollars, which it promises to pay him or his assigns on the first day of October, 1865, with interest at six percent a year from its date. It is attested by the treasurer's signature and the company seal. Scrip of this kind let a company settle obligations with paper rather than coin, postponing payment while binding holders to the road's fortunes.

description: A blank preliminary bond-sale agreement, valid only after the sellers' confirmation by separate letter, issued by the banking and brokerage house Y. title: Deutsches Reich Treasury Note
description: A Treasury note of the German Reich, second issue of 1923, with a face value of five million marks in Reich currency, issued at Berlin on 25 May 1923 by the Reichsschuldenverwaltung under the law of 2 May 1923. It bears interest at a floating rate tied to the Reichsbank discount rate, bounded between a minimum of 8 and a maximum of 15 percent, and is redeemable from 1 September 1927. An attached strip of half-yearly coupons falls due each 1 March and 1 September of 1926 and 1927, void after 1930 and 1931. The mark was depreciating rapidly at the time of issue, and a fixed coupon had become untenable.

title: Eendracht Polder Bond, Zaamslag (Zeeland)
description: A part-printed, part-manuscript bond recording a debt undertaken by the Heeren van Zaamslag, acting as administrators of the newly diked Eendracht Polder on the island of Axel in Zeeland, sealed at Sluys on the first of July 1779. The undersigned acknowledge themselves indebted to Pieter Paul van Gelce, or the lawful bearer, in the capital sum of one hundred Flemish pounds, borrowed to finance the reclamation and its works, at 3 percent interest a year free of charges. Beyond the fixed interest, the holder shares by lot in the profits of the polder's produce, blending a loan with a claim on the harvest.
creator: Heeren van Zaamslag
notes: Eendracht Polder bond, No. 353. Heeren van Zaamslag, island of Axel, Zeeland. Capital: £100 Flemish at 3% p.a. Issued to Pieter Paul van Gelce or bearer. Holders entitled to participate in polder produce profits distributed by lot. Dutch land reclamation finance, ca. 18th century.

title: Chinese Imperial Government Gold Loan of 1903 Bond
description: A 500-franc bearer bond from the Imperial Chinese Government's 5 percent Gold Loan of 1903, issued at Brussels on 12 April 1905. The loan, totalling 25,000,000 francs in 50,000 bonds of 500 francs, was dedicated exclusively to constructing the railway between Kaifeng-Fou and Honan-Fou in Honan province, undertaken through the Compagnie Impériale des Chemins de Fer Chinois and Belgian railway interests under imperial edicts of the Kuang-Hsü reign. Interest of 25 francs runs at 5 percent a year, payable each 1 January and 1 July in gold, and the bond is redeemable over twenty years by annual drawings from the tenth year. Its text is in French, with Chinese imperial seals and signatures.

pages.description: The bond's face: a pagoda-form orange border crowns the titles "Gouvernement Impérial de Chine, Emprunt Chinois 5% Or 1903," and "Obligation de Cinq Cents Francs au Porteur." French text states the railway purpose, the 25-franc annual interest, and thirty-year redemption. Chinese seals, three authorising signatures, and two attached coupons (57th, 58th) appear. "500 Francs" sits at base. Page 1 of 2.

The reverse, printed in dense French. An "Obligation Générale" preamble is followed by two "Édit de S.M. l'Empereur de Chine" (dated 1899 and 1903) and a "Création de l'Emprunt" extract of the contract. A twenty-column amortisation table (1915–1934) details capital, interest, and totals across the loan's life. A signature closes the text. Page 2 of 2.

title: Imperial Russian Gold Loan Bond, Sixth Issue
description: An Imperial Russian Government 4 percent Gold Loan bearer bond, the Sixth Issue of 1894, Class A, in the denomination of 125 gold rubles, authorized by Highest Imperial ukase of 9 February 1894. The face restates the sum as 500 French francs, 404 German marks, £19 15s 6d sterling, 239 Dutch guilders and 96.25 gold dollars, and it bears four percent paid quarterly on coupons honoured at St. Petersburg, Paris, London, Berlin, Amsterdam and New York. The whole emission totalled 113,600,000 gold rubles, or 454,400,000 francs, and was issued to buy out the shares and founders' scrip of the Main Company of Russian Railways as the line passed to the treasury. The bonds are redeemable at par by drawings over eighty-one years, and the text is printed in Russian on the face and in French, German and English on the reverse.

Centred is the obligation "ОБЛИГАЦІЯ въ сто двадцать пять рублей золотомъ" (125 gold rubles / 500 fr.), marked "НА ПРЕДЪЯВИТЕЛЯ" (to bearer), Class A. Each states the 125-rouble value with equivalents of 500 francs, 404 marks, 19 livres 15s 6d sterling, 239 florins, and 96.25 dollars, payable to bearer, followed by dense conditions of the loan. Page 2 of 2.

The Russian and French face of the talon. A header names the 4% gold loan, sixth issue of 1894, and the 187 rouble 50 kopek obligation, with its franc, reichsmark, sterling, florin, and dollar equivalents. Below, a grid of detachable coupons (numbered roughly 97 to 116) each states amount, due date, and paying cities. Page 1 of 2.

The German and English face of the same talon, headed "Russische 4% Gold-Anleihe, sechste Emission, von 1894" and "Russian 4% Gold Loan, Sixth Issue, 1894." A continuing grid of coupons, German entries left and English right, repeats the obligation's terms and lists redemption at St. Petersburg, Berlin, Paris, London, and Amsterdam. Page 2 of 2.

**А.**

**ОБЛИГАЦІЯ** — **125 Руб. Зол.**

**№059944**

**ВЪ СТО ДВАДЦАТЬ ПЯТЬ РУБЛЕЙ ЗОЛОТОМЪ**

= 500 фр. = 404 герм. марк. = 19 фунт. ст. 15 ш. 6 п. = 239 голл. гульд. = 96,25 долл. зол.,

записанная въ Государственную Долговую Книгу, кн. [3 — handwritten] стр. [96 — handwritten]

**НА ПРЕДЪЯВИТЕЛЯ.**

Владѣлецъ сей облигаціи имѣетъ право на сумму СТО ДВАДЦАТЬ ПЯТЬ рублей золотомъ, приносящую ЧЕТЫРЕ процента въ годъ дохода до погашенія оной тиражемъ. Облигація сія освобождена навсегда отъ всякихъ русскихъ налоговъ. Проценты уплачиваются четыре раза въ годъ: (20 Марта / 1 Апрѣля — 19 Іюня / 1 Іюля — 19 Сентября / 1 Октября — 20 Декабря / 1 Января) по предъявленіи купоновъ, по желанію владѣльца:

въ С.-ПЕТЕРБУРГѢ: въ ГОСУДАРСТВЕННОМЪ БАНКѢ, золотомъ или кредитными билетами по курсу дня;

въ ПАРИЖѢ: въ Парижско-Нидерландскомъ Банкѣ, Ліонскомъ Кредитѣ, Національной Учетной Конторѣ, въ Отдѣленіи Русскаго для Внѣшней Торговли Банка и у Гг. Готтингеръ и К°, во франкахъ;

въ ЛОНДОНѢ: въ Агентствѣ Русскаго для Внѣшней Торговли Банка, въ фунтахъ стерлинговъ;

въ БЕРЛИНѢ: у Гг. Мендельсонъ и К°, въ герм. маркахъ;

въ АМСТЕРДАМѢ: у Гг. Липманъ, Розенталь и К°, въ голландскихъ гульденахъ;

въ НЬЮ-ЙОРКѢ: у Гг. Берингъ, Магунъ и К°, въ долларахъ золотомъ.

Облигаціи сіи подлежатъ выкупу по нарицательной цѣнѣ въ теченіе 81 года, посредствомъ имѣющихъ быть въ Государственной Коммиссіи Погашенія Долговъ два раза въ годъ, 20 Марта / 1 Апрѣля и 19 Сентября / 1 Октября каждаго года, тиражей, начиная съ 19 Сентября / 1 Октября 1894 года. Для этой цѣли отчисляется въ каждое полугодіе 0,08428[%] съ нарицательнаго капитала займа, съ присоединеніемъ 2% на всѣ погашенныя облигаціи.

До 19 Декабря 1903 г. / 1 Января 1904 г. вышеупомянутое отчисленіе на погашеніе займа не будетъ увеличиваемо, а равно до того же срока не будетъ приступлено и къ выкупу, ни къ конверсіи настоящаго займа.

Уплата капитала по вышедшимъ въ тиражъ облигаціямъ производится за тиражемъ срока платежа процентовъ, въ тѣхъ же городахъ и въ тѣхъ же валютахъ, какъ и уплата купоновъ.

Купоны, срокъ коимъ истекаетъ послѣ срока уплаты капитала, должны быть представлены вмѣстѣ съ облигаціями; въ противномъ случаѣ, сумма недостающихъ купоновъ будетъ удержана при выдачѣ капитала по вышедшей въ тиражъ облигаціи.

Облигаціи сего займа сохраняютъ силу въ теченіе 30 лѣтъ со сроковъ, назначенныхъ для ихъ оплаты, а купоны сихъ облигацій — въ теченіе 10 лѣтъ со срока ихъ оплаты.

Облигаціи сіи снабжены купонами за 19 Декабря 1903 г. / 1 Января 1904 г. и талономъ, для возобновленія купоновъ.

По истеченіи срока купоннаго листа, представляющемъ талонъ отъ облигацій, которыя до тѣхъ поръ не вышли въ тиражъ, будутъ выданы, безплатно, новые купонные листы, въ мѣстахъ оплаты купоновъ.

Облигаціи сіи выпускаются именныя и на предъявителя. Правила относительно обращенія именныхъ облигацій въ предъявительскія и обратно утверждаются Министромъ Финансовъ.

**TO BEARER.**

The holder of this bond is entitled to the sum of ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE gold rubles, yielding FOUR per cent per annum in income until its redemption by drawing. This bond is forever exempt from all Russian taxes. Interest is paid four times a year (20 March / 1 April — 19 June / 1 July — 19 September / 1 October — 20 December / 1 January) upon presentation of the coupons, at the holder's choice:

in ST. PETERSBURG: at the STATE BANK, in gold or in credit notes at the rate of the day;

in PARIS: at the Banque de Paris et des Pays-Bas, the Crédit Lyonnais, the Comptoir National d'Escompte, at the Branch of the Russian Bank for Foreign Trade, and at Messrs. Hottinguer & Co., in francs;

in LONDON: at the Agency of the Russian Bank for Foreign Trade, in pounds sterling;

in BERLIN: at Messrs. Mendelssohn & Co., in German marks;

in AMSTERDAM: at Messrs. Lippmann, Rosenthal & Co., in Dutch guilders;

in NEW YORK: at Messrs. Baring, Magoun & Co., in gold dollars.

These bonds are subject to redemption at par over the course of 81 years, by means of drawings to be held at the State Commission for the Redemption of Debts twice a year, on 20 March / 1 April and 19 September / 1 October of each year, beginning on 19 September / 1 October 1894. For this purpose there is set aside each half-year 0.08428[%] of the nominal capital of the loan, with the addition of 2% on all redeemed bonds.

Until 19 December 1903 / 1 January 1904 the above-mentioned redemption allocation shall not be increased, and likewise before that same date there shall be no recourse to redemption or to conversion of the present loan.

Payment of the capital on bonds drawn is made, following the drawing, at the date of interest payment, in the same cities and the same currencies as the payment of the coupons.

Coupons whose maturity falls after the date of payment of the capital must be presented together with the bonds; otherwise, the amount of the missing coupons will be withheld upon payment of the capital on the drawn bond.

The bonds of this loan remain valid for 30 years from the dates set for their payment, and the coupons of these bonds for 10 years from the date of their payment.

These bonds are furnished with coupons up to 19 December 1903 / 1 January 1904 and with a talon for the renewal of coupons.

Upon expiry of the coupon sheet, against the talon of bonds which have not by then been drawn, new coupon sheets will be issued free of charge at the places of coupon payment.

These bonds are issued as registered and to bearer. The rules concerning the conversion of registered bonds into bearer bonds and vice versa are confirmed by the Minister of Finance.

title: Koninklijke Fransche Lyfrente Negotiatie van Maart 1781 — Nominee Register, Amsterdam
description: A notarial register, headed "Copia," recording nominees in a Dutch life-annuity loan on the French crown, the Koninglyke Fransche Lyfrente Negotiatie van Maart 1781, directed by Pieter Stadnitski and Hendrik Vollenhoven. It was executed at Amsterdam on the first of May 1787 before the notary Abraham van Beem, with Abraham Fock and Adriaan Scharff as commissioners. It concerns fifty-nine contracts of 25,000 livres capital each and lists here nominees numbered 30 through 59, all of them women. A marginal note records that No. 74, on the life of Elisabeth Judith de Vries, lapsed at her death on 14 February 1787. In such loans investors pooled funds to buy royal annuities written on young nominees, so that survivors absorbed the income of those who died.
creator: Abraham Fock; Adriaan Schaap (Commissioners)

description: A bearer bond for £20 sterling, one of a £5,000,000 issue placed under the Imperial Chinese Government Gold Loan of 1908, signed and dated at Paris on 1 March 1909. title: Compagnie des Indes Life Annuity (Rente Viagère), Paris
description: A notarial act drawn at the Châtelet de Paris and dated 13 January 1725, cast in the prévôtal form headed by Gabriel-Jérôme de Bullion, Prévôt of Paris. By it the Syndic and Directors of the Compagnie des Indes, acting in the company's name, constitute a life annuity of 275 livres, payable yearly in coin from the company's funds, purchased by Charles-Claude Poyrier, Écuyer, Conseiller-Secrétaire du Roi, and his wife, Dame Élizabeth Louise, but measured on the life of their son, Louis François, who is to enjoy it after his parents' death. The act invokes the royal Council edicts of February and 20 June 1724 that reorganized the company after the collapse of John Law's System. The annuity forms part of a lottery-tontine, the shares of surviving annuitants growing as fellow annuitants die.
creator: Compagnie des Indes (French East India Company)
notes: Compagnie des Indes legal document, January 13, 1745, Paris. Director: Gabriel-Jérôme de Bullion. Concerns share transfers and Loterie de Saint-Quentin proceeds. References King's Council edict February 3, 1724. Parties include Dame Juliane Elizabeth de Guise Holler.

# Compagnie des Indes Life Annuity (Rente Viagère), Paris — Transcription

## Original:

*(Language: French. Notarial deed of the Prévôté / Châtelet de Paris. Printed form with handwritten insertions in the blanks, plus manuscript marginal notes and a fiscal stamp. Handwritten portions are rendered in *italics*; printed portions in roman.)*

*(Top left, manuscript date:)* *13 Janvier 1725.*

*(Upper centre, engraved tax stamp of the généralité:)* **ACT. DES N. — 13 SOLS 4 D. — GEN. DE PARIS** *(caduceus device between two medallions)*

*(Above centre, manuscript:)* *né 27 8bre 1717* *(i.e. "né 27 octobre 1717")*

*(Centre, second inked stamp / cartouche:)* **PREMI. D'EXPE. 4. — FEUIL. DITIONS. LIVR.**

*(Upper right, manuscript file annotations:)* *Mr et Mad.e / Poyrieu. / N° 336.*

---

*(Main printed body, opening initial "A":)*

**A** TOUS ceux qui ces presentes Lettres verront, Gabriel-Jerosme de Bullion, Chevalier Comte Desclimont, Mestre de Camp du Regiment de Provence Infanterie, Conseiller du Roy en tous ses Conseils, Prevost de la Ville, Prevoté & Vicomté de Paris, SALUT. Sçavoir faisons que pardevant M[es] *[handwritten: Et Jean Gaschieu]* Conseillers du Roy, Notaires, Gardes-nottes & Gardes-scel de Sa Majesté au Chastelet de Paris, soussignez, furent presens *[handwritten: Estienne Demeunier fils]* *Escuyer* ...... Syndic de la Compagnie des Indes, Et *[handwritten: sieur François Mouchard & Vincent pierre Fromaget Escuyer]*

Directeurs de ladite Compagnie; lesquels en vertu de l'Arrest du Conseil d'Estat du Roy du 15. Fevrier 1724. par lequel Sa Majesté a accordé à ladite Compagnie le Privilege Exclusif de faire dans l'estenduë du Royaume, differentes Loteries; Et en execution de la Déliberation du 13. Decembre audit an, prise dans l'Assemblée generale d'Administration de ladite Compagnie, au sujet de la Loterie composée de Lots payables, les uns en Argent, & les autres en Rentes Viageres, qui doivent former un corps de Tontine de Vingt-huit mille sept cens cinquante Numero, chacun d'iceux, susceptible d'accroissement, à mesure des decés des Rentiers interessez à ladite Loterie; sçavoir, pour moitié au profit de ladite Compagnie, Et pour l'autre moitié à ceux des Rentiers survivans, que le sort préferera dans les Loteries qui doivent estre tirées annuellement & successivement. Lesquelles Rentes Viageres qui seront assignées sur le fonds de ladite Compagnie, lesdits Sieurs Syndic & Directeurs ont pouvoir de constituer tant au profit des Sujets de Sa Majesté, que des Estrangers, ausquels le payement des Arrerages & des Accroissemens en doit estre fait, quand même ils resideroient hors du Royaume, & même en temps de guerre, sans que lesdites Rentes puissent estre retranchées ou saisies pour quelque cause que ce soit, pas même pour les propres deniers & affaires de Sa Majesté, conformément à l'Arrest du 20. Juin 1724. ainsi qu'il est plus au long porté en ladite Déliberation, par laquelle il est permis aux Acquereurs desdites Rentes, d'en faire passer les Contracts sous le nom de telles personnes qu'ils voudront choisir, pour en joüir, tant par eux, que par ceux qu'ils nommeront sur leurs Quittances, pendant la vie des personnes sur la teste desquelles les Constitutions auront esté mises. Ont lesdits Sieurs Syndic & Directeurs comparans, en vertu desdites Déliberations & Arrests du Conseil des 15. Fevrier & 20. Juin 1724. vendu, créé & constitué, assis & assigné par ces presentes; Et promis pour & au nom de ladite Compagnie des Indes, garentir de tous troubles & autres empêchemens generalement quelconques, A

*[handwritten, filling the blank:] Mre Charles Claude Poyrieu Escuyer Conseiller Secretaire du Roy Receveur general des finances d'Orleans Et Dame Elizabeth Louise Mollée son Epouse, pour joüir par eux et le survivant d'eux de la rente cy après sur la teste et pendant la vie de Louis François Poyrieu leur fils qui la jouira après le decds [decès] de sesd[its] pere et mere, lesd[its] sieur et D[am]e Poyrieu, elle dudit sieur son mary autho[risée] à l'effet des presentes, demeurant à paris Rue Thevenot, à ce jour[d'huy] les acceptant Acquereurs, Deux cent soixante quinze [livres]*

de Rente Viagere; laquelle Rente lesdits Sieurs Syndic & Directeurs, comparans pour & au nom de ladite Compagnie des Indes, promettent de faire bailler & payer en Especes sonnantes par chacun an, à Bureau ouvert, des Deniers de ladite Compagnie, à *[handwritten: usd[its] s[ieu]r Et Dame Poyrieu, Et après eux aud[it] s[ieu]r leur fils]* .......... sous Quittances, qui ne pourront estre passées que *[printed text cut off at foot of leaf]*

*(Foot right, manuscript notary signature:)* *M. Bouttra[ys?]* *(with paraph)*

*(Foot left, faint manuscript:)* *le 1. [illegible]*

*(Left margin, manuscript approbation note, largely illegible:)* *[illegible] ... dix* *(with paraph)*

---

*(Right margin, manuscript accretion notes, in later cursive; readings of the tontine numbers are uncertain:)*

*Inventaire soixante quatorze* *(with paraph)*

*Le present Contrat en r[e]presente d'Trois cent vingt livres de rente viagere, le num[éro] 20749[?] l'un de ceux porté au present Contrat ayant gagné quarante cinq livres de rente viagere par le tirage de la lotterie d'accroissement de lad[ite] Compagnie des Indes du dix neuf juin mil sept cent Cinquante quatre, ainsy qu'il paroit par une liste imprimée des gagnans de lad[ite] lotterie signée des s[ieu]rs Sindic et directeurs de lad[ite] Compagnie, en consequence de laquelle j'ai fait la presente mention et autant sur la minute, et l'un et l'autre porté sur un carnet subrogé à la pratique de m[aîtr]e [illegible]* *(with paraph and flourish)*

*La Rente portée au present Contrat en cette [augmentation] est de trois cent soixante cinq livres, au moyen de ce que le n[umér]o 20748 compris aud[it] Contrat y a gagné quarante cinq livres de rente viagere par le tirage* *[illegible / continues off the torn edge]*

*(Top left, date:)* 13 January 1725.

*(Engraved tax stamp:)* **STAMP OF THE NOTARIES — 13 sols 4 deniers — GENERALITY OF PARIS**

*(Above centre:)* born 27 October 1717

*(Second stamp:)* **First [sheet] of Expedition, 4. — Additional sheets, [per] livre.**

*(Upper right file note:)* Monsieur and Madame Poyrieu. No. 336.

**T**O all those who shall see these present Letters, Gabriel-Jérôme de Bullion, Knight, Count Desclimont, Field Colonel (Mestre de Camp) of the Regiment of Provence Infantry, Councillor of the King in all his Councils, Provost of the City, Provostry and Viscounty of Paris, GREETING. We make known that before the Masters *[Et Jean Gaschieu]*, Councillors of the King, Notaries, Keepers of the Records and Keepers of the Seal of His Majesty at the Châtelet of Paris, the undersigned, were present *[Étienne Demeunier the younger]*, Esquire, ...... Syndic of the Company of the Indies, and *[Sieur François Mouchard and Vincent Pierre Fromaget, Esquire]*,

Directors of the said Company; who, by virtue of the Decree of the King's Council of State of 15 February 1724, by which His Majesty granted to the said Company the exclusive privilege of conducting, throughout the extent of the Kingdom, various Lotteries; and in execution of the Resolution of 13 December of the said year, taken in the general Assembly of Administration of the said Company, concerning the Lottery composed of Prizes payable, some in Money and the others in Life Annuities (Rentes Viagères), which are to form a body of Tontine of Twenty-eight thousand seven hundred and fifty Numbers, each of them being subject to accretion (accroissement) in proportion to the deaths of the Annuitants (Rentiers) interested in the said Lottery; that is to say, for one half to the profit of the said Company, and for the other half to those of the surviving Annuitants whom the drawing shall favour in the Lotteries which are to be drawn annually and successively. The which Life Annuities, which shall be charged upon the funds of the said Company, the said Sieurs Syndic and Directors have power to constitute both to the benefit of the Subjects of His Majesty and of Foreigners, to whom the payment of the Arrears and of the Accretions must be made even should they reside outside the Kingdom, and even in time of war, without the said Annuities being liable to be cut down or seized for any cause whatsoever, not even for the King's own moneys and affairs, in conformity with the Decree of 20 June 1724, as is set forth more fully in the said Resolution, by which it is permitted to the purchasers of the said Annuities to have the Contracts made out under the name of such persons as they shall choose, so as to enjoy them, both by themselves and by those whom they shall name upon their Receipts (Quittances), during the life of the persons upon whose head (teste) the Constitutions shall have been placed. The said Sieurs Syndic and Directors, appearing, by virtue of the said Resolutions and Decrees of the Council of 15 February and 20 June 1724, have sold, created and constituted, settled and assigned by these presents; and have promised, for and in the name of the said Company of the Indies, to warrant against all troubles and other hindrances whatsoever, to

*[Master Charles Claude Poyrieu, Esquire, Councillor-Secretary of the King, Receiver-General of the finances of Orléans, and Dame Elizabeth Louise Mollée his wife, to be enjoyed by them and by the survivor of them, upon the head and during the life of Louis François Poyrieu their son, who shall enjoy it after the death of his said father and mother — the said sieur and dame Poyrieu, she being authorized by the said sieur her husband for the purpose of these presents, dwelling at Paris, Rue Thévenot, who this day accept as Purchasers — Two hundred and seventy-five [livres]]*

of Life Annuity; which Annuity the said Sieurs Syndic and Directors, appearing for and in the name of the said Company of the Indies, promise to cause to be delivered and paid in ringing coin (espèces sonnantes) each year, at the open Office (Bureau), out of the moneys of the said Company, to *[the said sieur and dame Poyrieu, and after them to the said sieur their son]* .......... under Receipts, which may only be given *[printed text cut off at the foot of the leaf]*

*(Notary's signature at foot right:)* M. Bouttra[ys?]

*(Left-margin approbation note, largely illegible)*

---

*(Right-margin accretion notes, added later; the tontine numbers cited are uncertain readings:)*

Inventory seventy-four.

The present Contract now represents Three hundred and twenty livres of life annuity, number 20749[?] being one of those carried on the present Contract, having won forty-five livres of life annuity by the drawing of the accretion lottery of the said Company of the Indies of the nineteenth of June one thousand seven hundred and fifty-four, as appears by a printed list of the winners of the said lottery signed by the Syndic and directors of the said Company, in consequence of which I have made the present notation, and the like upon the minute, both being entered in a register, [I being] subrogated to the practice of Master [illegible].

pages.description: This is a C. Perpetual Mortgage Debenture, No. 291, for £100, issued by The Liverpool Corn Trade Association, Limited, and carrying interest at 3¾ per cent per annum. Incorporated under the Companies' Acts 1862 to 1893, with capital of £60,000 in 400 shares of £150 each and a registered office at 8, Brunswick Street, Liverpool, the Association issued the debenture under the authority of Clause 54 of its Articles and a board resolution of 26 May 1897, as part of a £100,000 issue; it is given under the Common Seal in June 1897 and signed by the chairman, a director, and the secretary, Edward Bridson. As a perpetual mortgage debenture, the instrument pledges the Association's whole property and effects, present and future, as security for borrowings that funded the trade body's premises and operations in Liverpool's great grain market. The engraved Gothic blackletter masthead and dense classical border evoke the mercantile gravitas of a Victorian commercial corporation, lending the printed obligation the look of institutional permanence its 'perpetual' terms promise.

This is a perpetual mortgage debenture, numbered 291, of the Liverpool Corn Trade Association, Limited, issued to George Grossman for £100 sterling and signed by Edward Briggs, Secretary. The printed conditions establish it as one of a series of "C." perpetual debentures securing principal not exceeding £100,000 in all, charged on the Association's property and bearing interest not above £5 per centum per annum. Issued at Liverpool, the great corn-importing port of late-Victorian Britain, the instrument let a self-governing trade association raise long-dated capital from its own members rather than a bank, the perpetual form fixing a permanent charge in place of a maturing loan. Handwritten endorsements trace its passage: on George Grossman's death his sons take it under letters of administration, Ernest Clifford Grossman of Great Crosby receives the transfer in June 1919, and Hannah Jones, spinster, of West Derby acquires it in 1933. The austere engraved frame and blackletter title eschew allegory, presenting the bond as a sober commercial covenant. (Reverse of the certificate, with conditions printed below.)

description: A handwritten Dutch notarial certificate drawn by Victor Hendrik Hoogenbergh, a Dutch public notary admitted to practise in London, dated London, the 16th of March 1798. title: State of Massachusetts Bay Commodity-Indexed Treasury Note
description: A printed and manuscript interest-bearing treasury note of the State of Massachusetts-Bay, dated the first day of January, 1780. In behalf of the State, the subscriber in the Office of Treasurer promises to pay Elisha Curtis, or his order, the sum of two hundred and fifty-five pounds with interest at six percent a year, on or before the first day of March 1783. Both principal and interest were payable not in a fixed sum but in a greater or lesser sum, according as a fixed market basket, five bushels of corn, sixty-eight and four-sevenths pounds of beef, ten pounds of sheep's wool, and sixteen pounds of sole leather, should then cost in the current money of the State. The note records that this basket then cost about one hundred and thirty pounds, thirty-two and a half times what the same goods commanded under the price schedule of the 1777 Act to prevent Monopoly and Oppression. It was issued under a February 1780 act to supply the Treasury and meet the State's quota of the Continental Army. The Treasurer's signature is struck through, marking redemption.
creator: State of Massachusetts Bay (Treasurer; Committee)
notes: State of Massachusetts Bay interest-bearing state note, £230. Payable to Elisha Curtis. January 1, 1780. Interest 6% p.a., payable quarterly. Pursuant to Act authorizing additional taxation. Signed by Committee and Treasurer. Revolutionary War Massachusetts state finance.

title: Mexican Five Per Cent Deferred Stock Bond, London
description: An engraved bearer certificate for £500 sterling of Mexican Five Per Cent Deferred Stock, issued in London on 30 September 1837 under the hand of Don Agustín de Iturbide, Chargé d'Affaires for the Republic of Mexico, and countersigned by the agents for the conversion of the Mexican foreign debt. Interest runs only from 1 October 1847, and the stock is convertible at the holder's option into a land warrant for 2,000 acres. A presidential decree of 12 April 1837 created a National Consolidated Fund at five percent to absorb the whole external debt, terms a London bondholders' meeting accepted on 5 September 1837; surrendered deferred bonds, receipts and dividend warrants were exchanged here, half into this deferred stock and half into the consolidated fund. A full coupon sheet remains attached.

title: Share Subscription Contract for the Ostend Company
description: A printed and manuscript forward contract in shares of the Generale Keijserlijke Indische Compagnie, the Ostend Company, executed at Antwerp and dated in the printed close 10 November 1729. The contract binds the undersigned subscriber, having received a cash premium, to deliver and transfer six shares at 70 percent on the first available transfer-day, the agreement standing as an option to 1 August 1730. It pledges the seller's person and goods under Antwerp law, and an embossed armorial seal bearing the motto DUM SPIRO SPERO crowns the sheet. The company had been chartered by Emperor Charles VI in 1722 to trade to the Indies from the Austrian Netherlands. Issued on a stock form sold by the Antwerp printer Alexander Everaerts and engraved by Petrus van Pinxen.

title: New York State Per Cent Stock Certificate, Albany
description: A New York State "Per Cent Stock" certificate, a funded public-debt obligation issued by the Comptroller's Office at Albany and dated 10 October 1815. It acknowledges that the People of the State of New York owe Walter Perry of the State of Connecticut, or his assigns, the sum of three thousand dollars, bearing interest at seven per centum a year and payable quarterly on the first Mondays of January, April, July and October. title: Notarial Deed of the Demerara Plantation Negotiatie ("The Garden of Eden" and "The Kitty"), Amsterdam
description: A printed and manuscript notarial deed passed on 4 March 1817 before Everard Cornelis Bondt, public notary at Amsterdam, governing a negotiatie, a planters' mortgage-loan fund, of three hundred thousand guilders divided into shares of one thousand guilders each, of which two hundred ninety-four remain outstanding. The loan is secured upon the plantations "The Garden of Eden" and "The Kitty" on the east coast of the river Demerary in the Colony of Demerara, held by Thomas Cuming, with Cornelis Frymersum and his son acting through the firm C. Frymersum en Zoon as directors, and a broker and a merchant serving as commissioners. Such funds channelled Amsterdam capital into West Indian estates worked by enslaved people, the land and the enslaved pledged as collateral.
creator: Everard Cornelis Bordt (Notaris); C. Frymersum en Zoon (Directie)
notes: Lollenpolder en Hassendael Negotiatie legal agreement. Amsterdam, March 4, 1817. Notary Everard Cornelis Bordt. Parties: Cornelis Freymerius, Thomas Cuming (vice-agent), Werbard van Vloter Aanraede and Siek Jan Voombergh (Commissioners). 292 shares. Registered Amsterdam February 21, 1817.

# Document Transcription

**Original (Dutch):**

Op den vierden Maart des jaars achtien honderd zeventien; compareerden voor Mr. EVERARD CORNELIS BONDT, Openbaar Notaris te Amsterdam resideerednde, en voor de ondergenoemde getuigen.

De Heer CORNELIS FRYMERSUM, Koopman, wonende binnen deze Stad op de Keizersgracht tusschen de Leliegracht en Heerengracht, negotieernde onder de firma van C. FRYMERSUM en ZOON, en alzoo voor en in den naam van dezelvfe zijne firma van C. FRYMERSUM en ZOON, als Directeuren van de negotiatie groot dicemaal honderd duizend guldens, ten laste van den Heer THOMAS CUMING, onder verband van deszelfs Plantaadjen THE GARDEN OF EDEN EN THE KITTY; in de Kolonie Demerory geleegen; in den jaare seventien honderd twee-en-negentig, onder directie van den Heer SEBASTIAAN VAN NOOTEN JANES, allier opgerijgt.

En de Heeren DIRK WERNARD VAN VLOTEN ABRAHAMES; Makelaar, allier woonachtig op de Heerengracht bij de Vijzèlstraat, en DIRK JAN VOOMBERGH, Koopman, allier woonachtig in de Nieuwe Doelenstrat; beide in qualiteit als Commissarissen der voorschrevene Negotiatie.

Te kunnen gevende: Dat overeengkomdig de gemmaakte fehlkkingen niet den Heer THOMAS CUMING voornemoed, en de qualificatie der houders van de groote meerderheid der twee honderd vier-en-negentig overgeblevene Aandaclen, ieder van daizend guldens, in de voorschrevene Negotiatie, de hier voregenomelde Plantaadje genaamd THE GARDEN OF EDEN, geleegen op de Oost-kust van de rivier Demerory, met alle derzelver gebouwen, haven en verdere toebehooeren, op den achtlen Augustus des jaars achtien honderd vijftien, ten overlslans van Commissarissen van het Hof van crimineeele en civiele Justitie van de Kolonie Demerory en Essequebo, is goedeord, getransporteerd en in vollen vrijen eigendom overgegeven aan en te behoeve van de Heeren CORNELIS FRYMERSUM en CORNELIS FRYMERSUM Jr Jozor, negotieernde onder de firma van CORNELIS FRYMERSUM en ZOON, van Amsterdam, in derzelver qualiteit als Directeuren van zekere leening, gevestigd op de Plantaadjen KITTY EN GARDEN OF EDEN; zoo als blijkt uit het bij hun Heeren Comparanten ontvangene authentieke affidavit van het voormelde transport, waarop gefchreven staat:

"Geregistreerd te Amsterdam den zee en twintigten Febr. 1817, D. S. f. 179 verfo, vak 3 en 4. ontvangen met de Verhoog. negeri "en vijftig en 1 Cents (getteekend BONDAM."

En dat de Heeren Comparanten als nu, ter verdere voldoening aan den wil en het verlangen der voormelde houders van Aandaclen, met overleg van zooladige drie Heeren geinteressecrden in de voorschrevene negotiatie, welke voor het groothste getal Aandaclen tot de gezegde qualificatie hebben geoconcurreerd, hebben bepaald en vastgesteld, zoo als zij verklaren te bepalen en vaststelllen bij deren:

Dat de hier voregenomelde, als nu aan de houders der voorschrevene twee honderd vier-en-negentig Aandaclen in gemeenschaftspelijken eigendom toebehoorde Plantaadije THE GARDEN OF EDEN, met alle derzelver gebouwen, haven en verdere toebehooeren; en al wat werder tot het fonds der Associatio behoerende zijn mag, zal worden gereegerd en geadministreerd door de Heeren C. FRYMERSUM en ZOON, Kooplieden te Amsterdam, als Directeuren van het fonds der Plantaadije THE GARDEN OF EDEN, golegen

---

**English Translation:**

On the fourth day of March in the year eighteen hundred seventeen; appeared before Mr. EVERARD CORNELIS BONDT, Public Notary residing in Amsterdam, and before the hereinafter named witnesses.

Mr. CORNELIS FRYMERSUM, Merchant, residing within this City on the Keizersgracht between the Leliegracht and Heerengracht, negotiating under the firm name of C. FRYMERSUM and ZOON, and thus on behalf of and in the name of his said firm C. title: Poyaisian Land Grant
description: A bilingual English and Spanish land-grant certificate, Class C, conveying 400 acres in "Poyais Proper," dated London, 28 April 1834, issued under the hand of Gregor MacGregor, styling himself "Cazique of Poyais," and countersigned at London by trustees appointed for the exchange and redemption of the outstanding Poyaisian securities. MacGregor's grant is subscribed at Edinburgh. The sheet reproduces the purported original grant from the Mosquito Shore before promising the bearer a regular title to any unappropriated land, subject to an annual quit rent of one cent per acre payable each 24 December. Poyais was an invented Central American republic, and the certificate belongs to the winding-up of the scheme a decade after it drew British capital.

pages.description: A bilingual English/Spanish land-grant certificate (Class C) conveying 400 acres in "Poyais Proper," issued under the hand of Gregor MacGregor, styling himself "Cazique of Poyais," and countersigned at London by trustees appointed for the exchange and redemption of the outstanding Poyaisian securities. Dated London, 28 April 1834, with MacGregor's grant subscribed at Edinburgh, the sheet reproduces the purported original grant from the Mosquito Shore before promising the bearer a regular title to any unappropriated land, subject to an annual quit rent of one cent per acre payable each 24 December. Poyais was the imaginary Central American republic MacGregor invented to draw British capital after South American independence; the crest's motto, NESCIUS VINCI ("not knowing how to be conquered"), lends spurious sovereignty to one of the era's most notorious financial deceptions, here being wound up a decade on.

The reverse (endorsement side) of a Poyaisian Land Grant certificate for 400 acres, issued in London under Gregor MacGregor — self-styled “Cazique of Poyais” — as part of the notorious Poyais scheme, a fraud that sold settlers and investors title to land in a non-existent Central American country. Folded for filing, the certificate shows a printed docket panel headed “POYAISIAN LAND GRANT” with the Poyais arms (a crowned shield flanked by a unicorn and lion, with flags) and the motto “Nescius vinci,” the denomination “400 Acres,” and the grant’s class (Class C) and number. Manuscript initials and signatures of the issuing trustees appear below. It is the verso of a Class C grant, matching the Poyaisian Land Grant recorded at goetzmann0506.

# ENGLISH TRANSLATION / SUMMARY:

**PRICE-CURRENT OF SECURITIES.** Year 1822. Amsterdam, Thursday, 16 May. No. 39.

A printed Amsterdam stock-exchange price list quoting bid-and-ask ranges for three trading days (14, 15 and 16 May); the 16th fell on a holiday (*Feestdag*), so only the 14th and 15th are priced. The sheet is arranged by issuer and by country.

**United Netherlands** — the active and deferred national debt, syndicate bonds, and Netherlands bank-notes; the loans of the Treasury of the City of Amsterdam (negotiations of 1791–1819, redeemable, some payable in bank-money or cash); and Middelburg obligations.

**Domestic private negotiations** — shares and certificates in Dutch funds and infrastructure through named banking houses (van Harpen & Pluym & Backer; Mercker & van Ophoven; Ketwich & Voombergh), including the Rhineland negotiation, the Muidersluis, the Amstelveen road, the Slooten causeway, the ceded East-Frisian domains, the Society for Beneficence (Vlaer & Kol, Utrecht), the Nieuwe Diep & Koegras and Groote Wegen works, the Linge–Steenenhoek canal, and shipping and lands in Overyssel.

**Foreign negotiations:**
- **America** — United States federal debt placed through the Amsterdam houses of Van Staphorst (3% and 6% funds, 1791 issues), Daniel Crommelin & Sons (deferred and "liquidated debts"), Texier, Angely & Massac, Croese & Co., and Stadnitski & van Heukelom (certificates of liquidated debts and obligations on American lands).
- **Russia** — Hope & Co. obligations, inscriptions in the Grand Book (in paper and in silver), and Hamburg administration certificates.
- **Denmark** — toll, crown, loan-and-exchange-bank, and Asiatic Company obligations, and the National Bank.
- **Austria** — Vienna Bank obligations and metalliques through Goll & Co., Hope & Co., and J. Osy & Son; Vienna Bank shares; the 1820 loan and the 37½-million loan.
- **Italy / Sicily** — Milan monte certificates (Saportas); Neapolitan consolidated debt (Lamaison & Bouwer).
- **Spain** — obligations via Echenique & Co. and Hope & Co.; the 1820 Paris loan; premium-bills; vales reales.
- **Great Britain** — India and Bank stock, South Sea annuities, and 3% and 4% Consols (settlement 12 Aug. 1822).
- **France** — inscriptions in the Grand Book deliverable at Paris, liquidation acknowledgements, and the City of Paris premium loan (bank shares via Buys & Kerkhoven).
- **Lordships of Count Bentinck**, the **Three English Princes**, the **Grand Duchy of Baden** (Goll & Sons, Frankfurt), and **Colombia** (London obligations).

**Exchange and specie rates of Amsterdam (15 May)** — bill rates on Madrid, Bilbao, Cadiz, Seville, Lisbon, Oporto, Naples, Venice, Livorno, Genoa, Paris, Bordeaux, London, Hamburg, Vienna, Augsburg, Frankfurt, Berlin and St. Petersburg, followed by quotations for gold coin (guineas, sovereigns, louis-d'or, bar gold) and silver coin (Mexican dollars, French and Brabant crowns, five-franc pieces, rixdollars).

title: Middelburg Plantation Bond for Essequibo and Demerara
description: A handwritten plantation mortgage bond, No. 90, drawn on the Register of Middelburg in Zeeland and dated at Middelburg the first of January 1760. It is signed by Kornelis van den Helm Boddaert as director for the money-lenders of various plantations in the colony of Essequibo and Demerary, issued under the printed plan of mortgages secured upon the colonial estates and authenticated with the company seal. It acknowledges a capital of six hundred guilders courant at five percent yearly interest. Such bonds belonged to the Dutch system of plantation loans, by which mortgages on West Indian estates worked by enslaved people were bundled and sold to investors at home. Later endorsements record its long secondary life.
creator: Kornelis van den Helm Boddaert; Middelburg Administration

title: French Life Annuity on Four Million Livres
description: A French royal life annuity, a partly printed and partly manuscript receipt issued by Antoine Pâris, Conseiller du Roy and Garde du Trésor Royal, acknowledging receipt at Paris in 1723 of a principal of 1,175 livres in exchange for a yearly annuity of forty-seven livres, four percent of the principal. The annuity belongs to the four millions of livres raised under the edict of July 1723, charged on the tailles and other impositions, and is constituted for Simonne Pinault, widow of Claude Rabaroux, upon the life of Simonne Agathe Rabaroux. A marginal note records the annuity's later reduction to 23 livres 10 sols under the edict of November 1726.
creator: Jean Antoine Paris, Conseiller du Roy

title: Royal Life Annuity Contract, Hôtel de Ville of Paris
description: A partly printed, partly manuscript contract for a French royal life annuity on one head, dated 26 July 1759 and passed before the notaries and gardes-scel of His Majesty at the Châtelet de Paris and the Prévôt des marchands et échevins of the city, Jean-Baptiste-Élie Camus de Pontcarré. It executes the edict of November 1758, registered by the Parlement on 12 December following, which authorized the sale of three million six hundred thousand livres of life annuities, charged by preference upon the royal treasury and payable through the garde du trésor royal. Annuities could be constituted on one or two heads, with returns graduated by the holder's age into six classes, from one hundred livres per thousand of capital in the first class to one hundred forty in the sixth, and eighty per thousand on two heads. The terms recruited even foreigners and members of religious orders, with the inducement that the rents be exempt from the two vingtièmes, the deux sols pour livre, and the droits d'aubaine, bâtardise et confiscation. The manuscript docket names the holder as the Comtesse de Pons-Saint-Maurice.
creator: Notaires du Châtelet de Paris; Jean-Baptiste-Élie Canus de Pontcaillé
notes: Rente Viagère Sur une Tête, Édit de Novembre 1738, Première Classe. Nominee: Comtesse de Saint-Hermaurice. Issued July 26, 1739, Paris. Notaires du Châtelet. Marchands et Echevins financing (4,000 livres capital each). French royal life annuity under Louis XV.
transcription:
# Royal Life Annuity Contract on One Head, Hôtel de Ville of Paris (Edict of November 1758) — Transcription

## Original:

(Handwritten docket, top left):
Mᵈᵉ La Comtesse de Pons St Maurice
26. Juillet 1759

(Engraved oval seal, center): **GEN. DE PARIS** / [ornamental arms, part illegible] / [...] 3 SOLS

(Right margin, large handwritten flourish + printed word): 1.ᵉ **Classe.**

**RENTES VIAGÈRES SUR UNE TÊTE.**

**Édit de Novembre 1758.**

(Left margin, handwritten): S.ʳ Grosset / ad plias [illegible marginal note]

**PAR-DEVANT** les Conseillers du Roi, Notaires, Gardes-notes & Gardes-scel de Sa Majesté au Châtelet de Paris, soussignés, furent présens, M.ʳᵉ **JEAN-BAPTISTE-ÉLIE CAMUS DE PONTCARRÉ**, seigneur de Viarme, Seugy, Belloy & autres lieux, Conseiller d'État, Prevôt des Marchands;

(Handwritten insertions naming the échevins):
Jean François Bralles Ecuyer Con.ᵉʳ du Roy au l'Hôtel de Ville
Jean Baptiste Vernay Ecuyer.
Jean Olivier Boutray Ecuyer Con.ᵉʳ du Roy quartenier
Et Jean André [surname illegible] Ecuyer avocat au Parlement et ès Conseils du Roy

**Tous Échevins de cette ville de Paris.**

**LESQUELS** ont dit que Sa Majesté, par son édit du mois de novembre 1758, enregistré au Parlement le 12 décembre suivant, auroit ordonné que par les Commissaires que Sa Majesté nommeroit à cet effet, il seroit vendu & aliéné auxdits sieurs Prevôt des Marchands & Échevins, trois millions six cens mille livres actuelles & effectives de rentes viagères, à prendre sur tous les deniers provenans des droits d'aides, gabelles & cinq grosses fermes, que Sa Majesté a affectés, obligés & hypothéqués par préférence à la partie du trésor royal, au payement des arrérages desdites rentes, qui pourroient être acquises, soit sur une seule tête, à divers taux, suivant l'âge des acquéreurs, ou sur deux têtes indistinctement, à raison de huit pour cent par an.

Que les constitutions particulières desdites rentes, qui ne pourroient être moindres sur une seule tête de cinquante livres, & sur deux têtes de quarante livres de jouissance annuelle, seroient faites par lesdits sieurs Prevôt des Marchands & Échevins, à ceux qui en auroient fourni les capitaux en deniers comptans entre les mains du sieur Savalete de Magnanville, Garde du Trésor royal, pour en jouir par les acquéreurs leur vie durant, soit sur leur tête, soit sur celle ou celles de toutes autres personnes que bon leur sembleroit, & que les contrats seroient passés par-devant tels Notaires du Châtelet de Paris que lesdits acquéreurs voudroient choisir, qui seroient tenus de leur délivrer lesdits contrats sans frais.

Que les rentes qui seroient acquises sur une tête, seroient réparties en six classes, suivant l'âge des acquéreurs; la première, depuis la naissance jusqu'à cinquante ans accomplis; la deuxième, depuis cinquante ans jusqu'à cinquante-cinq; la troisième, depuis cinquante-cinq ans jusqu'à soixante; la quatrième, depuis soixante ans jusqu'à soixante-cinq; la cinquième, depuis soixante-cinq ans jusqu'à soixante-dix; & la sixième, depuis soixante-dix ans jusqu'à soixante-quinze ans & au dessus.

Que les rentes sur deux têtes seroient acquises sans distinction d'âge ni de classe; & dans l'une comme dans l'autre espèce desdites rentes viagères, il seroit justifié de l'âge de ceux sur la tête desquels elles seroient constituées, par des extraits baptistaires ou actes équipolens, suivant & conformément à ce qui a été ci-devant prescrit en pareil cas; & qu'annuellement il seroit payé aux acquéreurs desdites rentes, pendant leur vie ou de ceux sur la tête desquels elles seroient constituées, savoir, pour les rentes sur une seule tête & pour chaque constitution de mille livres en capital dans la première classe, cent livres; dans la deuxième, cent cinq livres; dans la troisième, cent dix livres; dans la quatrième, cent vingt livres; dans la cinquième, cent trente livres; & dans la sixième, cent quarante livres: Et pour les rentes sur deux têtes quatre-vingt livres, aussi pour chaque constitution de mille livres en capital.

Que toutes sortes de personnes indistinctement, de quelque âge, sexe, qualité & condition qu'elles puissent être, même les religieux & religieuses qui, suivant leur Ordre, peuvent avoir quelque pécule, pourroient acquérir lesdites rentes; le survivant des pères & mères qui les auroient acquises sous le nom de leurs enfans, en jouiroit, sans être tenu dans aucun cas de leur en rendre compte; les enfans & autres qui entreroient en religion & feroient profession dans quelque Ordre que ce puisse être, conserveroient par forme de pension alimentaire, celles qui auroient été par eux acquises, ou qui ayant été constituées sur leur tête leur auroient été abandonnées avant leur profession: Comme aussi, que même ceux qui sont demeurans hors du royaume, pays, terres & seigneuries de l'obéissance de Sa Majesté, pourroient, ainsi que ses propres sujets, acquérir lesdites rentes, encore bien qu'ils fussent sujets de Princes & États avec lesquels Elle est ou pourroit être en guerre; en conséquence, Sa Majesté a voulu que lesdites rentes & les arrérages qui en seroient dûs au jour du décès de ces rentiers, soient exemptes de toutes lettres de marque & de représailles, droits d'aubaine, bâtardise, confiscation, ou autres qui pourroient lui appartenir, auxquels Sa Majesté a renoncé, conformément à l'édit du mois de décembre 1674 & autres subséquens.

Que lesdites rentes seroient exemptes de la retenue des deux Vingtièmes, des Deux sols pour livre

(Signature, bottom): M.ᵉ Gervais no.ᵉ [notaire; surname reads "Gervai(s)"]

---

## English Translation:

(Handwritten docket, top left):
Madame the Countess of Pons Saint-Maurice
26 July 1759

(Engraved oval seal, center): GENERALITY OF PARIS / [...] 3 SOLS

(Right margin): 1st Class.

**LIFE ANNUITIES ON ONE HEAD.**

**Edict of November 1758.**

(Left margin, handwritten): Sieur Grosset / [illegible marginal note]

**BEFORE** the Councillors of the King, Notaries, Keepers of the Minutes & Keepers of the Seal of His Majesty at the Châtelet of Paris, the undersigned, were present Maître **JEAN-BAPTISTE-ÉLIE CAMUS DE PONTCARRÉ**, lord of Viarme, Seugy, Belloy & other places, Councillor of State, Provost of the Merchants;

(Handwritten insertions naming the aldermen):
Jean François Bralles, Esquire, Councillor of the King at the Hôtel de Ville
Jean Baptiste Vernay, Esquire.
Jean Olivier Boutray, Esquire, Councillor of the King, quartenier [ward officer]
And Jean André [surname illegible], Esquire, advocate at the Parlement and in the Councils of the King

**All Aldermen of this city of Paris.**

**WHO** stated that His Majesty, by his edict of the month of November 1758, registered by the Parlement on the 12th of December following, had ordered that, through the Commissioners His Majesty should appoint to that effect, there should be sold & alienated to the said Provost of the Merchants & Aldermen three million six hundred thousand livres, actual & effective, of life annuities, to be taken upon all the revenues arising from the duties of the aides, the gabelles & the five great farms, which His Majesty has assigned, bound & mortgaged by preference to the account of the royal treasury, for the payment of the arrears of the said annuities, which might be acquired either upon a single head, at various rates according to the age of the purchasers, or upon two heads without distinction, at the rate of eight per cent per year.

That the individual constitutions of the said annuities, which could not be less than fifty livres upon a single head, & forty livres of annual enjoyment upon two heads, should be made by the said Provost of the Merchants & Aldermen to those who should have furnished the capital in ready money into the hands of the Sieur Savalete de Magnanville, Keeper of the Royal Treasury, to be enjoyed by the purchasers during their lifetime, whether upon their own head, or upon that or those of any other persons as should seem good to them, & that the contracts should be passed before such Notaries of the Châtelet of Paris as the said purchasers might choose, who should be bound to deliver the said contracts to them without charge.

That the annuities acquired upon one head should be divided into six classes according to the age of the purchasers: the first, from birth to fifty years completed; the second, from fifty to fifty-five; the third, from fifty-five to sixty; the fourth, from sixty to sixty-five; the fifth, from sixty-five to seventy; & the sixth, from seventy to seventy-five years & above.

That the annuities upon two heads should be acquired without distinction of age or class; & in the one as in the other kind of the said life annuities, the age of those upon whose head they should be constituted must be proved by baptismal extracts or equivalent acts, according & conformably to what has heretofore been prescribed in like cases; & that annually there should be paid to the purchasers of the said annuities, during their life or that of those upon whose head they should be constituted, namely, for annuities upon a single head & for each constitution of one thousand livres of capital: in the first class, one hundred livres; in the second, one hundred and five livres; in the third, one hundred and ten livres; in the fourth, one hundred and twenty livres; in the fifth, one hundred and thirty livres; & in the sixth, one hundred and forty livres: And for annuities upon two heads, eighty livres, also for each constitution of one thousand livres of capital.

That all sorts of persons without distinction, of whatever age, sex, quality & condition they may be, even religious men & women who, according to their Order, may hold some private means, might acquire the said annuities; the survivor of fathers & mothers who had acquired them in the name of their children should enjoy them, without being bound in any case to render account thereof to them; children & others who should enter religion & make profession in whatever Order it might be, should retain by way of alimentary pension those which had been acquired by them, or which, having been constituted upon their head, had been abandoned to them before their profession: Likewise, that even those who dwell outside the kingdom, lands, territories & lordships under the obedience of His Majesty might, like his own subjects, acquire the said annuities, even though they were subjects of Princes & States with which He is or might be at war; in consequence, His Majesty has willed that the said annuities & the arrears due thereon at the day of the death of these annuitants be exempt from all letters of marque & reprisal, rights of aubaine, bastardy, confiscation, or others that might belong to Him, to which His Majesty has renounced, conformably to the edict of the month of December 1674 & others subsequent.

That the said annuities should be exempt from the withholding of the two Twentieths, of the Two sols per livre

title: Republic of New Granada Deferred Bond
description: A £100 sterling bearer bond styled "Deferred," issued in London on 1 June 1845 by the Chargé d'Affaires of the Republic of New Granada under an agreement signed at Bogotá on 15 January 1845 between the Republic's Secretary of Finance, Juan Climaco Ordóñez, and Powles, Illingworth, Willson & Co., agents of the bondholders of the foreign debt of Colombia. By its terms New Granada acknowledges half of the loans contracted by the old Republic of Colombia in 1822 and 1824, exchanging new bonds for one-half of each Colombian bond surrendered. Interest is genuinely deferred: nothing falls due until 1 December 1861, and the rate climbs from one percent, rising a quarter-point yearly toward six, payable half-yearly at Baring, Brothers & Co. New Granada was the successor state to Gran Colombia.
creator: Republic of New Granada; Powles, Illingworth, Willson & Co.
