# Chilian 5 Per Cent Loan 1896 — Interest Coupon Sheet (N. M. Rothschild & Sons, London) — Transcription

## Original:

*(Layout: A horizontal sheet of detachable semi-annual interest coupons for bond serial No. 10,269 of the "Chilian 5 Per Cent Loan 1896." All coupons carry the same engraved wording, differing only in the due-date and the sequential coupon number printed as a large bold numeral. A finely engraved pale-green guilloche security ground repeats the microtext "CHILIAN FIVE PER CENT LOAN 1896" throughout each coupon, and the outer decorative borders repeat "CHILIAN 5 PER CENT LOAN 1896." Every coupon bears the serial number "10,269" twice and the value "£2.10.0." twice. The currency mark is an ornate pound sign; the shillings/pence form "2.10.0" = £2 10s 0d, i.e. one half-year of 5% interest on £100. The top row runs left-to-right; two ornamental engraved vignette panels close the right end of the sheet; one further coupon (No. 80) is detached at the lower right.)*

**Standard text printed on each coupon:**

title: Monte del Sale Share Transfer, Florence
description: A transfer certificate of shares in the Monte non vacabile del Sale della Città di Firenze, the non-redeemable salt fund of the Florentine public debt, dated 10 September 1693. The fund was erected by provision published in the Senate of the Forty-Eight on 12 September 1645. The certificate records the conveyance of 44½ luoghi from Pier Carlo Giraldini to Caterina Gianfigliazzi, widow Giraldini, each luogo carrying a capital value of 100 scudi and an annual rendita of 4 scudi paid quarter by quarter, a fixed 4 percent return on a perpetual, inheritable claim on salt-tax revenues. It was issued under the name of the Grand Duke of Tuscany and authenticated by the Protettori del Monte, their chancellor, and an affixed wax seal.
creator: Protettori del Monte del Sale, Firenze
notes: Monte non vacabile del Sale della Città di Firenze (Non-vacuous Salt Fund of Florence). Transfer of 44.5 luoghi to Caterina del fu Giov. Battista Gianfigliazzi (née Giraldini). Signed by Protettori del Monte. Wax seal at lower left. Florence, September 10, 1693. Grand Duchy of Tuscany.
transcription:
# Certificate of Transfer of Places in the Non-Redeemable Salt Fund of the City of Florence — Transcription

## Original (Italian):

*(Three engraved devices across the top: at left and right, ornamental foliate urns/vases; at center, the crowned Medici arms — a shield charged with the palle.)*

**NOi Protettori del Monte non vacabile del Sale della Città di Firenze,** eretto d'ordine del Serenissimo Gran Duca di Toscana nostro Signore, per la Prouisione pubblicata nell'Amplissimo Senato de' Quarant'otto il dì di 12. Settembre 1645. A tutti quelli, che vedranno la presente nostra facciamo piena, & indubitata fede, come [manoscritto: **La Sig.ra Caterina del già Sig.re Balt.re Giovan Battista Gianfigliazzi Vedova ne Giraldini**]

Apparisce [manoscritto: *segnatura, illeggibile*] ——— credit. al Libro di detto Monte segn. ——— di Luoghi [manoscritto: **Quarantaquattro e mezzo**]

di valuta di scudi cento per ogni luogo, con li frutti [manoscritto: **à suo favore decorsi, e da decorrere**] ——— come per Partito nostro di questo

in futuro risegnatili dal conto di [manoscritto: **Sig.r Pier Carlo Giraldini**] al quale si abbia relatione. Però annullando ogn'altra Patente fatta per

giorno al libro delle Permute a c. [manoscritto: **367** (?)] ammettiamo detta cessione, traslazione, e risegna, e per tenore della pre-

sente facciamo, e dichiariamo detta [manoscritto: **Sig.ra Caterina Gianfigliazzi ne Giraldini**] questa somma di luoghi del detto Monte,

credit. ——— di detto Monte di detti luoghi [manoscritto: **Quarantaquattro e mezzo**] che gli cediamo, & assegniamo con

annua rendita di scudi quattro per luogo da pagarsili frutti di tre Mesi in tre Mesi per rata, e con li Priuilegi, condi-

zioni, e dichiarazioni di che in detta Prouisione; Et in virtù della presente ordiniamo

al nostro Camarlengo presente, e che per li tempi sarà, che li paghi detti frutti di tre Mesi in tre Mesi: Et in fede ab-

biamo fatta la presente, quale sarà sottoscritta da vno di Noi Protettori, e dal nostro Cancelliere, e sigillata con il

nostro solito sigillo.

Dat. in Firenze nell'Vfizio del nostro Monte del Sale il dì [manoscritto: **10 Settembre 1693.**]

*(Signature, one of the Protectors:)* **Attilio Vettori uno de' Protettori**

*(Signature, the Chancellor, lower right:)* **Ottav.no Parigi Canc.** *[surname uncertain]*

*(Affixed wax seal in the lower-left corner, tan/beige, over a paper cover.)*

*(Note: the printed form's founding Provision is dated 12 September 1645; the manuscript execution of this transfer is dated 10 September 1693 — two distinct dates, consistent with the record description.)*

## English Translation:

*(Three engraved devices across the top: left and right ornamental foliate urns; center the crowned Medici arms with the palle.)*

**We, the Protectors of the Non-Redeemable Salt Fund of the City of Florence,** erected by order of the Most Serene Grand Duke of Tuscany our Lord, pursuant to the Provision published in the Most Ample Senate of the Forty-Eight on the 12th of September 1645. To all who shall see the present [instrument] we give full and undoubted faith that, as [manuscript: **the Lady Caterina, [daughter/widow] of the late Sir Baltasarre Giovan Battista Gianfigliazzi, Widow Giraldini**]

there appears [manuscript: *ledger mark, illegible*] ——— credited in the Book of the said Fund, marked ———, with Places [manuscript: **Forty-four and a half**]

of a value of one hundred scudi for each place, together with the interest [manuscript: **accrued and to accrue in her favour**] ——— as per Our Decree of this

date, herein reassigned from the account of [manuscript: **Sir Pier Carlo Giraldini**], to which reference shall be had. Therefore, annulling every other Patent made for

the day, in the Book of Exchanges at folio [manuscript: **367** (?)], we admit the said cession, transfer, and reassignment, and by tenor of the pre-

sent we make and declare the said [manuscript: **Lady Caterina Gianfigliazzi née Giraldini**] [holder of] this sum of places of the said Fund,

creditor ——— of the said Fund for the said places [manuscript: **Forty-four and a half**], which we cede and assign to her with

an annual return of four scudi per place, the interest to be paid quarter by quarter pro rata, and with the Privileges, condi-

tions, and declarations set forth in the said Provision; and by virtue of the present we order

our Chamberlain, both the present one and whoever shall hold the office in future, to pay her the said interest quarter by quarter. And in faith we

have made the present [instrument], which shall be subscribed by one of Us Protectors and by our Chancellor, and sealed with

our customary seal.

Given in Florence, in the Office of our Salt Fund, on the day [manuscript: **10 September 1693.**]

*(Signature, one of the Protectors:)* **Attilio Vettori, one of the Protectors**

*(Signature, the Chancellor:)* **Ottaviano Parigi, Chancellor** *[surname uncertain]*

# Ottoman Public Debt — "Series A" 1928 Bond for Annuities in Arrear (Reverse: Coupon sheet and Contract Extracts) — Transcription

## Original:

(This is the reverse of an Ottoman Public Debt "Series A" 1928 bond representing the *Annuities in Arrear*. The sheet is divided into two zones: at the left, a grid of detachable redemption coupons (*Gutscheine / Senedat*), each printed bilingually in German and Latin-script Turkish; at the right, the "Extracts from the Contract" printed in four parallel columns — **French**, **English**, **German**, and **Turkish** (Latin script). Several red circular stamps reading *DETTE PUBLIQUE OTTOMANE / OTTOMAN PUBLIC DEBT* with an "OD" monogram overprint the sheet. A folded corner at the lower left shows one coupon printed in English. The scan is low-resolution and much of the French, German and Turkish column body text is blurred; the English column is transcribed in full below as the legible representative text, with the parallel column headings and figures given as printed.)

---

**Column headings (four parallel columns, left to right):**

**EXTRAITS DU CONTRAT** (French)

**EXTRACTS FROM THE CONTRACT** (English)

**AUSZÜGE AUS DEM VERTRAGE** (German)

**MUKAVELENAMEDEN MÜSTAHREÇ AHKÂM** (Turkish)

---

### English column (transcribed in full):

**EXTRACTS FROM THE CONTRACT**

**Art. IV.**
**Prorogation and mode of repayment of the Annuities in Arrear**

§ 5. — The *Bonds representing Arrears* will be of three Series:

"*Series A*" will be composed of 766,864 Bonds of the nominal amount of T£. 22, or £. 20, or Fr. Frs. 500, or their multiples.

"*Series B*" will be composed of 64,412 Bonds of the nominal amount of Fr. Frs. 1,000, or their multiples, liable to repayment with the increase provided for in Article XII.

"*Series C*" will be composed of 245,430 Bonds of the nominal amount of Fr. Frs. 1,000, or their multiples.

These Bonds shall be printed in the Turkish, French, English and German Languages.

They shall be to bearer.

(*The provisional figures indicated in the present paragraph at the time of the drawing up of the Contract, have been adjusted later on and replaced by definite figures which are printed on the face of this Bond.*)

§ 6. — Their redemption shall take place by way of repayment in 30 yearly instalments the amount of which will be fixed in conformity with the provisions of the present Contract. For that purpose the new Bonds will have attached to them 29 redemption coupons, and the Bond itself must be surrendered upon payment of the thirtieth yearly instalment.

§ 7. — The yearly redemption coupons will be payable, pursuant to the provisions of Article XII, on the 25th November in each year — the first coupon being that of the 25th November 1929 — at Stamboul, Paris, London, Berlin, Brussels, Rome and, if necessary, at other places to be indicated by the Council, in conformity with § 11:

a) "*Series A*", in T£, or £, or French Frs.;

b) "*Series B*", in French Frs., plus the increase provided for in Article XII;

c) "*Series C*", in French Frs.

The currency for the payment of the coupons of "*Series A*" (Turkish Pts., or Sh., or Fr. Frs.) will be fixed at each date of maturity by the *Council* in conformity with the provisions of Article XVI, § 7.

At places of payment where the local currency differs from the currency fixed by the *Council*, the Holders will receive the equivalent of this latter currency, in local currency, at the sight rate of exchange of the day of presentation of the coupons.

§ 8. — Redemption coupons not presented for payment within fifteen years from the date when they became payable will be forfeited in favour of the debtor States, in the proportion respectively in which each of these States will have contributed to the constitution of the fund forming the cover for the said coupons.

§ 12. — The new *Bonds* and their redemption coupons shall be at all time be exempt from all imposts, stamp duties and taxes in Turkey.

. . . . . . .

**Art. VI.**
**Total Annuities**

§ 1. — For the entire service of the annuities incumbent upon Turkey in respect of the long term Loans, and of the Treasury Bonds and the *Arrears*, extended as to time under the conditions laid down in Articles III and IV respectively, and comprising all the liabilities enumerated in Article X, the *Government* shall pay to the *Council* the following fixed total annuities:

(table — Periods / Duration / Amounts)

| Periods | Duration | Amounts |
|---|---|---|
| I. 7 years | from the 1st June 1929 to the 31st May 1936 | Gold T£ 2,000,000 |
| II. 6 years | from the 1st June 1936 to the 31st May 1942 | Gold T£ 2,380,000 |
| III. 5 years | from the 1st June 1942 to the 31st May 1947 | Gold T£ 2,780,000 |
| IV. 5 years | from the 1st June 1947 to the 31st May 1952 | Gold T£ 3,180,000 |
| — | from the 1st June 1952 onward | Gold T£ 3,400,000 |

until the portion of the total annuity of Gold T£ 3,400,000 allocated to the interest and redemption corresponds to the amounts indicated in the annexed Table No. 1 for the service of the interest and redemption of all the *Loans*, *Bonds for the Consolidation of the Treasury Bonds* and the *Bonds representing the Annuities in Arrear*.

From that date onward the total annuity to be paid by the *Government* shall be reduced progressively by the amount of the annuities relating to the various *Loans*, at the respective dates when they should be redeemed, according to the annexed Table, whether the said Loans be actually redeemed or not.

. . . . . . .

**Art. VII.**
**Assigned Revenues**

§ 1. — In order to secure the regular payment of the annuities fixed in Article VI, the *Government* assigns, for the duration of the present Contract, and to the extent of the amount of each current annuity:

a) for the period from the 1st June 1929 to the 1st June 1942: the gross receipts of the Customs duties and Consumption taxes collected at all the Custom Houses in the Districts (*Beche-mudirieh*) of Stamboul, Galata and Haïdar Pacha;

b) for the period subsequent to the 1st June 1942: the said gross receipts, with the addition of the gross receipts of the Customs duties and Consumption taxes collected at all the Custom Houses in the District of Samsoun.

The surplus of the assigned receipts shall remain at the free disposal of the *Government*, under the conditions provided in Article XVI.

(*See also paragraphs 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 of the same Article, and Articles VIII, XVI and XVII.*)

**Art. X.**
**General Provisions**

§ 1. — The fixed total annuities to be paid by the *Government*, from the 1st June 1929 onward, pursuant to Article VI, shall be applied by the *Council* to the various services of the Ottoman Public Debt, as regards the portion incumbent upon Turkey, in the order hereunder indicated:

a) in the first instance, and by way of preliminary deduction, the fixed amount agreed upon for the expenses of the *Council*;

b) secondly:
— the amount required for the annuity of interest on the long term *Loans* and on the *Bonds for the Consolidation of the Treasury Bonds*, calculated in accordance with the percentages indicated in Article XI, §§ 2, 3, 4 and 5;
— the amount required for the yearly payment in French Francs applicable to the service of the premiums, redemption and repurchases of the *Turkish Lottery Bonds*, pursuant to the provisions of Article II relating to the said Bonds;
— the amount required for the redemption of the *Bonds representing the Annuities in Arrear*, calculated in accordance with the percentages indicated in Article XII, § 1;
— the commissions allowed by the *Government* to the Financial Establishments for the foregoing services, and the various expenses incidental thereto;

the order in which the four aforesaid services are mentioned shall not imply any prior right whatsoever in favour of any one of them.

c) the surplus of the total annuities to be paid by the *Government* shall be applied to redemption under the conditions laid down in Article XIII, and to the payment of the commissions and expenses incidental thereto.

**Art. XII.**
**Service of repayment of the Bonds representing the Annuities in Arrear**

The yearly repayment devolving upon Turkey for the service of the yearly redemption coupons of the *Bonds representing the Annuities in Arrear* shall be taken by the *Council* out of the total annuities paid by Turkey, on the basis of the currency of the payment which it will have fixed, in accordance with Article XVI, as regards Series "*A*", and in French Francs, as regards Series "*B*" and "*C*", to be paid to the Holders under the following conditions:

a) *Series* "*A*". — These coupons — marked in T£, £ and French Frs. — shall be paid, in one of the optional currencies in accordance with the percentages hereunder, in relation to the thirtieth portion of the amortisation which they represent:

(table — Periods / Duration / Percentage payable)

| Periods | Duration | % |
|---|---|---|
| I. 7 years | From the 1st June 1929 to the 31st May 1936, i.e. seven annuities | 28 % |
| II. 6 years | From the 1st June 1936 to the 31st May 1942, i.e. six annuities | 44 % |
| III. 5 years | From the 1st June 1942 to the 31st May 1947, i.e. five annuities | 58 % |
| IV. 2 years | From the 1st June 1947 to the 31st May 1949, i.e. two annuities | 68 % |
| V. 3 years | From the 1st June 1949 to the 31st May 1952, i.e. three annuities | 90 % |
| — | From the 1st June 1952 until the complete extinction of the Bonds | 100 % |

**Art. XXX.**
**Drawing up of the Contract**

The present Contract is drawn up in the French Language and in as many copies as there are Parties to the Contract.

title: Ottoman Empire Unified Converted Debt Bond
description: A bearer bond of the 4 percent Unified Converted Debt of the Ottoman Empire, issued at Constantinople in 1903 under the administration of the Ottoman Public Debt Council. Each obligation carries a face value of 500 francs, equivalent to £20, drawn from a consolidated loan that reorganised the empire's defaulted external borrowings into a single uniform instrument. The certificate sets French and English columns to either side of a central Ottoman Turkish and Arabic text crowned by the Sultan's tughra.

Reverse, in green and red. Columns of decree extracts run in French, Ottoman, and English across the top. A central TABLEAU D'AMORTISSEMENT lists redemption draws. Three large vignettes below repeat the Fr. 500 / £20 denomination around a tughra; numbered coupons line the left margin. Page 2 of 2.

title: Hagenow Municipal Benzol-Value Bond
description: Inflation-era commodity-value bond (Benzolwert-Anleihe) issued by the Staedtisches Gas- und Elektrizitaetswerk (Municipal Gas and Electricity Works) of Hagenow in Mecklenburg, series Lit. C, bearing 5% interest. Rather than a fixed sum of money, the Schuldverschreibung is denominated in the monetary value of 50 (fuenfzig) kilograms of benzol (benzene), pegging the obligation to a real commodity instead of the collapsing paper Mark. Dated Hagenow, 30 July 1923, at the height of the German hyperinflation. Signed for Der Rat (the town council) and by the Stadtverordnetenvorsteher (chairman of the city assembly). The face carries a red diagonal cancellation overprint; the serial is Lit. C, No. 173 (read beneath the red cancellation overprint).

# English Translation:

**Announcement**

5% Benzene-Value Loan
of the
Municipal Gas and Electricity Works
Hagenow i. M.

The Municipal Gas and Electricity Works Hagenow i. M. is raising, with the approval of the City Council of Hagenow and the State Administration Council, a loan in the amount of 14,000 kilograms of benzene. The individual loan documents are denominated in the respective value of the benzene quantity contained therein. Pieces of 5, 10, and 50 kilograms of benzene will be issued. The pieces are made out to bearer. Each loan document is accompanied by 14 semi-annual interest coupons. The interest coupons are denominated in the respective value of half of 5% of the benzene quantity belonging to the corresponding loan document. Thus, for a loan document denominated at 10 kilograms of benzene, a semi-annual interest of 1/4 kilogram of benzene is given. The interest is paid semi-annually in arrears on January 2 and July 1 respectively upon submission of the interest coupons in gold. The loan to be announced will be calculated according to the last official benzene price from November and May respectively and will be published in the Hagenow District Gazette and in the Official Bulletin of the Mecklenburg-Schwerin Government Gazette.

The redemption of the loan begins from July 1, 1924 onwards with at least 2,000 kilograms of benzene annually through free purchase or by drawing. Payment of the drawn pieces occurs on January 2 and July 1 of each year, first on July 1, 1924. In 1930, payment is made for the drawn pieces not yet drawn by then. The price for benzene is determined in the same manner as for determining the respective interest amount. Notification of the drawn pieces is made in the Hagenow District Gazette and in the Official Bulletin of the Mecklenburg-Schwerin Government Gazette.

The city of Hagenow and the Municipal Gas and Electricity Works are liable for the loan.

The proceeds of the loan are designated for the establishment of a benzene recovery and waste heat utilization system at the City Gas Works Hagenow.

description: A municipal redemption-loan bond of the City of Rostock in Mecklenburg-Schwerin, Letter E, for 200 reichsmark, dated Rostock, 12 November 1927. title: Silesian Loan of Holy Roman Emperor Karl VI
description: AMSTERDAM. 5% Obligatie Fl.1000. black. No 1254. The Habsburg emperors were always short of money. A large refinancing operation was required by 1734, and Karl VI raised a loan with the Amsterdam banking-house of Willem Gideon Deutz. In guarantee, he offered the Silesia tribute fund, into which payments were made by the princes and nobles of Silesia (thus, the Silesian loan). As interest rates declined, a conversion operation was carried out in 1736. The new bonds, paying 5% interest, were for a total of 700.000 gulden. The new loan was very successful, and within two months had attracted all the capital needed. At first, interest was paid regularly from the contributions by the Silesian nobility. However, after 1742, things changed, when, after the war between Maria Theresia, daughter and successor of Karl VI, and Frederick the Great of Prussia led to Prussian rule over the Silesian territories. There were no further interest payments ; the investors lost everything they had lent. The founder of the important house of Deutz, Willem Gideon Deutz, has signed this bond in person. He was burgomaster of Amsterdam at this time.

WY KAREL de Zesde, door Godsgénaden verkooren Roams Keyzer, ten allen tyde Vermeerderaar des Kyks, Koning in Germanien en Spanjen, Hongarien, Bohemen, Arrds-Hertzog van Oostenryk, Hertzog van Burgiindien, Stirien, Carinthien, Crain, en Wurtenberg, in Opper-en Neder-Silselen, Markgraaf tot Mähren, in Opper en Neder-Lausitz, Graaf tot Habsburg, Tyrol en Goritzy &c. bekennen, voor Ons, onze Erven en Nakomellingen, in kragt dezes Schulthbrief openlyk, en doen daar nevens kond aan een igelyk, dat op onze genadiafte bewilfiginge en goedkeurige, door middel en directie van Willem Gideon Deutz, tot Amsterdam, van versckeydene Persoonen en Particulieren, ten decle ook op andere plaatsen voorgesteld, een declen ook op andere plaatsen voorgesteld, dienst van onseu van het gemeneete weezen genegotieerd, en by forme van beleeninge opgebragt, gelyk meede in handen van onze Keizerlyke Schatkamer in contant geld, tegens de da vour volle krijtige beteonibg valg gelyk vol zekere somme contant geld, bedragende zevenmal hondert duytzend guldens Hollands Courant, en wy derhalven de gemelde somme van zevenmal hondert duytzend Guldens Hollands Courant, aantmen hier by derhalven de gemelde somme van zevenmal hondert duytzend Guldens Hollands Courant, aantmen hier by Willem Gideon Deutz, en verdiere mede Geinteresseerdenis, dewelkee boventialade leeningen te zamen hebben opgestoroten, verthioldigt zyn geworden, en aan entregens voor Ons, ondat Wy en Nakomellingen, voorwerens en verplicht agte tot voorgaande onderhandeling daar over met zyne daar toe benoernde Gevolmagtigidens gehouden, toegezegd, betaald, en en wy voor het gemeelde ter lenen opgenomene Kapitaal s jaarlrks aan Intereellen, na rato des tyds betalen zullen vyf per cent, dat wy ook de voornoelmde opgenomene, en vertrekte somsme van zevenmal hondert duytzend guldens Hollands Courant, wyftien Jaaren binnen Amsterdam, in gelyck Hollandtze Courant Munt weder zullen lettelderen Obligation dertelonen, ondat namntlyk in de tien eerft naalkoomende Jaaren, synde Anno een duytzend zeventhondert zeven en derttig, tot Anno een duytzend zeventhondert zes en veertig ingeslotene, die invoeging der voornoemde kapitaals, zal in de tyd pertiode elk van vijf pertiode elk van vijf jaaren, als meede ten naastvolf der jaaren, dertelonen, tot bilyk een volkomeh gemongen van hem Willem Gideon Deutz, en der overige mede Geinteresseerdenrs; zonder enig manjagement afgeloid, en onder volkdan ze boramen worden, wyl wy nu het zelve Obligatoire Instrument door onze Voorten en Standen in Silselen deswegns opgemaakt, dat namntyk de afflositinge zo wel van het ter lenen veniltaande wyze, en in de vailgeldeelde ternynen, zonder ceedige exception oft uyttel gelchieiden zal ; alleins voor aangenaem gehouven, en daer over onze genadigte toe teminyge en goedkeurige verleend hebben.

WY

## English Translation:

WE CHARLES the Sixth, by the Grace of God elected Roman Emperor, at all times increaser of the Empire, King in Germany and Spain, Hungary, Bohemia, Archduke of Austria, Duke of Burgundy, Styria, Carinthia, Crain, and Württemberg, in Upper and Lower Silesia, Marquis of Moravia, in Upper and Lower Lusatia, Count of Habsburg, Tyrol and Gorizia etc. acknowledge, for Us, our Heirs and Successors, by virtue of this deed of bond publicly and hereby declare to all that at our gracious will and good pleasure, through the mediation and direction of Willem Gideon Deutz, of Amsterdam, from various Persons and Individuals, partly also at other places, a sum required for the service of our State has been negotiated and through means of borrowing raised, in like manner deposited in our Imperial Treasury in ready money, against the said for full discharge thereof. And we therefore acknowledge the mentioned sum of seven hundred thousand guilders, Hollands Courant, and we do hereby, through Willem Gideon Deutz, and further interested parties, who have together contributed these loans, confirm and obligate ourselves to the same.

And we declare that we owe and are bound for the named loan, that we shall to the mentioned gathered borrowed Capital annually pay interest, at the rate of five percent, and that we will also the aforesaid borrowed and received sum of seven hundred thousand guilders, Hollands Courant, fifteen years within Amsterdam, in like Hollandse Courant money repay to the Obligation herein mentioned, namely in the ten first coming years, being in the year one thousand seven hundred and thirty-seven, until the year one thousand seven hundred and forty-six, with the consequence that in each five-year period, as also at the following of the years, shall be paid, without full and complete discharge of him Willem Gideon Deutz, and the other interested parties; without any management excluded, and under full faith and credit, we have caused this Obligatoire instrument through our authorities and estates in Silesia to be made, namely that the payment, as well of the principal and interest to be loaned, in the agreed and appointed terms, without any exception or failure shall happen; solely for acceptance esteemed, and thereover our gracious approval and good pleasure granted.

WE

title: Commerce d'Asie & d'Afrique (Trieste Company)
description: ANVERS. Action de 1000 Florins. black. No 194. - Date: October 1, 1781 -  In 1775 Guilleaume Bolts obtained permission from Empress Maria Theresa to establish a company in the Austrian free port of Trieste, for trading with the East Indies. In 1781 the first shares were issued, with great success. The director was the famous Antwerp businessman Charles de Proli, son of the founder of the Keyserlijke Indische Compagnie, of Ostend; he was also linked with the formation of the Assurance d'Anvers. The company could not compete with the French and English competition, and after an unfortunate expedition to China, the company was unable to meet its liabilities. The Trieste Company is the last of the great trading companies of the Habsburgs. The share is printed on hand-made paper, and is signed by Guillaume Bolts, Count Charles de Proli, and J.C.J. Borrekens.

title: The Caracas Company (Real Compañía Guipuzcoana de Caracas)
description: MADRID. 1 June 1752. Accion de 500 escudos. black. #2000. No 2530. The 'Caracas Company', the Real Compania Guipuzcoana de Caracas, was formed by a group of merchants in the Guipuzcoa province, around San Sebastian, in the Basque region of Spain, to trade with the Caracas province of Venezuela, with the further aims of (a) developing its agriculture, especially cocoa, and (b) keeping watch on the coast, from the mouth of the river Orinoco to the river Hacha (later extended to cover Maracaibo). This latter aim was to prevent illegal (in Spanish eyes) trading, particularly by the Dutch from Curaçao. The leader of this group was the Count of Penaflorida. This was the first of the great Spanish overseas trading companies, and the first Spanish trading company known to have issued shares to the general public. The company had the right to send two ships per year from San Sebastian and nearby Pasajes to Venezuela, carrying all types of Spanish goods. For the return voyage the ships brought precious metals, cocoa, sugar, tobacco and leathers, back to Sevilla and, later, Cadiz. In 1730 the company set about establishing a chain of trading-posts along the coast of what is now Venezuela and the offshore islands of Margarita and Trinidad, and in 1732 obtained a monopoly of trade between Caracas and Spain; in 1742 this was extended for an indefinite period. In that same year the company's Head Office was moved from San Sebastian to Madrid. From the outset the company was very profitable, paying large dividends to its shareholders. King Felipe V and the Queen took 100 shares each, for a combined investment of 100,000 escudos. The initial capital was 1,000,000 escudos (2,000 shares of 500 escudos of 15 reales each), but shares were a new idea to the Spanish public, and they did not sell well at first; only 500,000 escudos were sold (including those to the royal house, as above). The capital was later increased, in 1752, and again in 1766. The company's activities expanded rapidly, especially after 1734, when restrictions on the number of sailings were removed. The Caracas production, especially of cocoa, rose sharply. By mid-century the company owned 12 large ocean-going ships and 19 coastal ships, with some 2,500 crew, and carrying 2,500 or more tons of freight annually in each direction. However, the company mis-used its monopoly powers, by charging excessive prices for imported goods, and cutting steadily the already low prices paid to Caracas growers for their produce; this, together with interference in the government of Caracas, led in the end to a rebellion by the the colonists. Not until 1752 was this finally subdued, and these events led the Spanish government to reduce the company's privileges and introduce fixed prices for buying cocoa and other produce. Profits fell sharply, and the company's fortunes went into steady decline. Its investments in Spain were unsuccessful; wars against England in 1761-3 and 1779-83 cost it dearly; the free-trading policies of King Carlos III were the final blow. In 1781 the company lost the monopoly with Venezuela, and in 1785 it was absorbed by the Real Compania de Filipinas. The Caracas shares were exchanged for those of the Filipinas company. The share is very attractive, printed on vellum, with a fine copper-engraving. At the top are the royal arms of Guipuzcoa; on each side, and down the sides is a fine design of leaves, fruit,weapons, and an Indian man, with bow-and-arrow, and woman. Boxes of company freight are all around. There is a fine paper seal, also with the royal arms of Guipuzcoa. This is a share from the fist capital increase.

title: Swedish West-India Company
description: STOCKHOLM. 15 December 1787. Share of 100 Reichstaler. black. No 259. Folds. As early as 1745 the trading house Abr. Jocab Arfwedson & Co. was given the privilege of creating a West India company, but due to a sharp protest from the Spanish envoy in Stockholm against this undertaking, the firm renounced its privilege. After the Swedish acquisition in 1784 of Saint Barthélemy in the West Indies, town secretary Johan Liljencrants put a proposition to the Chamber of Commerce for the formation of a share-based company to conduct trade in the West Indies. In 1786, the company received a 15-year privilege for commerce and shipping with the Swedish island of Saint Barthélemy and other islands of the West Indies as well as with North America. Liljencrants and the Stockholm wholesale dealers Arfwedson, Schinkel and Pauli were to supervise the subscription. The business did not develop as hoped for, and the first expedition was lost as a consequence of the war with Russia in 1788. Later on, the business was paralysed due to prohibitions of importation of certain goods, especially coffee. High costs caused by captures of ships brought bad commercial results and the company was dissolved in 1805. The island became French, as part of Guadeloupe, in 1878. A 4-page document, ink-cancelled with a large 'X'. Printed, with manuscript additions of payment

title: Société Toulousaine du Bazacle Share
description: A bearer founder's share of the Société Toulousaine du Bazacle, a joint-stock company with its registered seat at 10, Quai Saint-Pierre in Toulouse, created by the extraordinary general assembly of 26 April 1928. The statutes, deposited before Maître Moyne, notary at Paris, were modified by the extraordinary assemblies of 18 March 1927 and 26 April 1928, the company's capital then standing at 13,150,000 francs, divided into 131,500 shares of 100 francs each. This instrument stands apart from that capital, conferring instead a one twenty-thousandth claim on the founders' advantages reserved by the statutes. The company, raised upon Toulouse's Garonne mill works, had by this date become an electricity concern.

title: Hotel Waldorf-Astoria Corporation Specimen Share
description: A specimen certificate of no-par common stock in the Hotel Waldorf-Astoria Corporation, incorporated in New York as the company behind the new Waldorf-Astoria. Marked SPECIMEN and numbered 000, it is an unissued printer's proof. It names The First National Bank of Boston as transfer agent. The 47-story tower at 301 Park Avenue opened on 1 October 1931 as the largest hotel in the world; the original Waldorf-Astoria had been demolished in 1929 to clear its Fifth Avenue site for the Empire State Building.

pages.description: A specimen certificate of no-par common stock in the Hotel Waldorf-Astoria Corporation, incorporated in New York as the company behind the new Waldorf-Astoria. Printed in green within an ornate engraved border and headed by an allegory of prosperity and hospitality, it names The First National Bank of Boston as transfer agent. Behind the paper lies one of the era's boldest ventures: the original Waldorf-Astoria, built in the 1890s by two rival Astor cousins, was demolished in 1929 to clear its Fifth Avenue site for the Empire State Building, and its name was carried north for a single dollar. Raised on roughly $40 million of bank credit, the 47-story Art Deco tower at 301 Park Avenue opened on 1 October 1931 — in the depths of the Great Depression — as the largest hotel in the world. Marked SPECIMEN and numbered 000, it is the unissued printer's proof of the equity behind that gamble.

The reverse, printed in black, quotes clauses of the certificate of incorporation governing share issuance, director self-dealing, and the absence of preference among common shares. Below, a blank assignment and power-of-attorney form for transferring the stock, with punched binding holes at the margin. Page 2 of 2.

title: Kokueki Petroleum Association Share Certificate
description: A share certificate of the Kokueki Sekiyu Kumiai, the National-Profit Petroleum Association, a Japanese oil cooperative, issued in 1900. The reverse provides a transfer ledger and a dividend-payment table.

title: Connecticut Land Company Certificate
description: A trust certificate of the Connecticut Land Company, issued at Hartford on 5 September 1795, recording one investor's fractional share in the Connecticut Western Reserve, the tract in present-day Ohio that the company had purchased from the State of Connecticut. The instrument vests a holder with an undivided proportion of the Reserve held by trustees under a Deed of Trust, transferable by assignment under the company's Articles of Agreement, and recordable before a magistrate. The accompanying leaves carry the registration docket and a later deed assigning the share, with consideration stated in dollars.

Verso docket: "No. 151. Certificate from Trustees to Calvin Austin. Received Novr. 15. 1796 & entered in the Book of Records of the Connecticut Land Company for registering Certificates. Teste Eph. Root, Clerk of the Directors." Faint mirror-offset script bleeds through at left. Page 2 of 4.

title: Rhode Island Land-Bank Mortgage Indenture, Newport and Providence
description: A printed and manuscript mortgage indenture securing a loan of colonial bills of credit under Rhode Island's public land-bank scheme, the engraved form made in the twelfth year of His Majesty's reign, 1738. It names the trustees John Wanton, George Goulding, Jahleel Brenton, Daniel Updike, John Gardner and James Sheffield, appointed by Act of Assembly to emit paper upon loan. Against bills advanced, the borrower mortgages a sixty-acre parcel in Providence township, bounded northerly by the land of James Williams and westerly by the highway, covenanting repayment with interest at five per centum in passable bills of public credit. It was recorded at Providence on 20 April 1739 in the book for the sixth bank's mortgages by town clerk Richard Waterman.

title: Share Receipt (Recepis) for the Garphytte Iron and Alum Works and Beata Christina Alum Work
description: A Dutch-language share receipt, issued at Amsterdam on 1 April 1776, certifying a 1/1063 interest in the iron manufactory and alum works at Garphytte and in the alum work Beata Christina, both in Sweden, financed through a negotiation floated on the Amsterdam capital market. It is given in exchange for a share in the outstanding loan, together with the arrears of unpaid interest coupons, and records that part of the underlying obligations had already been redeemed by lottery drawing. It was printed under the directors' authority and registered before a notary.

Claeywanger and a second, [illegible]) and registered by notary Paulus [Huntum]. Page 1 of 2.

A sheet of detachable dividend receipts (quittances) tied to Recepis No. 27. A header notes that on surrender of this number new receipts will be issued in 1786, signed M.H. Coster, April 1776. Below run repeated printed acknowledgements of one year's distribution on the Garphytte and Beata Christina works, dated by descending year (1785, 1784, 1783…), each signed M.H. Coster. Page 2 of 2.

title: Marine Insurance Policy on the French Corvette La Byzantine (Brussels)
description: A French-language marine insurance policy underwritten at Brussels on 13 April 1757. The underwriter, F. Depestre, insures Monsieur James Dormer for 2,800 florins in exchange money on his interest in the French corvette La Byzantine, commanded by Captain Guillaume Moulin de la Perelle, for a voyage from the river of Nantes to Cap-Français on the island of Saint-Domingue, present-day Haiti. The printed policy form enumerates the perils covered: sea, wind, tempest, shipwreck, fire, pirates, privateers, enemies, warships, letters of marque, and seizure by any power, against a wartime premium of thirty-five percent, payable in account within six months. Any dispute was to be settled by two merchants of the country, with a third called in if they disagreed, on penalty of a thousand florins. The policy is subscribed "Bon pour deux mille huit cens florins de change" and signed by F. Depestre.
creator: F. Depestre (underwriter)
notes: Marine insurance policy formerly bound with the Garphytte share receipt (goetzmann0931), where it had been catalogued as its third page; detached and catalogued separately. Underwritten at Brussels during the Seven Years' War for a Nantes–Saint-Domingue voyage.
transcription:
# Marine Insurance Policy on the French Corvette La Byzantine — Transcription

## Original (French):

**AU NOM DE DIEU AMEN.**

JE soussigné assure à Vous *Monsieur James Dormer* pour vôtre Compte, ou de tout autre à qui il pourroit appartenir en total ou en partie, soit ami ou ennemi, sçavoir la somme de *deux mille huit Cens Florins argent de Change* sur intérêts à la *Corvette Française la Byzantine*, dont est maître (Après Dieu) Capitaine *Guillaume Moulin de la Perelle* (lecture incertaine), sans pouvoir faire aucune contestation sur le nom du Capitaine ou Vaisseau (quel qu'il soit); le risque à courir sur *lesdits intérêts* commençant du jour & heure que ledit Vaisseau étoit encore à *la rivière de Nantes* jusqu'à ce qu'il soit arrivé *au Cap Français, isle de St Domingue*, lieu de sa destination, où les risques finiront sur *ledit Vaisseau* vingt-quatre heures après qu'il y aura jetté l'ancre, et sur lesdites *marchandises* après leur entière décharge à terre à bon sauvement.

Il sera permis au dit Vaisseau de naviger à droit, à gauche, en avant ou en arriére pendant son Voyage, sans que cela puisse causer aucun préjudice à la presente assurance. Je me soumets de courir les risques & perils auxquels *ledit Vaisseau et lesdites marchandises* pourroient être assujettis, ou endomagemens qui pourroient y survenir, soit en totalité ou en partie, dans toutes les rencontres imaginables, de quelle maniere ou façon qu'elles puissent arriver; car je m'oblige de garantir tous perils de Mer, Vent, Tempêtes, Naufrage, Echouement, Abordage, jets en Mer, Feu, Arrets, Pirates, Corsaires, Voleurs, Ennemis, Vaisseau de Guerre, lettres de marque ou contremarque, prise inimicale, surprise, detention, confiscation, represailles, vexations des Rois, Princes, Puissances & Peuple quelconque; & generalement de tous autres perils, pertes, fortunes ou cas fortuits, qui sont, ou pourroient avenir, en quelque maniere que ce soit que l'on puisse imaginer au detriment ou dommage *desdits intérêts* ou d'une partie d'iceux.

[Suivent les clauses imprimées d'usage: engagement de rembourser toute perte excédant trois pour cent à proportion de la somme assurée, en diminuant deux pour cent en cas de perte; pouvoir donné à l'assuré de travailler à la salvation du Vaisseau et des marchandises aux frais de l'assureur.]

Confesse être payé du prix de la présente assurance de vous M.r *James Dormer* (*en compte payable dans six mois*) à raison de *trente-cinq par cent*; & en cas de quelque contestation entre nous, pour le réglement & vérifications des avaries ou pertes, & pour l'exécution de la présente police, le tout sera réglé par deux Négocians de ce Pays, qui seront nommez à cet effet, sçavoir un par vous M.r *James Dormer* & l'autre par moi soussigné; lesquels, en cas qu'ils ne s'accordent, pourront s'adjoindre un tiers aussi de ce Pays, non suspect aux parties; à peine de mil Florins de Change que le contredisant sera obligé de payer, moitié aux pauvres de cette Ville, & l'autre moitié à l'acceptant. Le tout en bonne foi sans fraude ni malice.

Fait à Bruxelles ce *treizième Avril mil sept Cens cinquante-sept* [13 April 1757].

*Bon pour deux mille huit cens florins de change.*

*[signé] F. Depestre*

---

## English Translation:

**IN THE NAME OF GOD, AMEN.**

I the undersigned insure to You, *Monsieur James Dormer*, for your account or that of any other whom it may concern in whole or in part, be he friend or enemy, namely the sum of *two thousand eight hundred florins in exchange money* upon interests in the *French corvette La Byzantine*, of which the master (after God) is *Captain Guillaume Moulin de la Perelle* (reading uncertain) — no objection to be raised as to the name of the captain or the vessel (whatever it may be); the risk to run upon the said interests beginning from the day and hour that the said vessel was still in *the river of Nantes*, until it shall have arrived *at Cap-Français, island of Saint-Domingue*, the place of its destination, where the risks upon the said vessel shall end twenty-four hours after it has cast anchor, and upon the said goods after their entire unloading ashore in safety.

The said vessel shall be permitted to sail to the right, to the left, forward or backward during its voyage, without that causing any prejudice to the present insurance. I undertake to run the risks and perils to which the said vessel and goods may be subject, or the damages that may befall them, in whole or in part; for I bind myself to guarantee against all perils of sea, wind, tempests, shipwreck, stranding, collision, jettison, fire, arrests, pirates, privateers, thieves, enemies, warships, letters of marque or reprisal, hostile capture, surprise, detention, confiscation, reprisals, and the vexations of kings, princes, powers, and any people whatsoever; and generally all other perils, losses, and misfortunes that are or may come to pass.

[There follow the customary printed clauses: an undertaking to repay any loss exceeding three per cent in proportion to the sum insured, deducting two per cent in case of loss; and power given to the insured to work for the salvage of the vessel and goods at the insurer's charge.]

I acknowledge to be paid the price of this insurance by you, Mr *James Dormer* (*on account payable within six months*), at the rate of *thirty-five per cent*; and in case of any dispute between us, for the settlement and verification of average or losses and for the execution of this policy, the whole shall be settled by two merchants of this country, appointed for that purpose — one by you, Mr *James Dormer*, and the other by me the undersigned; who, should they not agree, may join to themselves a third, likewise of this country and not suspect to the parties; on penalty of one thousand florins of exchange, which the party in default shall be obliged to pay, half to the poor of this city and the other half to the accepting party. All in good faith, without fraud or malice.

Made at Brussels, this *thirteenth of April one thousand seven hundred and fifty-seven* [13 April 1757].

*Good for two thousand eight hundred florins of exchange.*

*[signed] F. Depestre*

description: A bearer bond of the Unified Debt of Egypt, issued under decrees of the Khedive dated 7 May and 18 November 1876. Printed in parallel French and English columns, it bears 7 percent interest on a denomination of 2,500 francs, or 100 pounds sterling, drawn from a total capital of 1,475,000,000 francs, and is redeemable at par over sixty-five years through half-yearly drawings. It is signed at Cairo for the Khedive's government and countersigned by Commissioner-Directors of the Caisse de la Dette Publique, among them E. Baring and E. de Blignières.

pages.description: The bond face, in facing French and English columns under a "7%" panel and an Egyptian-revival border of lotus columns and sphinxes. It recites the 1876 decrees, the 1,475,000,000-Franc capital, redemption at par in 65 years, and a quoted Commissioners' resolution "Fait au Caire, le 19 avril 1877." Denomination panels read Fr. 2,500 and £100; manuscript signatures and an attached coupon block sit below. Page 1 of 2.

The reverse, showing two large engraved counterfoils repeating the bond's terms for the £100 (English) and Fr. 2,500 (French) sides, alongside the surviving talon of coupons worth Fr. 87.50 / £3:10:0 each. A boxed "Amortissement / Amortization" note explains that no redemption table could be drawn, the sinking fund depending on the fifty-four remaining years and budget surpluses under the decree of 18 November 1876. Page 2 of 2.

title: Antwerp Marine Insurance Policy with an Amsterdam Survivorship Contract
description: A grouping of two unrelated risk-pooling instruments from the eighteenth-century Low Countries. The first leaf is a printed marine insurance policy of the Chambre Impériale et Royale d'Assurance d'Anvers, headed "AU NOM DE DIEU"; its blanks are completed in manuscript to cover a bale of merchandise aboard the vessel La Paix, dated and signed at Antwerp on 25 April 1761 with a wax seal. The remaining four leaves form a separate printed survivorship contract, the Contract van Overleeving, under the device "De Tyd baard Roozen," issued at Amsterdam in 1774, setting out its conditions in numbered articles and ending in a manuscript registration certificate.

pages.description: Printed marine insurance policy of the Chambre Impériale et Royale d'Assurance d'Anvers, with an engraved roundel of a ship in heavy seas and the words "AU NOM DE DIEU." Manuscript entries insure a bale of goods on the vessel La Paix; signed by Thomas Joseph De Bie and Charles Crol, dated Antwerp 25 April 1761, with an embossed wax seal. Page 1 of 5.

Letterpress title and opening articles of a survivorship contract, headed "CONTRACT VAN OVERLEEVING, Letter G" under the motto "DE TYD BAARD ROOZEN." Dense two-column "Conditien en Voorwaarden" begin the numbered terms, followed by tables of subscription sums by age class. Page 2 of 5.

Continuation of the printed articles of the survivorship contract, two columns of closely set numbered clauses governing nominees, classes, payments, and administration. Wholly typographic, with no manuscript entries. Page 3 of 5.
Final printed columns of the contract's articles, closing the regulations; the lower text records its enactment at Amsterdam in 1774. Two columns of small type, no illustration. Page 4 of 5.

Manuscript registration certificate: the directors certify that Diderikus Tijk is entered on the small list, no. nine, in the age class 15 to 35, under letter G, for a subscription of f10 furnished by himself; dated Amsterdam 31 October 1774. Below are folded ledger leaves of annual handwritten entries. Page 5 of 5.

# Marine Insurance Policy of the Imperial and Royal Insurance Chamber of Antwerp (1761) — Transcription

## Original:

(Top left, printed with manuscript number:)
**N° _2766_**

(Engraved circular vignette, center top: a ship tossed on stormy seas, a castaway on the shore in the foreground, a flag lettered **S.A.**; legend around the rim:)
**SECURUS PELLAGI**
(engraver's signature beneath the medallion: *L. Fruytiers f.*)

(Printed heading, split to the left and right of the vignette:)
**CHAMBRE IMPERIALE ET ROYALE D'ASSURANCE D'ANVERS.**

**AU NOM DE DIEU.**

(Body — printed text with manuscript insertions shown in *italics*:)

**Nous soussignés Directeurs de la Chambre d'Assurance d'Anvers, reconnoissons & confessons avoir pris aux Risques, Perils & Fortunes de la dite Chambre de Vous** *Madame Ladoüa J: Dormer & C°* **pour le compte neutre de qui il appartiendra la Somme ci-après mentionnée sur** *Un Balot marq[ué] ADI N°.1 pour Compt[e] Espagnole Chargée à bord du Navire Hollandois La Paix Capitaine Izaac Geynstroom à Ostende Destiné pour Cadix*

(several blank ruled lines follow)

**lesquelles Marchandises Vous estimez ensemble à la Somme de** *Dix Sept Cens Cinquante Florins Argent de change* **de la quelle Estimation nous nous contentons, & en cas de Pillage ou Avaries, ils ne seront à notre charge que lorsqu'ils excéderont Trois pour Cent.**

**Lesquels Risques nous prennons à la charge de la Compagnie, depuis le Jour & Heure, que les dites Marchandises ont été embarquées à bord du dit Navire, jusqu'à tant que les dites Marchandises soient arrivées à** *Cadix* **à bon sauvement, & accordons que le dit Navire, faisant le dit Voyage, pourra naviguer avant & arriere, à dextre & à senextre côte: nous soumettans de courir Risque de tous Perils de Mer, de Feu, de Vents, d'Amis, d'Ennemis, de Lettres de Marque & Contre-marque, d'Arrets & Détentions des Rois, Princes & Seigneurs quelconques, & de Baraterie de Patron, Maître, Mariniers, & généralement de tous autres Perils, Fortunes ou Cas fortuits qui pourroient avenir en quelque maniere que l'on puisse s'imaginer, se mettant de tout en la place de l'Assuré pour le garantir & indemniser de toutes Pertes & Dommages qui pourroient arriver: & en cas de Perte ou Dommages aux dites Marchandises (ce que Dieu ne veuille) promettons & nous obligeons de payer ou rembourser au Porteur de cette Police, la perte ou dommage, à proportion de la Somme que nous avons assurée, à raison de Quatre-vingt Dix-huit pour Cent, & ce comptant après que nous serons dûement informés de la Perte ou Dommage arrivé aux dites Marchandises, & en tel cas donnons Pouvoir special au dit Assuré ou à son Commis pour tant à notre Dommage que Profit, travailler ou faire travailler à la Salvation des dites Marchandises, promettant en tout évenement de payer les Fraix & Dépens faits pour leur Salvation, soit qu'elles soient récouvrées ou non, ajoûtant foi & entier credit au Compte, & à la Personne ou Personnes qui auront fait les dits Fraix & Dépens. Confessons être payés du Prix de la présente Assurence par le dit Assuré à raison de** *1 ¾* **pour Cent.** *La Somme de Trente florins Douze sous & demi Argt de change*

**[Fait] de bonne Foi, sans fraude ni malengin: & en cas de Contestation entre nous pour le fait de la présente [Assurance] & dépendance d'icelle, nous conviendrons d'Arbitres pour juger de nos différens. [Fait au] Bureau de la Chambre d'Assurance à Anvers le** *25 avril 1761*

(Manuscript signatures, lower right:)
*Thomas Joseph De Bie*
*Charles Crol[e]*

(Embossed paper wax seal, lower left.)

(Left margin, printed vertically:)
**NB. La Compagnie n'entre point dans le Coulage des liquides, ni dans les Avaries sur toute sorte de Grains, Graine ou Semence, Poisson, Cuirs, Tabac, Sel, Fruis verts ou secs, à moins que l'Avarie ne soit grosse, ni sur Chanvre, Lin, Sucre, que lorsqu'elle excéde Dix pour Cent.**

(Note: the source image contains only this single leaf — the printed Antwerp marine policy. The Amsterdam survivorship contract (Contract van Overleeving) mentioned in the catalogue description is on other leaves not present in this image.)

---

## English Translation:

**No. 2766**

(Engraved medallion, legend:) **SECURE FROM THE SEA** (flag: **S.A.**; engraver: *L. Fruytiers*)

**IMPERIAL AND ROYAL INSURANCE CHAMBER OF ANTWERP.**

**IN THE NAME OF GOD.**

**We the undersigned Directors of the Insurance Chamber of Antwerp acknowledge and confess that we have taken upon the Risks, Perils & Fortunes of the said Chamber from You** *Madame Ladoüa J. Dormer & Co.* **for the neutral account of whomsoever it may concern, the Sum hereafter mentioned upon** *One Bale marked ADI No. 1 for Spanish account, loaded aboard the Dutch Ship La Paix, Captain Isaac Geynstroom, at Ostend, destined for Cadiz*

**which Merchandise You value altogether at the Sum of** *Seventeen Hundred and Fifty Florins in exchange money*, **with which Valuation we are content, and in case of Pillage or Average, they shall not be to our charge unless they exceed Three per Cent.**

**Which Risks we take upon the charge of the Company, from the Day & Hour that the said Merchandise was loaded aboard the said Ship, until such time as the said Merchandise shall have arrived at** *Cadiz* **in safety; and we agree that the said Ship, making the said Voyage, may sail forwards and backwards, to the right and to the left side: submitting ourselves to run the Risk of all Perils of the Sea, of Fire, of Winds, of Friends, of Enemies, of Letters of Marque & Counter-marque, of Arrests & Detentions of Kings, Princes & Lords whatsoever, and of Barratry of the Owner, Master, Mariners, and generally of all other Perils, Fortunes or fortuitous Cases that might occur in any manner one may imagine, placing ourselves entirely in the stead of the Insured to guarantee and indemnify him against all Losses & Damages that might occur: and in case of Loss or Damage to the said Merchandise (which God forbid) we promise and bind ourselves to pay or reimburse to the Bearer of this Policy the loss or damage, in proportion to the Sum we have insured, at the rate of Ninety-eight per Cent, and this in cash after we shall have been duly informed of the Loss or Damage befallen the said Merchandise; and in such case we give special Power to the said Insured or to his Clerk, as much to our Loss as Profit, to work or cause to be worked at the Salvage of the said Merchandise, promising in every event to pay the Costs & Expenses incurred for their Salvage, whether they be recovered or not, giving full faith and entire credit to the Account and to the Person or Persons who shall have made the said Costs & Expenses. We confess to be paid the Price of the present Insurance by the said Insured at the rate of** *1 ¾* **per Cent.** *The Sum of Thirty florins Twelve sous and a half in exchange money.*

**[Made] in good Faith, without fraud or deceit: and in case of Dispute between us concerning the matter of the present [Insurance] and its dependencies, we shall agree upon Arbitrators to judge our differences. [Done at the] Office of the Insurance Chamber at Antwerp, the** *25 April 1761*

*Thomas Joseph De Bie*
*Charles Crol[e]*

(Left margin:) **NB. The Company does not enter into the Leakage of liquids, nor into the Average on any kind of Grain, Seed or Seed-corn, Fish, Hides, Tobacco, Salt, Fruit fresh or dried, unless the Average be great; nor on Hemp, Flax, Sugar, except when it exceeds Ten per Cent.**

title: Egyptian Treasury Payment Order to Oppenheim & Cie, Legalized at Alexandria
description: A payment order of the Egyptian Treasury addressed to the banking house J.H. Oppenheim Neveux & Cie, dated 23 Zilhicce 1282 of the Muslim calendar. It promises payment of £E195,000, equivalent to 390 bourses, on 8 November 1866, and is signed by the Minister of Finance Mohamed Hafiz Pacha. The item survives as a pair: the Arabic original, bearing the bankers' registration stamp and ministerial seal, and a certified French translation. Both sheets carry the legalizations of the French Consulate General at Alexandria, dated 12 May 1866, authenticating the seal of the Finance Minister and the signature of the acting Foreign Affairs Minister, Raghib Pacha.

pages.description: The certified French translation of the order, opening “Bon sur le ministère des finances” and promising £E 195,000 (390 bourses) to MM. Oppenheim Neveux & Cie, signed Mohamed Hafiz Pacha, 23 Zilhicce 1282. Below, the First Dragoman B. Garnier certifies the translation and the Consul General legalizes it, with two oval consular seals, Alexandria, 12 May 1866. Page 2 of 2.

The Arabic original: a Treasury order (سند طلب على ديوان المالية المصرية) for £E 195,000 payable 8 November 1866 to Oppenheim & Cie. Bears the blue bankers’ stamp “H.O.N. & Co. No 1694,” a red exchange notation, Arabic ministerial seals, and French consular legalizations of the Finance and Foreign Affairs ministers’ marks, Alexandria, 12 May 1866. Page 1 of 2.

# Egyptian Treasury Payment Order to J.H. Oppenheim Nephews & Co., Certified French Translation Legalized at Alexandria (1866) — Transcription

## Original:

**Bon sur le ministère des finances.**

Du Trente Rabi 1er 83 correspondant au 8 novembre 1866, il sera payé par le trésor du ministère des finances à Messieurs J.H. Oppenheim neveux et Cie, ou à leur ordre la somme de £E 195,000 équivalent à Bourses 390 en espèce à l'exclusion de monnaie en cuivre et cela à valoir de leur crédit du ministère des finances.

Prix seulement la somme de cent quatre vingt quinze mille piastres tarif soit trois cent quatre vingt dix Bourses.

Le 23 Zilheggé 1282.

Le ministre des finances

(P.P.) mohamet Haffiz Pacha.

(certification of translation)

Pour Traduction Certifié conforme

Alexandrie le 12 Mai 1866.

Le premier Drogman.

*B. Garnier* (signature)

(consular legalization)

Vu pour légalisation de la signature ci-dessus de M<sup>r</sup> B. Garnier Premier Drogman du Consulat Général de France à Alexandrie d'Égypte.

Alexandrie le 12 Mai 1866.

P. l'Agent et Consul Général

Le Consul

[signature — illegible]

(left margin, written vertically) N° 8956 — Art. 71 — pour V[ou]s — [illegible]

(two blue circular consular seals, lower left and mid-left: **CONSULAT GÉNÉRAL DE FRANCE / A ALEXANDRIE**, with imperial eagle at center)

(structural notes: the amount abbreviation is written "£.E." before the figure "195,000"; the opening date "Trente Rabi 1er 83" is the Muslim-calendar date the writer equates to 8 November 1866 — best read as 30 Rabi' [al-awwal] (12)83; the internal ministerial date "23 Zilheggé 1282" = 23 Dhū al-Ḥijja 1282. A few words are given as best readings: the summation word "Prix", and the marginal registration note, are uncertain.)

---

## English Translation:

**Bond drawn on the Ministry of Finance.**

On the Thirtieth of Rabi' I [12]83, corresponding to 8 November 1866, there shall be paid by the treasury of the Ministry of Finance to Messrs J.H. Oppenheim Nephews & Co., or to their order, the sum of £E 195,000, equivalent to 390 Bourses, in specie, to the exclusion of copper coin, and this to be charged against their credit with the Ministry of Finance.

Say only the sum of one hundred ninety-five thousand piastres tariff, that is, three hundred ninety Bourses.

The 23rd of Dhū al-Ḥijja 1282.

The Minister of Finance

(By proxy) Mohamet Haffiz Pacha.

(certification of the translation)

Certified a true translation.

Alexandria, 12 May 1866.

The First Dragoman.

*B. Garnier* (signature)

(consular legalization)

Seen, for legalization of the above signature of Mr B. Garnier, First Dragoman of the Consulate General of France at Alexandria, Egypt.

Alexandria, 12 May 1866.

For the Agent and Consul General

The Consul

[signature — illegible]

(left margin, written vertically) No. 8956 — Art. 71 — for you — [illegible]

title: Dutch Life-Annuity Negotiation Deed and Nominee List
description: A printed copy of a notarial deed establishing a Dutch life-annuity negotiation at Amsterdam, opening with the date 1 May 1787. The loan is directed by Pieter Stadnitski and Hendrik Vollenhoven and was passed before the notary Abraham van Beem. Each subscribed share carries one thousand guilders, with interest paid against coupons due 1 November and 1 May. The income runs upon the lives of a long roster of named young women, whose survival governs each share's duration. Printed articles fix the terms, and subscribers acquire numbered shares against receipt.

pages.description: Headed "Copia." Opening deed dated 1 May 1787 names directors Pieter Stadnyski and Hendrik Vollenhoven and notary Abraham van Berk, followed by a dense block of printed conditions. Below, a numbered roster of female nominees (from No. 30) begins, each a named life upon which a share rests. Page 1 of 3.

Continuation of the numbered nominee roster (about Nos. 60–86), listing further women's names in italic. The lower half resumes printed articles (Art. I, Art. II) governing the negotiation, quittances, interest, and the directors' obligations. Page 2 of 3.

Printed articles continue (Art. III–VII) on payment of coupons and reckoning, closing with the directors' and notaries' signatures, Amsterdam 5 May 1787. A printed receipt at foot acknowledges one thousand guilders for a share, coupons due 1 November and 1 May, dated 8 May 1787, with handwritten ledger entries. Page 3 of 3.

Art. III.
Dat vermits volgens de gevoonde kans Reekening in ieder Actien Maanden, een hoofd, van de renten, kan en moet Sterven, als dan het verlies door ieder liefdeburen zou worden gedeeld, en naar dezen hoofd, in evenredigheijd met ½ pCo., ½ jaars vermrindering van Interest zou kunnen vergoed worden, zo als ook ieders, becom bij zijne keuring hoofd ook het vermeêrderen der Interest; met ½ pCo., ½ jaars goude toeslachen, waar der beide gevallen, het opgeteggen Capitaal, geneogzaam zoude blijven Accresfeefering op by overgalving van dit lastfte hoofd weder galyck aan de Inlang te zyn. De Heeren Eerste Compagnen hebben vermeinerd dit het eevenaudige middel tot herttel van 't goene tegen de Intrestenfoorders mogte, zoude zyn, dog vermits de veranderering van Interest egter juist niet om middelyk, op het Eerthe omregulering in den loop der Vereffeningen nodig is, zo sullen de Heeren Directeuren zhooren tot het eerste over te gaan de Gemeentesfoerdens Convocestenyen en als dan overgelegd worden of men de ½ pCo. zal blijven onderseeren, en dus de Negotiatie eene hoewel twijsom, oger en einde boornen, dan of men 't Interest jets verminnderen zal, om daardoor betatig te doen zyn, zullende Usthun in dit geval genoomen worden bij meerdeheid van Stemmen.

Dat indien deze Negotiatie niet den uiteinde haar reguliere loop houd en de Interesfenste tot ½ pCo., differentia even bij Harta de doorgetting benoemd, bestaald zyn: de gezanmuddyke Gemeintesfoerdens de aangekocke Effecten verifleeten zullen of zodanige andere Schikingen beraa men zij op die Tijd door de Meerderheld zal grodgevonden worden.

title: Chinese Imperial Government Tientsin-Pukow Railway Loan Bond
description: A £100 bearer bond from the Imperial Chinese Government's 5 percent Tientsin-Pukow Railway Loan, a £5,000,000 sterling issue raised in London on 1 September 1908 to build the trunk line linking Tientsin with Pukow on the Yangtze. Authority is vouched by two vermilion calligraphic seals, a purple seal and a manuscript signature, and the issue is countersigned for the Chinese Central Railway, London.

description: A share certificate of the Kousanie Tea Company, Limited, issued at Kousanie in northern India and dated 22 April 1874. title: Compagnie des Associés aux travaux du midi de Lyon, Share for the Pont de la Mulatière (Lyon)
description: An engraved share certificate of 500 livres in the Compagnie des Associés aux travaux du midi de Lyon, the venture charged with building the bridge of La Mulatière at Lyon. The share yields thirty livres of annual interest and a hundred-livres premium at redemption, returning 600 livres if repurchased. Its security is layered: charged specifically on the bridge's tolls and generally on company assets, with express subrogation to a 1,500,000-livre loan raised at Genoa and a 350,000-livre Crown advance. A sinking fund, opening 1 January 1790, retires twenty shares yearly by lot until the issue, capped at 880 shares, is extinguished. It is signed at Lyon by the company's director, treasurer and commissioners.

transcription:
# Document Transcription

**Original (French):**

*[Left margin, vertical text:]*
SUR LE PONT DE LA MULATIERE.

*[Header ornament]*

Action de cinq cents livres sur le pont de la Mulatiere, produisant trente livres d'intérêt, avec une prime de cent livres lors du remboursement.

Nous, souffignés, Directeur, Tréforier, & Commiffaires de la Compagnie des Affociés aux travaux du midi de Lyon, duement autorisés à cet effet, reconnoiffons avoir reçu de M. la fomme de cinq cents livres, pour être employée aux travaux du pont de la Mulatière, fous les clauses & conditions.

1°. Que la préfente action eft fpécialement affectée fur les produits du péage dudit Pont.

2°. Que, fans deroger à cette hypotheque particuliere, le porteur jouira d'une hypotheque générale fur les biens de la Société, avec fubrogation expresse fur lefdits biens aux droits, privileges & hypotheques résultant, soit de l'emprunt de Gênes, montant à 1,500,000 livres, soit de l'avance de 350,000 livres, faite par Sa Majesté à la Compagnie, qui, ne pouvant être affranchie de ces deux créances qu'à la charge du Pont, déclare que sa libération fera l'ouvrage de ceux qui fourniront des fonds pour le construire, & qui, par conséquent, auront les mêmes droits sur l'entreprise que les anciens créanciers avoient acquis.

3°. Que ladite action produira trente livres d'intérêt, dont le premier paiement fera fait par M. le préfident de Fleurieu, tréforier de la Compagnie, dans un an, à dater de ce jour; le second, à la même époque de l'année fuivante, & ainsi de fuite.

4°. Qu'au cas que la Compagnie rachete ladire action, comme elle s'en réserve la faculté, le porteur en fera remboursé fur le pied de 600 l., c'est-à-dire, avec une prime de 100 l. en capital.

5°. Que, dans dix années au plus tard, à compter du 1.er Janvier 1790, il fera procédé chaque année, & par la voie du fort, au remboursement de vingt actions, jusqu'à l'extinction totale des actions qui auront été vendues, & dont le nombre n'excèdera pas 880.

A LYON;

*[Signatures below]*

---

## English Translation:

**Action for five hundred livres on the bridge of Mulatiere, producing thirty livres of interest, with a premium of one hundred livres upon redemption.**

We, the undersigned, Director, Treasurer, & Commissioners of the Company of Associates for the works of the south of Lyon, duly authorized for this purpose, acknowledge having received from M. the sum of five hundred livres, to be employed in the works of the Mulatière bridge, under the following clauses and conditions.

1°. That this present action is specially charged upon the revenue from tolls of the said Bridge.

2°. That, without derogating from this particular mortgage, the holder shall enjoy a general mortgage on the assets of the Company, with express subrogation on said assets to the rights, privileges & mortgages resulting, either from the Genoese loan, amounting to 1,500,000 livres, or from the advance of 350,000 livres, made by His Majesty to the Company, which, being unable to be freed from these two debts except at the charge of the Bridge, declares that its liberation shall be the work of those who shall provide the funds to construct it, & who, consequently, shall have the same rights on the enterprise as the former creditors had acquired.

3°. That the said action shall produce thirty livres of interest, the first payment of which shall be made by M. the president of Fleurieu, treasurer of the Company, within one year from this date; the second, at the same time in the following year, & so on.

4°. That in the case that the Company redeems the said action, as it reserves the faculty to do so, the holder shall be reimbursed at the rate of 600 l., that is to say, with a premium of 100 l. in capital.

5°. That, within ten years at the latest, commencing from the 1st of January 1790, there shall be proceeded each year, & by means of the lottery, to the redemption of twenty actions, until the total extinction of the actions which shall have been sold, & of which the number shall not exceed 880.

pages.description: A $2,000 bond of the State of Mississippi, styled a "Five Per Cent Loan," issued for the benefit of the Mississippi Union Bank. The State promises to pay the sum in current money of the United States to the order of the bank's President, Directors and Company on the fifth day of February 1850, with interest at five per cent per annum payable half-yearly on the first of May and November. Signed and sealed at Jackson in June 1838, with a sheet of interest coupons still attached. The instrument records Mississippi's pledge of public credit to capitalize a state-chartered planters' bank during the speculative cotton boom that preceded the Panic of 1837's aftermath; the State would repudiate such Union Bank bonds in the early 1840s. The engraved vignette pairs a seated classical figure of Commerce with a feathered Native American amid corn and cotton bales above a river landscape, an allegory of the agrarian wealth offered as security.

This is the reverse of a sterling bond of the Mississippi Union Bank, bearing the engraved undertaking by which the President and Directors designate the Agency of the Bank of the United States in the city of London as the place of payment of the within bond and interest. The instrument is transferred to bearer for value received, declared equal to four hundred and fifty pounds sterling, and the payment guaranteed; it is subscribed by S. Gwin as cashier and H. G. Runnels as president. A red overprint identifies it as a "Mississippi State Bond," No. 562, £450, redeemable February 5th, 1850, and below runs a sheet of attached interest coupons, each for eleven pounds five shillings sterling payable at the agency of the Bank of the United States, London. Issued to fund a state-chartered bank, the bond shows Mississippi raising capital in the London market on the eve of the panic and repudiation that would soon make such state debts notorious. The face is plain and clerical, its authority resting on signatures and a guarantee rather than on ornament.

title: Dutch East India Company (VOC) Middelburg Chamber Obligation Receipts
description: Two related documents of 1622 and 1623 from the Middelburg Chamber in Zeeland of the Vereenigde Oost-Indische Compagnie, photographed together. The lower sheet is a handwritten obligation in which the accounting masters of the Chamber, acting through its receiver Dominicus van Hoontshoerle, acknowledge a loan of £1333 6s 8d Flemish, about 8,000 guilders, bearing interest at 6.25 percent a year and repayable to the bearer forty-four months after its date. It is drawn and signed at Amsterdam, 26 October 1622, the pre-printed place "Middelburgh" struck out and "Amsterdam" substituted, though the issuing body remains the Middelburg Chamber. The upper sheet is the matching printed payment order of the receivers of the East India Company, completed by a manuscript receipt acknowledging full satisfaction of capital and accrued interest, signed by Van Hoontshoerle at Amsterdam, 9 November 1623.

title: Monte di Pietà of Florence assignment of luoghi, Florence
description: A printed assignment of luoghi issued by the Officials, Protectors and Administrators of the Monte di Pietà of Florence, dated at Florence on 11 January 1627, conveying to a named holder, here a Marchese, a stake in the Monte's non-redeemable funded capital. Manuscript entries record four and a half luoghi, each valued at 100 scudi fiorentini reckoned at seven lire to the scudo, yielding five scudi a year, a five percent return paid in half-yearly portions. The text grounds the issue in the provision of 23 April 1616 by which the Grand Duke of Tuscany authorised the perpetual capital. A wax seal and secretarial and ducal signatures attest its authority.
creator: Monte di Pietà della Città di Firenze
notes: Bond certificate assigning luoghi of the Florentine Monte di Pietà. Interest 5 scudi per luogo per year. Established under Grand Ducal senate ordinance of 1616. A second, lower-resolution scan of this same document was catalogued as goetzmann1031 and removed as a duplicate on 2026-07-21.

# Assignment of Luoghi of the Monte di Pietà of Florence — Transcription

## Original (Italian):

*(top left margin, manuscript):* 1627 11 Genn.o

*(printed body, with manuscript insertions marked)*

**NOI Officiali del Monte di Pietà della Città di Firenze, Protettori, & Amministratori del Monte non vacabile** eretto d'ordine del S. G. D. di Toscana nostro Sig. per la Prouisione publicata nell'Amplissimo Senato de' 48. il dì 23. di Aprile 1616. cediamo, & assegniamo à [manuscript: Ill.mo Sig. Marchese fu B.o [illegible surname]] Luoghi [manuscript: quattro e mezzo] di detto Monte di valuta di scudi cento per ogni luogo di lire sette per scudo moneta Fiorentina con i frutti à ragione di scudi cinque l'anno simili per ogni luogo da hoggi in auuenire. Il prezzo de' quali luoghi di detto Monte ci è stato pagato di contanti in mano al nostro Camarlingo generale in scudi [manuscript: quattrocento cinquanta] come à Entrata D a [manuscript: 309]. E noi l'habbiamo fatto descriuere creditore, e padrone de sudetti luoghi al libro di detto Monte eretto per detta Prouisione segnato D de' Liberti à pagarli i frutti di sei mesi in sei mesi la rata portione, e con i priuilegi, condizioni, e dichiarazioni di che in detta Prouisione, e non altrimenti, nè in altro modo. Et in virtù della presente ordiniamo al Camarlingo generale del nostro Monte, che per i tempi sarà, che paghi detti frutti di sei mesi in sei mesi, & in fede habbiamo fatta fare la presente, quale sarà sottoscritta da vno de' nostri Officiali, e dal nostro Prouedittore, e Cancelliere, e sigillata con il solito sigillo di detto Monte.

**Data in Firenze nell'Offizio di detto Monte di Pietà il** [manuscript: 11 di Genn.o 1627]

*(lower right, manuscript signatures):* [illegible] officiale / Michele [illegible surname] (Cancelliere)

*(layout notes: engraved allegorical male figures at upper left and upper right flanking the crowned Medici arms at center top; red wax seal impression at lower left; the third digit of the year is an old open-form "2" (giving 1627), which can be misread as a "4".)*

---

## English Translation:

*(top left margin):* 1627, 11 January

We, Officials of the Monte di Pietà of the City of Florence, Protectors and Administrators of the non-redeemable Monte erected by order of His Serene Grand Duke of Tuscany our Lord, by the Provision published in the Most Ample Senate of the 48 on the 23rd day of April 1616, cede and assign to [the Most Illustrious Lord Marquis, the late B[.] [illegible surname]] [four and a half] Luoghi of the said Monte, of the value of one hundred scudi for each luogo, at seven lire to the scudo in Florentine money, with interest at the rate of five like scudi per year for each luogo from today onward. The price of which luoghi of the said Monte has been paid to us in cash into the hands of our Treasurer-General in [four hundred and fifty] scudi, as per Entry D at [folio 309]. And we have had him entered as creditor and proprietor of the said luoghi in the ledger of the said Monte erected for the said Provision, marked D of the Liberti, the interest to be paid every six months in its due portion, and with the privileges, conditions, and declarations set forth in the said Provision, and not otherwise nor in any other manner. And by virtue of the present [instrument] we order the Treasurer-General of our Monte, whoever shall hold office from time to time, to pay the said interest every six months; and in witness whereof we have caused the present to be drawn up, to be subscribed by one of our Officials and by our Provveditore and Chancellor, and sealed with the customary seal of the said Monte.

Given in Florence in the Office of the said Monte di Pietà, the [11th of January 1627].

*(signatures):* [illegible] Official / Michele [illegible surname], Chancellor
